November 12, 2026

National Stock Exchange of India Limited 
Mumbai 400 051

500247, 974396, 974682, 
974924, 975387

KMB30 
India International Exchange (IFSC) Limited 
Gandhinagar – 382050 
India INX Scrip Code:  500082 
NSE IFSC Limited 
Gandhinagar – 382050 
NSE IX Symbol:  KMBL 5.478 
 
Dear Sirs, 
 
Sub: 
Intimation under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with sub-para 20 of Para A of Part A of Schedule 
III thereto 
 
With reference to the captioned subject, we wish to inform you that the Bank had, on April 9, 2025, received an 
order dated April 9, 2025, passed by the Hon’ble Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Egmore,  
Chennai – 600 008, imposing a fine of Rs. 20,00,000 on the Bank under Sections 409 and 477(A) of the 
Indian Penal Code, 1860 (now known as Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023) and under Section 248(2) of the  
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1974 (now known as Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023). The matter 
arose from a complaint filed by Mr. R. Selvaraj, a customer of the Bank, in relation to the alleged excess 
collection of amounts towards loan repayment, delay in refund thereof following foreclosure of the loan 
account in 2007 and certain related matters concerning the furnishing of the Statement of Account and the 
Termination of Account Statement. 
 
The Bank has preferred an appeal against the aforesaid order and the matter. The Bank believes that it has 
adequate grounds to support its position in the matter. The impact of the aforesaid order is limited to the 
amount of fine levied on the Bank under the aforesaid order. 
 
We would also wish to clarify that the disclosure of the aforesaid order under Regulation 30 of the SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 was not filed earlier by the Bank, as the 
matter has been under dispute and sub-judice. However, in view of a communication received from a 
regulatory authority (National Stock Exchange of India Limited), the same is now being disclosed. 
 
We request you to take the above on record and disseminate the same on your website.  
 
Thanking you, 
 
Yours faithfully, 
For Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited  
 
 
Avan Doomasia 
President & Company Secretary 
AVAN 
KAYOMARS 
DOOMASIA
Digitally signed by 
AVAN KAYOMARS 
DOOMASIA

PRESS RELEASE 
Six Promising Researchers Win the Infosys Prize 2026 Awarded by the Infosys 
Science Foundation 
Laureates include researchers working at the frontiers of quantum technology, wireless 
networks, constitutional law, human health, macro-economics, and mathematics 
Bengaluru, India – November 12, 2026: Six rising stars of research were announced as winners of 
the Infosys Prize 2026 by the Infosys Science Foundation (ISF) today. The Prize is awarded in six 
categories - Economics, Engineering and Computer Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, Life 
Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, and Physical Sciences. Since it was established in 2009, the Infosys 
Prize has honored the remarkable accomplishments of individuals whose research and scholarship 
significantly advances knowledge and contributes to the progress of India and the world. The prize for 
each category comprises a gold medal, a citation, and a prize purse of USD 100,000 (or its equivalent 
in INR). 
 
The laureates of Infosys Prize 2026 were selected by an international panel of jurors comprising 
renowned scholars and experts. From 2024, the prize has shifted focus to honor researchers under the 
age of 40, emphasizing the need for early recognition of exceptional talent. This encouragement of early 
career researchers will serve as an inspiration for the next generation of scholars and future innovators. 
 
The winners of the Infosys Prize 2026 were announced by the trustees of ISF - Mr. Srinath Batni 
(President, Board of Trustees), Mr. K. Dinesh, Mr. Kris Gopalakrishnan, Dr. Pratima Murthy, and Mr. S. 
D. Shibulal. Mr. Narayana Murthy addressed the audience in a recorded message. The other trustees 
of ISF - Mr. Mohandas Pai, Mr. Nandan Nilekani, and Mr. Salil Parekh - also extended their 
congratulations to this year’s recipients. 
 
The Infosys Prize remains the largest award in India that acknowledges excellence in science and 
research. Laureates of the Infosys Prize have gone on to receive several prestigious international 
awards, including the Nobel Prize (Abhijit Banerjee and Esther Duflo), the Fields Medal (Manjul 
Bhargava and Akshay Venkatesh), the Dan David Prize (Sanjay Subrahmanyam), the MacArthur 
‘genius’ Grant and British Academy Book Prize (Sunil Amrith), the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental 
Physics and Oskar Kline Medal (Ashoke Sen), the Marconi Prize (Hari Balakrishnan), the Leverhulme 
Prize (Mahmood Kooria), and the Ramanujan Prize (Mahesh Kakde). Several laureates have also been 
elected fellows of the Royal Society, among them Gagandeep Kang, who became the first Indian 
woman to be elected Fellow of the Royal Society. 
 
Srinath Batni, President, Infosys Science Foundation, said, “I extend my warmest congratulations 
to the winners of the Infosys Prize 2026. Their work demonstrates how rigorous research and the pursuit 
of new knowledge can deepen our understanding of the world and help address some of humanity’s 
most complex challenges. Recognizing exceptional researchers early in their careers is particularly 

 
important, as it gives them the encouragement and opportunity to pursue bold questions, challenge 
established thinking and make lasting contributions to their fields. At the Infosys Science Foundation, 
we believe that nurturing scientific talent and fostering a strong research culture are essential to 
advancing knowledge and shaping a better future for humanity. I hope this recognition inspires more 
young minds to embrace research and push the boundaries of discovery.” 
 
Meet the winners of the Infosys Prize 2026 whose pioneering research is helping shape a better future: 
 
Economics 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Economics is awarded to Karthik Sastry, Associate Professor of Economics 
and Public Affairs at Princeton University, for his pioneering contributions to the field of climate change, 
and technological innovation, and to the study of business cycle fluctuations. His work provides deep 
insights into how societies adapt to climate change through technological innovations and is likely to 
have far-reaching policy implications. 
 
Engineering and Computer Science 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Engineering and Computer Science is awarded to Swarun Kumar, Assistant 
Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University. Prof. Kumar’s 
pioneering work extends low-power wireless networks beyond information delivery to perception and 
action in the physical world. He combines insights on the physics of wireless technology with novel 
architectures and algorithms to obtain innovative designs in connectivity, sensing, control, and 
actuation. 
 
Humanities and Social Sciences 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Humanities and Social Sciences is awarded to Gautam Bhatia, Adjunct 
Professor at Jindal Global Law School and Green Fellow at the University of New South Wales in 
Sydney. Prof. Bhatia is an outstanding young legal scholar, prodigiously productive, tremendously wide 
in his range of knowledge and interests, with a real gift for marshalling arguments rigorously towards 
conclusions that seek to make the law an instrument for constructing a fair, equal, and humane society. 
His five books and many academic articles amount to a formidable corpus of important work. His 
mastery of the scholarly literature goes beyond the law in to neighboring disciplines that have an impact 
on the law, such as macro-economics, sociology, political theory, and moral philosophy. 
 
Life Sciences 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Life Sciences is awarded to Isha Jain, Associate Investigator at the 
Gladstone Institutes and Assistant Professor at the Department of Biochemistry at the University of 
California, San Francisco. Prof. Jain has been awarded for her pioneering discoveries in oxygen 
biology, which showed that tissue damage in some mitochondrial diseases arises from excess oxygen 
rather than energy failure, and for turning fundamental biochemical insights into new therapeutic 

 
strategies, including designing a small-molecule to reduce oxygen levels and vitamin-based treatments 
for inherited metabolic disorders. 
 
Mathematical Sciences 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Mathematical Sciences is awarded to Riddhipratim Basu, Associate 
Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences of the Tata Institute of Fundamental 
Research (ICTS-TIFR) in Bangalore. Prof. Basu is being awarded for his outstanding contributions to 
probability theory and statistical physics. His work resolved the longstanding slow-bond problem and 
established new large deviations asymptotics. He has settled conjectures on fluctuations for percolation 
models including those that are not exactly solvable. He also developed explicit combinatorial 
descriptions of Wilson loop expectations in two-dimensional lattice Yang–Mills theory in an asymptotic 
strong-coupling regime. 
 
Physical Sciences 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Physical Sciences is awarded to Manoj Kumar Joshi, an experimental 
physicist and Assistant Professor at Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD). Prof. 
Joshi’s pioneering work with trapped ions, creating programmable quantum machines that reveal how 
complex quantum systems behave, and turning the promise of quantum simulation into experimental 
reality. Quantum computers and simulators promise to unlock discoveries beyond the reach of classical 
computers, transforming our understanding of matter and opening new possibilities in materials science 
and chemistry. 
 
About Infosys Science Foundation 
The Infosys Prize is awarded by the Infosys Science Foundation, a not-for-profit trust set up in 2009. 
The award is given annually to honor outstanding achievements of contemporary researchers and 
scientists in six categories: Economics, Engineering and Computer Science, Humanities and Social 
Sciences, Life Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, and Physical Sciences. Each prize consists of a gold 
medal, a citation and a purse of USD 100,000. The award intends to celebrate success in research and 
stand as a marker of excellence in these fields. 
 
Jury Chairs 
Prof. Kaushik Basu | Prof. Jayathi Murthy | Prof. Akeel Bilgrami | Prof. Mriganka Sur | Prof. 
Chandrashekhar Khare | Prof. Shrinivas Kulkarni 
 
Trustees 
K. Dinesh | Srinath Batni | S. Gopalakrishnan | Narayana Murthy | Pratima Murthy | Nandan Nilekani | 
T. V. Mohandas Pai | Salil Parekh | Shibulal S.D. 
 
About Infosys 

 
Infosys (NSE, BSE, NYSE: INFY) is a global leader 
in AI first business consulting and technology 
services.  Over 325,000 of our people work to amplify 
human potential and create the next opportunity for 
people, businesses, and communities. As navigators 
of enterprise transformation, we enable businesses 
in 59 countries to unlock AI value at scale. With over 
four decades of experience in managing the systems 
and workings of global enterprises, we accelerate 
business transformation through our AI-first value 
framework, deep domain expertise, and our unique 
ability to orchestrate innovations from our AI-native 
partner ecosystem. Infosys is recognized as the 
fastest growing IT services brand globally, committed 
to 
being 
a 
well-governed, 
environmentally 
sustainable partner for our clients where deep talent 
expertise, in an inclusive workplace, help them 
navigate their next.

Certain statements in this release, including those concerning our future events, future growth 
prospects, our future financial or operating performance and our offerings and collaborations are 
“forward looking statements” intended to qualify for the 'safe harbor' under the Private Securities 
Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Such forward-looking statements are based on our current expectations, 
assumptions, estimates and projections about the Company, our industry, economic conditions in the 
markets in which we operate, and certain other matters. These forward-looking statements are subject 
to substantial known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors, that could cause actual results 
or outcomes to differ materially from those implied by such forward-looking statements. Important 
factors that may cause actual results or outcomes to differ from those implied by the forward-looking 
statements include, but are not limited to, risks and uncertainties regarding the execution of our 
business strategy, increased competition for talent, our ability to attract and retain personnel, increase 
in wages, investments to reskill our employees, our ability to effectively implement a hybrid work model, 
economic uncertainties and geo-political situations, technological disruptions and innovations such as 
artificial intelligence, the complex and evolving regulatory landscape including immigration regulation 
changes, particularly in the United States, our Environmental, Social, Governance (“ESG”) vision, our 
capital allocation policy and expectations concerning our market position, future operations, margins, 
profitability, liquidity and capital resources, our corporate actions including acquisitions, cybersecurity 
matters, the outcome of pending litigation and the US government investigation, and the effect of current 
and future tariffs. These and additional factors that may cause actual results or outcomes to differ from 
those implied by the forward-looking statements are discussed in more detail in our US Securities and 
Exchange Commission filings including our Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended March 
31, 2026. These filings are available at www.sec.gov. In light of these and other uncertainties, you 
should not conclude that the results or outcomes referred to in any of the forward-looking statements 
will be achieved. Infosys may, from time to time, make additional written and oral forward-looking 
statements, including statements contained in the Company's filings with the Securities and Exchange 
Commission and our reports to shareholders. The Company does not undertake to update any forward-
looking statements that may be made from time to time by or on behalf of the Company unless it is 
required by law.

PRESS RELEASE 
Six Promising Researchers Win the Infosys Prize 2026 Awarded by the Infosys 
Science Foundation 
Laureates include researchers working at the frontiers of quantum technology, wireless 
networks, constitutional law, human health, macro-economics, and mathematics 
Bengaluru, India – November 12, 2026: Six rising stars of research were announced as winners of 
the Infosys Prize 2026 by the Infosys Science Foundation (ISF) today. The Prize is awarded in six 
categories - Economics, Engineering and Computer Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, Life 
Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, and Physical Sciences. Since it was established in 2009, the Infosys 
Prize has honored the remarkable accomplishments of individuals whose research and scholarship 
significantly advances knowledge and contributes to the progress of India and the world. The prize for 
each category comprises a gold medal, a citation, and a prize purse of USD 100,000 (or its equivalent 
in INR). 
 
The laureates of Infosys Prize 2026 were selected by an international panel of jurors comprising 
renowned scholars and experts. From 2024, the prize has shifted focus to honor researchers under the 
age of 40, emphasizing the need for early recognition of exceptional talent. This encouragement of early 
career researchers will serve as an inspiration for the next generation of scholars and future innovators. 
 
The winners of the Infosys Prize 2026 were announced by the trustees of ISF - Mr. Srinath Batni 
(President, Board of Trustees), Mr. K. Dinesh, Mr. Kris Gopalakrishnan, Dr. Pratima Murthy, and Mr. S. 
D. Shibulal. Mr. Narayana Murthy addressed the audience in a recorded message. The other trustees 
of ISF - Mr. Mohandas Pai, Mr. Nandan Nilekani, and Mr. Salil Parekh - also extended their 
congratulations to this year’s recipients. 
 
The Infosys Prize remains the largest award in India that acknowledges excellence in science and 
research. Laureates of the Infosys Prize have gone on to receive several prestigious international 
awards, including the Nobel Prize (Abhijit Banerjee and Esther Duflo), the Fields Medal (Manjul 
Bhargava and Akshay Venkatesh), the Dan David Prize (Sanjay Subrahmanyam), the MacArthur 
‘genius’ Grant and British Academy Book Prize (Sunil Amrith), the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental 
Physics and Oskar Kline Medal (Ashoke Sen), the Marconi Prize (Hari Balakrishnan), the Leverhulme 
Prize (Mahmood Kooria), and the Ramanujan Prize (Mahesh Kakde). Several laureates have also been 
elected fellows of the Royal Society, among them Gagandeep Kang, who became the first Indian 
woman to be elected Fellow of the Royal Society. 
 
Srinath Batni, President, Infosys Science Foundation, said, “I extend my warmest congratulations 
to the winners of the Infosys Prize 2026. Their work demonstrates how rigorous research and the pursuit 
of new knowledge can deepen our understanding of the world and help address some of humanity’s 
most complex challenges. Recognizing exceptional researchers early in their careers is particularly 

 
important, as it gives them the encouragement and opportunity to pursue bold questions, challenge 
established thinking and make lasting contributions to their fields. At the Infosys Science Foundation, 
we believe that nurturing scientific talent and fostering a strong research culture are essential to 
advancing knowledge and shaping a better future for humanity. I hope this recognition inspires more 
young minds to embrace research and push the boundaries of discovery.” 
 
Meet the winners of the Infosys Prize 2026 whose pioneering research is helping shape a better future: 
 
Economics 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Economics is awarded to Karthik Sastry, Associate Professor of Economics 
and Public Affairs at Princeton University, for his pioneering contributions to the field of climate change, 
and technological innovation, and to the study of business cycle fluctuations. His work provides deep 
insights into how societies adapt to climate change through technological innovations and is likely to 
have far-reaching policy implications. 
 
Engineering and Computer Science 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Engineering and Computer Science is awarded to Swarun Kumar, Assistant 
Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University. Prof. Kumar’s 
pioneering work extends low-power wireless networks beyond information delivery to perception and 
action in the physical world. He combines insights on the physics of wireless technology with novel 
architectures and algorithms to obtain innovative designs in connectivity, sensing, control, and 
actuation. 
 
Humanities and Social Sciences 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Humanities and Social Sciences is awarded to Gautam Bhatia, Adjunct 
Professor at Jindal Global Law School and Green Fellow at the University of New South Wales in 
Sydney. Prof. Bhatia is an outstanding young legal scholar, prodigiously productive, tremendously wide 
in his range of knowledge and interests, with a real gift for marshalling arguments rigorously towards 
conclusions that seek to make the law an instrument for constructing a fair, equal, and humane society. 
His five books and many academic articles amount to a formidable corpus of important work. His 
mastery of the scholarly literature goes beyond the law in to neighboring disciplines that have an impact 
on the law, such as macro-economics, sociology, political theory, and moral philosophy. 
 
Life Sciences 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Life Sciences is awarded to Isha Jain, Associate Investigator at the 
Gladstone Institutes and Assistant Professor at the Department of Biochemistry at the University of 
California, San Francisco. Prof. Jain has been awarded for her pioneering discoveries in oxygen 
biology, which showed that tissue damage in some mitochondrial diseases arises from excess oxygen 
rather than energy failure, and for turning fundamental biochemical insights into new therapeutic 

 
strategies, including designing a small-molecule to reduce oxygen levels and vitamin-based treatments 
for inherited metabolic disorders. 
 
Mathematical Sciences 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Mathematical Sciences is awarded to Riddhipratim Basu, Associate 
Professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences of the Tata Institute of Fundamental 
Research (ICTS-TIFR) in Bangalore. Prof. Basu is being awarded for his outstanding contributions to 
probability theory and statistical physics. His work resolved the longstanding slow-bond problem and 
established new large deviations asymptotics. He has settled conjectures on fluctuations for percolation 
models including those that are not exactly solvable. He also developed explicit combinatorial 
descriptions of Wilson loop expectations in two-dimensional lattice Yang–Mills theory in an asymptotic 
strong-coupling regime. 
 
Physical Sciences 
The Infosys Prize 2026 in Physical Sciences is awarded to Manoj Kumar Joshi, an experimental 
physicist and Assistant Professor at Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD). Prof. 
Joshi’s pioneering work with trapped ions, creating programmable quantum machines that reveal how 
complex quantum systems behave, and turning the promise of quantum simulation into experimental 
reality. Quantum computers and simulators promise to unlock discoveries beyond the reach of classical 
computers, transforming our understanding of matter and opening new possibilities in materials science 
and chemistry. 
 
About Infosys Science Foundation 
The Infosys Prize is awarded by the Infosys Science Foundation, a not-for-profit trust set up in 2009. 
The award is given annually to honor outstanding achievements of contemporary researchers and 
scientists in six categories: Economics, Engineering and Computer Science, Humanities and Social 
Sciences, Life Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, and Physical Sciences. Each prize consists of a gold 
medal, a citation and a purse of USD 100,000. The award intends to celebrate success in research and 
stand as a marker of excellence in these fields.

Chandrashekhar Khare | Prof. Shrinivas Kulkarni

Adani’s Kutch Copper and Chile’s Codelco Sign Strategic MoU 
for exploration of Kaburkaala project in Chile 
Editor’s Synopsis 
 Kutch Copper Ltd and Corporación Nacional del Cobre de Chile have signed a MoU 
for exploration of Kaburkaala project in Chile. 
 The MoU sets out terms for potential exploration partnership at the Kaburkaala 
copper project in Chile’s Calama copper belt.  
 
The partnership links Chilean copper resources with Adani’s integrated copper 
smelter complex at Mundra, India. 
Ahmedabad/Santiago, November 12, 2026: Kutch Copper Ltd (KCL), a unit of Adani Enterprises 
Ltd, and Corporación Nacional del Cobre de Chile (Codelco) today said they have signed a 
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for setting key terms of cooperation for forming a 
strategic exploration partnership at the Kaburkaala project in Calama copper belt of the 
Antofagasta Region in northern Chile, one of the most prolific copper districts in the world.  
The MoU was signed recently in presence of Shri. Jeet Adani, Director KCL, Dr. Vinay Prakash, 
CEO Adani Natural Resources and Mr Bernando Fontaine, Chairman Codelco, at LME Week 2026 
in London.  
“Critical resources, led by copper, are at the very heart of our future transformation. More than 
just a mining asset, we view this strategic partnership as a long-term investment in India's 
future. By securing robust access to global copper resources, we are building supply chain 
resilience for the critical industries driving our nation's growth—spanning renewable energy, 
advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, and technology. This partnership is a testament to our 
commitment to enhancing India’s resource security and supporting its journey to becoming a 
global economic powerhouse,” said Jeet Adani, Director, KCL.  
“This MoU represents an important step in the work we have carried out with Adani over the 
past year. This process demonstrates Codelco’s ability to attract world-class partners and create 
value from its exploration portfolio, while safeguarding the long-term interests of the company 
and the State of Chile,” said Bernardo Fontaine, Chairman of the Board, Codelco. 

 
Page 2 
For Adani, the proposed partnership, is a strategic step in building an integrated globally 
diversified copper value chain, linking upstream resources in Chile with its copper smelter 
complex at Mundra, India and securing long term access to a mineral that is key to 
electrification and global energy transition.  
For Codelco, this initiative is part of its strategy to create value from its exploration portfolio 
through public private partnerships, sharing risks and accelerating the advancement of copper 
projects with development potential.  
The collaboration also strengthens India-Chile cooperation in critical minerals at a time when 
resource security has become a strategic priority for both nations.  
The proposed partnership would enable exploration of the Kaburkaala project to advance 
through Adani’s contribution of capital, technology-led exploration and large-scale project 
execution capability, combined with Codelco’s deep geological knowledge and international 
experience, with both companies focused on responsible exploration, high standards of safety 
and environmental stewardship, and long-term value creation. 
 
About Adani Enterprises Limited and Kutch Copper Limited 
Adani Enterprises Limited (AEL) is the flagship company of the Adani Group, one of India’s largest 
business organisations, and has incubated and scaled businesses across ports, energy, utilities, logistics 
and primary industries. Kutch Copper Limited, a subsidiary of AEL, is developing one of the world’s largest 
single-location custom copper smelter complexes at Mundra, Gujarat, designed around state-of-the-art 
technology, digitalisation and high ESG standards to support India’s self-reliance in critical metals. For 
more information, visit www.adanienterprises.com. 
For media queries please contact: roy.paul@adani.com 
 
About Codelco 
Corporación Nacional del Cobre de Chile (Codelco) is a state-owned company of the Republic of Chile and 
one of the world’s largest copper producers. Headquartered in Santiago, Codelco operates a portfolio of 
large-scale mining divisions across Chile and plays a pivotal role in global copper supply. Codelco is 
committed to responsible and sustainable mining, innovation and value creation for Chile, and actively 
pursues partnerships to advance its exploration portfolio. For more information, visit www.codelco.com.

GAIL (India) Limited 
 
Press Release 
 
Awareness session for 300 TPD Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) based  
Compressed Biogas (CBG) Plant in Bengaluru organised 
 
Bengaluru, November 11, 2026: An awareness session on GAIL's 300 TPD Municipal Solid 
Waste (MSW) based Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) plant proposed to be set up at Karnataka 
Compost Development Corporation (KCDC) premises was organised here today for various 
stakeholders.  
 
The event was graced by Shri Tejaswi Surya, Hon'ble Member of Parliament, Bengaluru South 
and Shri Satish Reddy., Hon'ble Member of Legislative Assembly, Karnataka. Shri S. Mowar, 
Executive Director (Southern Region), GAIL, senior officials of GAIL, representatives of 
Resident Welfare Association, NGOs and media were present.  
 
The CBG plant is proposed to be set up with an investment of Rs. 123.42 crore and spread 
across approximately 18 acres and will process 300 tonnes of segregated organic municipal 
waste daily to produce approximately 12.6 tonnes of CBG and 21.6 tonnes of Fermented 
Organic Manure (FOM) every day. The CBG (Compressed Bio-Gas) produced from the facility 
will be supplied to GAIL Gas, a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL, contributing to the 
availability of indigenous clean fuel in the state. 
 
The proposed plant is expected to deliver substantial socio-economic and environmental 
benefits in the state of Karnataka. It will provide a sustainable solution for processing urban 
organic waste, reduce dependence on landfill disposal, promote cleaner cities and strengthen 
the state's waste-management infrastructure. With modern odour-control and effluent-treatment 
systems, the proposed facility will ensure environmentally responsible waste processing while 
addressing concerns associated with unmanaged organic waste. Further, the plant will convert 
municipal waste into commercially valuable clean energy and organic manure while 
contributing to the vision of circular economy. 
 
This initiative reinforces GAIL's commitment to support Karnataka's sustainable development 
priorities while contributing to the national objectives of Swachh Bharat Mission, Atmanirbhar 
Bharat and India's clean energy transition. The project is also envisaged as a replicable model 
for developing municipal waste-to-CBG infrastructure in other urban centres across the country.

Kalyani Strategic Systems Unveils 120mm R.A.M.S, the Rapid Attack Mortar System 
- Another Step Toward Making Bharat Safe - 
 
Vehicle-integrated 120mm mortar designed to deliver rapid, protected fire support at high altitude and 
in all weather, for the Indian Armed Forces and International Customers 
 
India | November 12, 2026: Kalyani Strategic Systems Limited (KSSL), the wholly-owned defence 
subsidiary of Bharat Forge Limited, today unveiled the 120mm R.A.M.S - the Rapid Attack Mortar System. 
Integrated on an agile 4x4 vehicle, R.A.M.S is designed to give mobile forces powerful, rapid-response 
mortar fire that keeps pace with future warfare strategies. It marks another step in KSSL's commitment 
to a Bharat that is secure, self-reliant and prepared to meet any threat to its sovereignty, and to partner 
nations that must protect their people against hostile threats. 
 
Fires from the vehicle. With the mortar integrated on the platform, crews can transition from march-to-
fire mission in moments, and relocate before the adversary can respond. By removing the need to 
dismount and emplace the mortar, the system is designed to reduce crew exposure, compress the sensor-
to-shooter cycle and keep the detachment protected throughout the engagement - faster response, 
greater mobility and improved crew safety. 
 
Built for the hardest terrain. R.A.M.S is engineered to retain its mobility at high altitude and its readiness 
through extreme cold, heat and monsoon. From mountain passes to desert and plains, it is designed to 
bring 120mm firepower to terrain where towed systems are slow to deploy and demanding to sustain. 
 
Designed for future warfare. R.A.M.S is shaped by the realities of future conflict: persistent surveillance, 
compressed targeting cycles and a premium on survivability. Speed, mobility and shoot-and-scoot agility 
define the system, which is designed to give commanders a decisive edge in contested environments and 
a platform with the headroom to evolve with the threat. 
 
Made in India, for the world. Designed and developed in India for the Indian Armed Forces and 
International Customers, R.A.M.S is set to advance Aatmanirbhar Bharat and reinforce India's growing 
standing as a trusted indigenous design-manufacturer and exporter of advanced defence platforms. 
 
 
Mr. Amit Kalyani, Vice Chairman and Joint Managing Director, Bharat Forge Ltd, the parent company of 
KSSL, said, "Deepawali celebrates the triumph of light and the protection of all we hold dear. Our purpose 
at KSSL is to keep Bharat safe, and to stand with nations facing hostile aggression. R.A.M.S is designed to 
give our armed forces credible, responsive capability at high altitude and in the most challenging 
conditions, while keeping our soldiers protected. We design for the challenges ahead - we design and build 
in India, for India and for our partners around the world. This is Aatmanirbhar Bharat in action, and 
another step towards a Sushakt Bharat, Surakshit Bharat." 
 
As India celebrates the festival of lights, R.A.M.S reflects KSSL's conviction that national security begins 
with technology built for national security and protection, and its commitment to a Bharat and partner 
nations that stay safe, strong and prepared. 
*** 
About Kalyani Strategic Systems Limited 
Kalyani Strategic Systems Limited (KSSL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Bharat Forge Limited, drives the 
defence business of the Kalyani Group, one of the world's foremost engineering and metallurgical 

 
enterprises. With more than six decades of expertise in design, engineering, metallurgy and advanced 
manufacturing, KSSL delivers sovereign defence capability across the land, marine and unmanned domains 
- spanning artillery systems, armoured and protected vehicles, small arms, ammunition, and marine and 
unmanned platforms. Beyond supplying battle-ready systems, KSSL enables partner nations to build their 
own defence industrial base through technology partnership, local industrialisation and assured through-
life support, backed by proven production at scale and security of supply. Trusted by both Indian and global 
armed forces and governments seeking resilient, self-reliant capability, KSSL is a trusted global defence 
partner of choice. 
 
About Bharat Forge 
Bharat Forge Limited (BFL), a Pune-based multinational company, is a technology-driven global leader in 
providing innovative, high-performance and safety-critical components and solutions across automotive, 
aerospace, defence, rail, marine, energy and industrial sectors. With a global manufacturing footprint and 
world-class engineering capabilities, BFL is at the forefront of supporting India's strategic industrial and 
defence ambitions. 
 
Media Contact 
Dimple Raisurana Kapur  |  Group Chief Communications Officer, Kalyani Group 
Email: Dimple.RaisuranaKapur@kalyani.in |  Mobile: +91 98205 25305

Press Release
Lupin Announces European Launch of Biosimilar Ranibizumab  
 
Mumbai, India, November 12, 2026: Global pharma major Lupin Limited (Lupin) today announced that 
its commercial partner, Sandoz has launched RanluspecTM, Lupin’s biosimilar Ranibizumab, across 
Europe, excluding Germany. 
 
The launch follows the European Commission approval of RanluspecTM in vial and pre-filled syringe 
presentations and marks an important step in expanding access to high-quality biologic treatment 
options for retinal diseases. 
 
Ranibizumab is a recombinant humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody fragment that binds and 
inhibits vascular endothelial growth factor A. The indications of RanluspecTM encompass the 
treatment of patients with neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration, macular edema 
following retinal vein occlusion, diabetic macular edema, proliferative diabetic retinopathy, and 
choroidal neovascularization. 
 
Thierry Volle, President EMEA and Emerging Markets, Lupin, said, “The launch of Ranluspec in 
Europe advances Lupin’s strategy of bringing high-quality biosimilars to more patients suffering from 
retinal and choroidal vascular diseases. Together with Sandoz, we will expand access to this 
important treatment across the region.” 
 
“The launch of Ranluspec reinforces our growing capabilities in biosimilars as it brings together our 
scientific expertise and manufacturing capabilities in biologics. It underscores our commitment to 
addressing unmet needs while supporting more sustainable healthcare systems,” said Dr. Cyrus 
Karkaria, President – Biotech Business, Lupin. 
 
About Lupin 
Lupin Limited is a global pharmaceutical leader headquartered in Mumbai, India, with products distributed in over 100 
markets. Lupin specializes in pharmaceutical products, including branded and generic formulations, complex generics, 
biotechnology products, and active pharmaceutical ingredients. Trusted by healthcare professionals and consumers 
globally, the company enjoys a strong position in India and the U.S. across multiple therapy areas, including respiratory, 
cardiovascular, anti-diabetic, anti-infective, gastrointestinal, central nervous system, and women's health. Lupin has 15 
state-of-the-art manufacturing sites and 6 research centers globally, along with a dedicated workforce of over 26,000 
professionals. Lupin is committed to improving patient health outcomes through its subsidiaries - Lupin Diagnostics, 
Lupin Digital Health, and Lupin Manufacturing Solutions.  
To know more, visit www.lupin.com or follow us on LinkedIn  https://www.linkedin.com/company/lupin

LTM Brings AI-Powered Quantum Error Mitigation to IBM Quantum Functions Catalog 
Mumbai, India – November 12, 2026: LTM, the Business Creativity partner to the world’s largest enterprises, today announced 
that AI-QEM, its proprietary AI-powered Quantum Error Mitigation capability, is now available in the IBM Quantum Functions 
Catalog. With this milestone, LTM becomes the first Global Systems Integrator (GSI) worldwide to publish a function in the 
catalog. 
 
The IBM Quantum Functions Catalog is an ecosystem of partner-built quantum software services that simplify quantum 
workflows and enable researchers and enterprises to run quantum experiments more efficiently for algorithm development 
and application prototyping. AI-QEM is available as a circuit function, allowing users of eligible IBM Quantum access plans to 
apply LTM's error mitigation capability directly within their Qiskit workflows. 
 
Quantum computers are inherently susceptible to noise and errors that can impact computational outcomes. While 
conventional error mitigation techniques often require additional circuit executions, quantum processing time, or auxiliary 
qubits, AI-QEM uses advanced AI models to learn and correct device-specific error patterns through classical post-processing. 
This supports improved result accuracy without additional QPU time, repeated circuit executions, or extra qubits, helping 
reduce the cost and complexity of running useful quantum experiments. 
 
The capability has been validated on IBM Quantum computers across a range of circuit sizes and complexities, including 
experiments involving more than 100 qubits. 
 
"LTM’s AI-QEM now available in the IBM Quantum Functions Catalog reflects the growing role of our ecosystem partners in 
advancing and expanding the tools available for the wider quantum community. The AI-QEM function will allow our users to 
mitigate errors faster and with fewer resources, in their efforts to develop algorithms and applications," said Scott Crowder, 
Vice President, IBM Quantum Adoption and Business Development. 
 
LTM continues to advance practical quantum applications across industries. Its work includes quantum optimization solutions 
for a leading global insurer, hybrid quantum machine learning for critical infrastructure operations, and quantum-safe security 
programs that help financial services and insurance organizations prepare for the migration to post-quantum cryptography. 
 
 
About LTM 
LTM — a Larsen & Toubro Group Company — is an AI-centric global technology services company and the Business Creativity partner to 
the world’s largest enterprises. We bring human insights and intelligent systems together to help clients create greater value at the 
intersection of technology and domain expertise. Our capabilities span integrated operations, transformation, and business AI — enabling 
new ways of working, new productivity paradigms, and new roads to value. Together with over 87,000 employees across 40 countries and 
our global network of partners, LTM owns outcomes for clients, helping them not just outperform the market, but Outcreate it. Read more 
at LTM.com.  
 
Media Contact: Shambhavi Revandkar | Global Media Relations | shambhavi.revandkar@ltm.com

Press Release 
 
Alkem reports 14% revenue growth in Q2FY27 
Mumbai, November 12, 2026: Alkem Laboratories Ltd. today announced its standalone and 
consolidated financial results for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Board of 
Directors took record of these results at its meeting held in Mumbai today. 
 
Q2FY27 Key Financial Metrics 
 
 
  
Commenting on the results, Mr. Sandeep Singh, MD of Alkem, said, “Our Q2FY27 
performance reflects continued momentum in the India business, supported by focused execution 
across our acute and chronic portfolios. The international business delivered steady progress 
despite continued pricing pressure in the US, with volume growth providing support. During the 
quarter, we also expanded our MedTech presence through the addition of Occlutech, while 
improving execution and operating performance at Enzene remains a key priority. We will 
continue to focus on strengthening our core business, improving productivity and deploying 
capital prudently to build sustainable growth across pharmaceuticals, biotech and MedTech.” 
We are pleased to welcome Dr. Amrut Naik as our Chief Executive Officer and wish him 
success in his new role. 
Q2 FY27 Key Financial Highlights 
• Total Revenue from Operations was ₹45,520 million, with YoY growth of 13.8%. 
o India sales were ₹30,275 million, YoY growth of 9.5%. 
o International sales were ₹14,540 million, with YoY growth of 22.3%. 
• Biotech sales were ₹704 million, with YoY degrowth of 35% 
• MedTech sales were ₹1,331 million (including Occlutech), integrated Occlutech from 
Q2FY27 onwards. 
• EBITDA at ₹10,252 million, resulted in an EBITDA margin of 22.5%, a growth of 
11.3% YoY. 
• R&D expenses for Q2 FY27 were ₹1,953 million, or 4.3% of total revenue from 
operations, vs. ₹1,302 million in Q2 FY26 at 3.3% of total revenue from operations. 
• Profit before tax (before exceptional item) was ₹ 9,646 million, YoY growth of 7.7%. 
• Net Profit (after Non-Controlling interest) was ₹6,753 million, YoY de-growth of 11.7%. 
• Net Cash stood at INR 49,054 mn (as on 30 September 2026) 
 
Q2FY27 Operational Highlights 
 
Domestic Business Key Highlights 
• The contribution of domestic sales to total sales was 68% vs. 70% in Q2 FY26. 
• According to IQVIA (SSA) data, for Q2 FY27: 

o The Company registered a growth of 13.8% YoY a t p a r w i t h Indian 
Pharmaceutical Market (IPM), growth of 13.8%. 
o Acute segment reported growth of 12.1% at par with IPM growth of 12.3%. 
o Chronic segment reported growth of 22.4% vs. IPM which grew by 16%, +640 
bps outperformance.  
o We have outperformed IPM in eight key focused therapies: VMN ~1.2x, Pain 
~1.5x, Anti-Diabetic ~1.5x, Cardiac by 1.1x, Urology by 1.1x, Respiratory 
~1.6x, Neuro/CNS by 1.1x and Derma ~1.6x. 
 
International Business Key Highlights 
• US sales were ₹7,830 million, YoY growth of 2.4%. 
• US business sales contributed 17% to total sales in Q2 FY27 vs. 19% in Q2 FY26. 
• Non-US sales were ₹6,710 million, YoY growth of 58%. Excluding Occlutech, Non-US 
sales grew 28.6% YoY. 
• Non-US business sales contributed 15% to total sales in Q2 FY27 v.s. 11% in Q2 FY26.

About Alkem: Alkem Laboratories Ltd. is the sixth - largest pharmaceutical company in the 
Indian market, with a legacy spanning over 50+ years of providing high-quality medicines to 
patients. It holds a dominant position in the therapy areas of anti-infectives, gastrointestinal 
disorders, pain management, and supplements. It also has a growing portfolio of products in 
chronic therapies, including diabetes, neurology, dermatology, and urology. It has 20+ state-of-
the-art manufacturing facilities and cutting-edge research and development (R&D) centres to 
develop and manufacture generic formulations, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and 
biosimilars. Apart from India, the company has a meaningful presence in the US, Latin America, 
Australia, Europe and several other Asian countries. “Inspiring Healthier Lives” is at the core of the 
organization’s values and culture, reinforcing its steadfast commitment to improving global health. 
For more information, please visit www.alkemlabs.com and follow us on LinkedIn, Instagram, 
and Facebook.

Press Release 
 
Alkem reports 14% revenue growth in Q2FY27 
Mumbai, November 12, 2026: Alkem Laboratories Ltd. today announced its standalone and 
consolidated financial results for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Board of 
Directors took record of these results at its meeting held in Mumbai today. 
 
Q2FY27 Key Financial Metrics 
 
 
  
Commenting on the results, Mr. Sandeep Singh, MD of Alkem, said, “Our Q2FY27 
performance reflects continued momentum in the India business, supported by focused execution 
across our acute and chronic portfolios. The international business delivered steady progress 
despite continued pricing pressure in the US, with volume growth providing support. During the 
quarter, we also expanded our MedTech presence through the addition of Occlutech, while 
improving execution and operating performance at Enzene remains a key priority. We will 
continue to focus on strengthening our core business, improving productivity and deploying 
capital prudently to build sustainable growth across pharmaceuticals, biotech and MedTech.” 
We are pleased to welcome Dr. Amrut Naik as our Chief Executive Officer and wish him 
success in his new role. 
Q2 FY27 Key Financial Highlights 
• Total Revenue from Operations was ₹45,520 million, with YoY growth of 13.8%. 
o India sales were ₹30,275 million, YoY growth of 9.5%. 
o International sales were ₹14,540 million, with YoY growth of 22.3%. 
• Biotech sales were ₹704 million, with YoY degrowth of 35% 
• MedTech sales were ₹1,331 million (including Occlutech), integrated Occlutech from 
Q2FY27 onwards. 
• EBITDA at ₹10,252 million, resulted in an EBITDA margin of 22.5%, a growth of 
11.3% YoY. 
• R&D expenses for Q2 FY27 were ₹1,953 million, or 4.3% of total revenue from 
operations, vs. ₹1,302 million in Q2 FY26 at 3.3% of total revenue from operations. 
• Profit before tax (before exceptional item) was ₹ 9,646 million, YoY growth of 7.7%. 
• Net Profit (after Non-Controlling interest) was ₹6,753 million, YoY de-growth of 11.7%. 
• Net Cash stood at INR 49,054 mn (as on 30 September 2026) 
 
Q2FY27 Operational Highlights 
 
Domestic Business Key Highlights 
• The contribution of domestic sales to total sales was 68% vs. 70% in Q2 FY26. 
• According to IQVIA (SSA) data, for Q2 FY27: 

o The Company registered a growth of 13.8% YoY a t p a r w i t h Indian 
Pharmaceutical Market (IPM), growth of 13.8%. 
o Acute segment reported growth of 12.1% at par with IPM growth of 12.3%. 
o Chronic segment reported growth of 22.4% vs. IPM which grew by 16%, +640 
bps outperformance.  
o We have outperformed IPM in eight key focused therapies: VMN ~1.2x, Pain 
~1.5x, Anti-Diabetic ~1.5x, Cardiac by 1.1x, Urology by 1.1x, Respiratory 
~1.6x, Neuro/CNS by 1.1x and Derma ~1.6x. 
 
International Business Key Highlights 
• US sales were ₹7,830 million, YoY growth of 2.4%. 
• US business sales contributed 17% to total sales in Q2 FY27 vs. 19% in Q2 FY26. 
• Non-US sales were ₹6,710 million, YoY growth of 58%. Excluding Occlutech, Non-US 
sales grew 28.6% YoY. 
• Non-US business sales contributed 15% to total sales in Q2 FY27 v.s. 11% in Q2 FY26.

1. We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of Consolidated Unaudited Financial Results of 
Alkem Laboratories Limited ("the Parent") and its subsidiaries (the Parent and its subsidiaries 
together referred to as "the Group") and its share of the net loss after tax and total comprehensive 
income of its associate for the quarter and six months ended September 30, 2026 ("the 
Statement") which includes the branch of the Group located at Nepal, being submitted by the 
Parent pursuant to the requirement of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended ("the Listing Regulations"). 
2. This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Parent's Management and approved by the 
Parent's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and 
measurement principles laid down in the Indian Accounting Standard 34 "Interim Financial 
Reporting" (''Ind AS 34"), prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with 
relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and 
in compliance with Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. Our responsibility is to express a 
conclusion on the Statement based on our review. 
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review 
Engagements (SRE) 2410 "Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent 
Auditor of the Entity", issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (!CAI). A review 
of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of Parent's personnel 
responsible for financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review 
procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with 
Standards on Auditing specified under Section 143(10) of the Companies Act, 2013 and 
consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant 
matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion. 
We also performed procedures in accordance with the circular issued by the SEBI under Regulation 
33(8) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as 
amended, to the extent applicable. 
4. The Statement includes the results of the entities mentioned in Annexure 1 to this report. 
5. Based on our review conducted and procedures performed as stated in paragraph 3 above and 
based on the consideration of the review reports of the other auditors referred to in paragraph 6 
below, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying 
Statement, prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in 
the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standard and other accounting principles generally accepted in 
India, has not disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms of Regulation 33 of the 
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended, including 
the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement.

As we conclude another successful quarter for the company, our priorities at Sai remain unchanged: 
to deepen our relationships with global pharmaceutical companies, expand the range and complexity 
of services we offer, and build the capacity and capabilities required to support customers over the 
long term. 
We are making progress on each of these fronts. We are seeing continued interest from large pharma, 
increased traction from our integrated outsourcing model, and steady progress on our capacity 
expansion programme. 
Let me begin with a brief overview of the broader operating environment. 
Tailwinds supporting supply chain diversification continue. We remain focused on converting these 
opportunities into sustainable business growth. 
Recent developments in the U.S. and China add another dimension to this. In the U.S., the proposed 
rules under the COINS Act seek to introduce additional restrictions on certain U.S. investments 
involving Chinese biotechnology companies. Separately, China's Ministry of Commerce and 
Ministry of Science and Technology have proposed additional controls on the export of selected 
technologies, including in the biomedicine space.

reinforce the importance of geographic diversification and the need for pharmaceutical companies to 
build resilient alternate supply chain partnerships.

relationships with global innovators, our integrated capabilities, our track record of supporting 
customers across discovery, development, and manufacturing. The advantage increasingly lies with 
CRDMOs that have scientific depth, infrastructure, and customer relationships to take on larger, more 
strategic engagements. 
The ongoing situation in the Middle East is also having some impact on the cost of certain chemicals 
and solvents. While this has created some cost pressure, our proactive supply chain management has 
ensured continuity of material availability. We are working closely with customers to recover the 
incremental costs wherever applicable. 
On the business front, we continue to see good traction in outsourcing opportunities from the large 
pharmaceutical companies. 
An important milestone this quarter has been the consolidation of our position as an integrated 
CRDMO of choice to large pharma customers. During the last investor call, we had announced our 
first end-to-end integrated collaboration with a top-tier market-cap pharma company. We have since 
commenced operations with this customer.

similar strategic engagement. We are also working on extending this model to other large 
pharmaceutical companies. Discussions are progressing with a few more large pharma customers, 
and we see encouraging potential to deepen these relationships over time. 
Our focus remains on building long-term partnerships where we can progressively expand the scope 
of work from individual projects to integrated engagements spanning discovery and development, 
and eventually into manufacturing. We believe that such integrated partnerships will help us build a 
robust, consistent, and predictable long-term pipeline and revenues. 
With that, I will hand this over to Siva to take you through the operating performance and the progress 
of our capacity expansion and capex programme.

OIL reported 20% growth in crude oil production resulting to 116% growth in 
Standalone PAT during Q2 FY27 
 
Oil India Limited, the Maharatna CPSE of Govt. of India, declared its financial results for 
Q2FY27, in its 586th meeting of the Board of Directors held on 12th November 2026 at New 
Delhi.  
The Company achieved a growth of 53% in 
Consolidated PAT at ₹ 2,521 crore in Q2 
FY27 vis-à-vis ₹ 1,644 crore in Q2 FY26. 
The consolidated PAT for the half year 
ended 30.09.2026 is ₹ 6,548 crore vis-à-vis 
₹ 
3,690 
crore 
during 
corresponding 
previous half year, a growth of 77%. 
The Company achieved a PAT of ₹ 2,259 Cr. 
in Q2FY27 vis-à-vis ₹ 1,044 Cr in Q2FY26, 
a growth of 116%, due to increase in crude 
oil production by 20% and crude oil price 
realisation by 35% from USD 68.19/bbl in 
Q2FY26 to USD 92.24/bbl in Q2FY27. The 
Company 
registered 
highest 
ever 
Standalone PAT for the half year ended 
30.09.2026 at ₹ 5,130 crore as compared to ₹ 1,857 crore during corresponding previous half 
year, a growth of 176%. 
The Board of Directors of the Company has recommended an Interim Dividend of ₹ 7.00/- per 
fully paid equity share of ₹10 each. 
In its efforts towards ensuring Nation’s Energy Security, the Company, continuing its sustained 
efforts, produced 1.021 MMT of crude oil from its matured and old oilfields in Q2FY27 vis-à-
vis 0.848 MMT in Q2 FY26. OIL has achieved highest daily production of 11,300 MT (87,051 
bbls) on 29.09.2026 of crude oil, which is highest daily production during the last decade.  

 
During the first half of the year, the Company recorded its highest-ever half-year drilling 
performance, with 42 wells drilled, setting a new benchmark in its operational achievements.  
OIL’s material subsidiary NRL continued to demonstrate strong operational performance 
supported by sustained operational efficiency and effective refinery management. Crude 
throughput during Q2 FY27 stood at 803 TMT, registering an increase over 753 TMT in the 
corresponding quarter of the previous year. For H1 FY 2026-27, crude throughput reached 
1,594 TMT, compared to 1,552 TMT in H1 FY 2025-26. 
The Refinery maintained capacity utilisation of over 100%, achieving 106.26% during H1 FY 
2026-27, compared to 103.48% in the corresponding period of the previous year. Distillate 
yield also improved to 87.15% from 86.64%, reflecting sustained focus on operational efficiency 
and product optimisation. 
NRL registered a strong improvement in refining performance, with its Gross Refining Margin 
(GRM) rising to US$ 28.24/bbl during half year ended 30.09.2026, compared to US$ 7.73/bbl 
during half year ended 30.09.2025, reflecting a robust 265% growth. 
Issued by -Public Relations Department, New Delhi

OIL reported 20% growth in crude oil production resulting to 116% growth in 
Standalone PAT during Q2 FY27 
 
Oil India Limited, the Maharatna CPSE of Govt. of India, declared its financial results for 
Q2FY27, in its 586th meeting of the Board of Directors held on 12th November 2026 at New 
Delhi.  
The Company achieved a growth of 53% in 
Consolidated PAT at ₹ 2,521 crore in Q2 
FY27 vis-à-vis ₹ 1,644 crore in Q2 FY26. 
The consolidated PAT for the half year 
ended 30.09.2026 is ₹ 6,548 crore vis-à-vis 
₹ 
3,690 
crore 
during 
corresponding 
previous half year, a growth of 77%. 
The Company achieved a PAT of ₹ 2,259 Cr. 
in Q2FY27 vis-à-vis ₹ 1,044 Cr in Q2FY26, 
a growth of 116%, due to increase in crude 
oil production by 20% and crude oil price 
realisation by 35% from USD 68.19/bbl in 
Q2FY26 to USD 92.24/bbl in Q2FY27. The 
Company 
registered 
highest 
ever 
Standalone PAT for the half year ended 
30.09.2026 at ₹ 5,130 crore as compared to ₹ 1,857 crore during corresponding previous half 
year, a growth of 176%. 
The Board of Directors of the Company has recommended an Interim Dividend of ₹ 7.00/- per 
fully paid equity share of ₹10 each. 
In its efforts towards ensuring Nation’s Energy Security, the Company, continuing its sustained 
efforts, produced 1.021 MMT of crude oil from its matured and old oilfields in Q2FY27 vis-à-
vis 0.848 MMT in Q2 FY26. OIL has achieved highest daily production of 11,300 MT (87,051 
bbls) on 29.09.2026 of crude oil, which is highest daily production during the last decade.  

 
During the first half of the year, the Company recorded its highest-ever half-year drilling 
performance, with 42 wells drilled, setting a new benchmark in its operational achievements.  
OIL’s material subsidiary NRL continued to demonstrate strong operational performance 
supported by sustained operational efficiency and effective refinery management. Crude 
throughput during Q2 FY27 stood at 803 TMT, registering an increase over 753 TMT in the 
corresponding quarter of the previous year. For H1 FY 2026-27, crude throughput reached 
1,594 TMT, compared to 1,552 TMT in H1 FY 2025-26. 
The Refinery maintained capacity utilisation of over 100%, achieving 106.26% during H1 FY 
2026-27, compared to 103.48% in the corresponding period of the previous year. Distillate 
yield also improved to 87.15% from 86.64%, reflecting sustained focus on operational efficiency 
and product optimisation. 
NRL registered a strong improvement in refining performance, with its Gross Refining Margin 
(GRM) rising to US$ 28.24/bbl during half year ended 30.09.2026, compared to US$ 7.73/bbl 
during half year ended 30.09.2025, reflecting a robust 265% growth. 
Issued by -Public Relations Department, New Delhi

4' Service Tax demand was raised on the Company for the period March 2016 to June, 2017 seeking to levy
Service Tax on Royalty paid on Crude Oil & Natural Gas under the Oil Fields (Regulation & Development)
Act, 1948 for the States of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Rajasthan. The Company has challenged the
demand on various grounds by filing writ petitions before different High Courts. However, pending
adjudication of the Writs, the Company has deposited under protest the entire Service Tax demand of {
257.13 crore.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented w.e.f, 1st July 2017 and as per the FAQs on Government
Services issued by CBIC, GST is payable on Royalty paid for assignment of right to use natural resources.
However, based on a legal opinion obtained by the Company, Service tax/GST is not payable on Royalty
payable/paid under the Oil Fields (Regulation & Development) Act, 1948. The Company has accordingly
filed Writ Petitions in different High Courts challenging such levy. Further, the Hon'ble Gauhati High Court,
vide its interim order dated 2nd November 202I has granted stay on the GST on royalty payments made by
the Company in the State of Assam until further orders. Keeping in view the jurisdiction of Gauhati High
Court, the Company has submitted a representation to GST Department, Arunachal Pradesh and the
payment of GST on this account in the state of Arunachal Pradesh was put on hold.
All pending cases of the Company before Gauhati High Court and Rajasthan High Court were transferred to
Hon'ble Supreme Court for hearing by the Nine Judge Constitution Bench. However, Hon'ble Supreme Court
vide its order dated 14th March 2024 de-tagged the cases from the Civil Appeals Nos. 4056-4064/1999. The
Hon'ble Supreme Court vide its judgement dated 25.07.2024 in Mineral Area Development Authority Vs.
Steel Authority of India Limited (MADA) held that royalty under Mines and Mineral (Development and
Regulation) Act (MMDR Act) is not a tax. However, the nature of royalty under Oilfields (Regulation and
Development) Act is to be decided by the Court separately as it has the distinct constitution provision.
In a recent development, the Hon'ble Supreme Court have taken note of the submission made on behalf of
the Company by the Learned Solicitor General of India to deposit the GST as per law within a period of six
weeks, subject to final outcome of the pending proceedings. The Hon'ble Supreme Court thereafter tagged
the Transfer Petition (C) 300-304/2024, with C.A. No. 1056012025 (Udaipur Chamber of Commerce and

Dear Sir/ Madam, 
 
Sub: Intimation under Regulation 30 read with Regulation 30(11) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 
 
Ref: Clarification on the news article published by Moneycontrol on November 11, 2026 titled 
"Waaree admitted misreporting solar import origin in submission to US trade 
commission"; our disclosures dated June 28, 2026 and November 2, 2026 
 
With reference to the above news article (the "Article"), which has gained widespread circulation on 
media, the Company considers it appropriate to provide the following clarification for information of 
its shareholders and other stake holders. 
 
The Article quotes from the public report of the US International Trade Commission (“USITC”) in its 
investigation into solar imports from India, Indonesia and Laos. That investigation covers the Indian 
solar industry as a whole; it is not a case against Waaree. Waaree took part in it, along with other 
Indian manufacturers, to defend the interests of Indian exporters. There is no finding, penalty or 
liability separately assessed against Waaree in that proceeding. 
 
The statement quoted in the Article is about how the country of origin was reported on certain past 
shipments to the United States. Our modules are made in India and were declared as Indian-origin, 
in line with Indian rules of origin. US Customs, for duty purposes, uses the country in which the solar 
cells were made. This difference affected certain historical shipments and had a duty impact on a 
limited number of entries. This is the same matter that US Customs and Border Protection (“CBP”) 
examined and that we disclosed to the stock exchanges on June 28, 2026. The data we provided to 
the USITC was prepared on the same basis and included information and reporting already covered 
by Waaree’s past disclosures. Nothing new has been admitted, and nothing has been withheld from 
the exchanges or from investors. 
 
After verifying our plant in India, CBP as part of its investigation confirmed that Waaree did not ship 
any modules made with Chinese cells to the United States and declined to extend its finding to all 
our shipments. CBP’s findings regarding AD/CVD duty liability remain limited to a small set of past 
shipments. 
 
There is no new financial or operational impact specifically for Waaree resulting from the ITC’s 
findings. The possible exposure of AD/CVD duties on the limited set of shipments is already reflected 
in our financial statements, as disclosed on November 2, 2026, and no fine or penalty has been 
imposed. Our US business, including our manufacturing facility in Texas, continues as usual.  

 
WAAREE Energies Ltd.

Email: waaree@waaree.com.Website:www.waaree.com 
Corporate Identity Number:L29248MH1990PLC059463 
 
 
The rationalisation of the Company's order book referred to in the Article was disclosed by the 
Company with its financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 and 
explained on the Company's earnings call. It reflects a prudent reassessment of certain direct-
export contracts in light of U.S. trade measures affecting imports of solar products into the United 
States generally, which are not specific to the Company. It is not a consequence of the CBP 
proceeding or of the Company's submissions to the USITC. The order book figures cited in the Article 
are those previously disclosed by the Company. 
 
As informed on November 2, 2026, we are evaluating a challenge to CBP's decision before the US 
Court of International Trade and will keep the exchanges informed. Shareholders are requested to 
rely only on the Company's official disclosures to the stock exchanges and on www.waaree.com,

are pleased to deliver double-digit revenue growth of 11.5% in Q2 FY27, driven by healthy volume 
growth, premiumisation and strong consumer response to our new launches. While raw material costs 
remained elevated, our profitability has remained within our planned range. With positive demand 
trends, strong brand momentum, an exciting pipeline of new product ranges and ongoing initiatives to 
improve operational efficiency, we look ahead with confidence.” 
Outlook and Trends:

months. Trusted brands, a fresh line-up of products and a wider retail presence leave us well placed to 
capture this momentum. Expanded manufacturing capacity, streamlined processes and technology-
led productivity gains will help us serve demand faster and at lower cost, while we stay vigilant on 
input costs.

Page Industries Limited delivers 11.5% revenue growth in Q2 FY27 
 
 
 
Bengaluru, 12th November 2026: Page Industries Limited, India’s leading apparel manufacturer, today 
announced its financial results for the second quarter and half year ended 30th September, 2026  
 
 
Key Financial Highlights for Q2 FY 27: 
• 
Revenue  was Rs. 14,396 million growing by 11.5% YOY 
• 
Sales volume was 59.7 million pieces growing by 5.5% YOY 
• 
EBITDA was Rs. 3,001 million growing by 7.4% YOY, a margin of 20.8% 
• 
Profit After Tax (PAT) was Rs. 2,025 million growing by 4% YOY, a margin of 14.1% 
 
Key Financial Highlights for H1 FY 27: 
• 
Revenue was Rs. 28,601 million growing by 9.7% YOY 
• 
Sales volume was 121.7 million pieces growing by 5.6% YOY 
• 
EBITDA was Rs. 5,891 million growing by 2.6% YOY, a margin of 20.6% 
• 
Profit After Tax (PAT) was Rs. 3,954 million, broadly flat YOY, a margin of 13.8% 
 
Commenting on the results, Mr. V.S. Ganesh, Managing Director, Page Industries Limited said, “We 
are pleased to deliver double-digit revenue growth of 11.5% in Q2 FY27, driven by healthy volume 
growth, premiumisation and strong consumer response to our new launches. While raw material costs 
remained elevated, our profitability has remained within our planned range. With positive demand 
trends, strong brand momentum, an exciting pipeline of new product ranges and ongoing initiatives to 
improve operational efficiency, we look ahead with confidence.” 
Outlook and Trends: 
As the festive season gets under way, we expect a healthy lift in consumer demand over the coming 
months. Trusted brands, a fresh line-up of products and a wider retail presence leave us well placed to 
capture this momentum. Expanded manufacturing capacity, streamlined processes and technology-
led productivity gains will help us serve demand faster and at lower cost, while we stay vigilant on 
input costs. 
 
About Page Industries Limited 
Page Industries is the exclusive licensee of JOCKEY International Inc. (USA) for manufacture, distribution and 
marketing of the JOCKEY® brand in India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Oman, Qatar, Maldives, Bhutan UAE, 
Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Bahrain. Page Industries is also the exclusive licensee of Speedo (Pentland Group) for 
the manufacture, marketing and distribution of the Speedo brand in India.   
 
Jockey is the company’s flagship brand and a market leader in the premium innerwear and athleisure category. 
The brand is distributed in 2,722 cities & towns and available in 1,14,591 Multi Brand Outlets, 1,626 Exclusive

materials linked to crude oil remained well above earlier levels. We chose to absorb part of this inflation 
ourselves through price increase initiated in Q1 and offset some of the strain. Even so, EBITDA margin stayed

Our transformation agenda is progressing steadily. The S/4HANA rollout is on course for a Q4 go-live, the

programmes are tracking well. Collectively, these investments are meant to make the organisation more agile

“
It gives me great pride to present our 7th Sustainability Report, which captures Page 
Industries’ continued journey of responsible growth, environmental stewardship, and 
social responsibility. This year’s report showcases how we have deepened our 
sustainability integration across all facets of our business while remaining aligned 
with India’s long-term development goals and global ESG best practices.
Despite a dynamic business environment, we delivered resilient performance in FY 
2024–25, meeting strategic and sustainability goals through strong governance, 
innovation, and stakeholder engagement. We strengthened our sustainability 
ambitions across water stewardship (ZLD, rainwater harvesting, and per-capita 
consumption), climate action, and resource efficiency. Renewable energy reached 
33% of total consumption, while Scope 1 & 2 GHG intensity declined to 5.42 tCO₂e 
per million minutes produced, marking a 42% reduction from the FY 2019–20 base 
year. Our circularity efforts achieved zero waste to landfill, validated through 
comprehensive traceability audits across all hazardous and non-hazardous waste 
recyclers.
Through Value Chain Partner (VCP) mapping and structured supplier engagement, 
we embed environmental, social, and ethical standards across our upstream 
partnerships, strengthening supply chain resilience and stakeholder trust. We also 
advance diversity and inclusion through women’s empowerment initiatives that 
promote equity and foster a culture where everyone can thrive viewed as both a 
social responsibility and a strategic advantage.
Sunder (Ashok) Genomal,
Looking ahead, we will continue to drive innovation-led 
sustainability, delivering profitable growth in harmony 
with people and the planet. On behalf of the Board, I 
thank our 23,400+ employees, partners, and stakeholders 
for their trust and collaboration, which inspire us to 
uphold excellence, ethics, and sustainability as a core 
strength of Page Industries.
“

7 The Board of Directors of the Company at their meeting held on August 13, 2026 and November 12, 2026, have declared

8 The Government of India has consolidated 29 existing labour legislations into a unified framework comprising four labour 
codes as follows: Code on Wages, 2019, Code on Social Security, 2020, Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (collectively referred to as the "New Labour Codes"). The New Labour 
Codes are effective from November 21, 2025 and introduce changes that include, among other things, setting a uniform 
definition of wages. The Government is in the process of issuing related rules to the New Labour Codes. The New Labour 
Codes have implications on employee benefits including gratuity, leave encashment and other related obligations. 
The Company had assessed the implication of the New Labour Codes and had recognised an incremental cost oft 3,408.90 
lakhs and t 91.52 lakhs towards employee benefit expenses and other expenses respectively, during the year ended March 
31, 2026. Considering the non-recurring nature of this impact, the Company had presented such incremental impact under 
'Exceptional items' in the Statement of Ind AS Financial Results for the year ended March 31, 2026. The Company continues 
to monitor the developments pertaining to the New Labour Codes and the impact of these will be accounted in accordance 
with applicable accounting standards. 
9 The Company has carr_ied out retail trading of Jockey and Speedo branded products, including imported products, through 
e-commerce without establishing physical retail stores. Such retail trading of imported products of multiple brands was not 
in accordance with the retail trading provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019, 
issued under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA).

On October 16, 2026, the RBI returned the application and advised the Company to first obtain post-facto approval from 
the Government of India. Management is in the process of obtaining the approval and plans to reapply for compounding 
thereafter. 
The Management expects the non-compliance to be compounded by the RBI and the financial impact, if any is not likely to 
be material. Accordingly, no adjustment has been made to the financial results. 
10 The Company has reclassified certain balances within inventories, trade receivables, other financial assets, other assets, 
other financial liabilities and other liabilities in the Balance Sheet as at March 31, 2026, in accordance with the applicable 
reporting requirements. The adjustments made to the comparative financial information are not considered material to these 
financial results.
