Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call Transcript 
November 05, 2026 
 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the PI Industries Q2 and FY27 
earnings conference call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only 
mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation 
concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an 
operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this 
conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Siddharth from 
CDR India. Thank you and over to you, Siddharth. 
Siddharth Rangnekar: Good afternoon and thank you for joining us on the PI Industries Q2 and H1 FY27 
earnings conference call. Today we are joined by senior members of the 
management team including:  
• 
Mr. Mayank Singhal, Executive Vice Chairperson and Managing Director  
• 
Mr. Sanjay Agarwal, Group Chief Financial Officer  
• 
Dr. Atul Gupta, CEO, CSM AgChem and Executive Director  
• 
Mr. Jagresh Rana, Global CEO of PI AgSciences 
We shall commence with key perspectives from Mr. Singhal, following which we will 
have Mr. Agarwal sharing his views on the company's financial performance. 
Thereafter, the forum will be open for question-and-answer session.  
Before we begin, I would like to underline that certain statements made on today's 
call could be forward-looking in nature. A disclaimer to this effect has been included 
in the investor presentation that is available on the stock exchange website and has 
been mailed to you separately earlier.  
With that, I would like to invite Mr. Singhal to share his perspectives with you. Thank 
you and over to you, sir. 

 
Page 2 of 21 
 
 
Mayank Singhal: 
Good afternoon, everybody and thank you for joining the call today. This has been a 
difficult quarter in a difficult year for the industry. The global crop protection cycle is 
at low points, and we are feeling like everyone in the business. What I want to do 
instead is to tell you what we are doing about it and why we believe PI comes out of 
this cycle stronger, more differentiated and more valuable. 
PI has been through cycles before. In each one, we have made the same choice. 
Keep investing in the capabilities that matter, take the hard decisions earlier than 
later and come out the other side with a better business. This is exactly what we are 
doing now. We have a strong track record of identifying emerging opportunities early, 
investing ahead of the curve and translating differentiated capabilities into scalable 
businesses. 
PI has always taken opportunistic and unique approaches to business. We start with 
innovative led agri-distribution, moved into CSM three decades ago and now I am 
proud to say, with our investment in R&D beginning 12 years ago, we are now India's 
first and only agchem innovator. With this long-term vision, we have consistently 
delivered stronger execution and value creation. 
We see similar potential in the platforms we are building today across the pharma 
CRDMO, global biologicals and specialty & electronic chemical manufacturing driven 
by continued innovation, capability development and customer engagement. These 
platforms are in the build-out phase, and we are confident these investments will 
increasingly contribute to our growth in time to come. 
PI's core is reflected in our innovation, manufacturing and marketing excellence 
through a decade of experience. We have been able to build the best-in-class assets, 
leveraging differentiated technologies and assess newer areas of the market. We 
talk a lot about innovation. We do so as the only Indian ag innovator. We continue to 
invest in deploying and building a moat around scientific talent, infrastructure, 
technology platform and product portfolios. These investments propel us into a 
differentiated category from molecules to markets deepening customer engagement 
and helping us build multi-engines for future growth.  
Turning to the global crop protection market, channel stocks are back to normal 
levels, and that part of the correction is behind the industry. Uneven weather across 
the key geographies, rising input costs, tight channel credits meant growers bought 
late, bought less and bought cheaper. Generic pricing pressure compounded that.  
None of this changes the structural picture. The world has to feed more people with 
less land, less water, tighter regulations on what can be used. That is the only 

 
Page 3 of 21 
 
 
possibility with innovation in products and with supply chains that partner can trust. 
Those are the two things PI spent decades building.  
In India, the season was defined by the weakest monsoon in over a decade with 
prolonged dry spells, delayed sowing and, as a result, lower pest pressure. Kharif 
acreage was flat and the season was lacklustre. Going into rabi, soil moisture and 
reservoir levels are below last year in several rain-fed belts, so we are planning for 
a cautious Rabi and will respond to how the season actually develops.  
On the brighter side, prices of major commodities have firmed up from their lows, 
which, if sustained, points to better farm economics in the next season. 
Now let me take you to the PI businesses. Let me address our export business.  
The environment remains hard: subdued crop economics, elevated input costs, 
genericization arriving faster than the industry expected and pricing pressures 
across the board. Considering the global market situation, we took pragmatic pricing 
decisions in order to compete for a higher volume that comes with genericization. 
Conversely, we have commercialized 20 plus molecules in the last three to five years 
in different parts of the life cycle, carrying differentiated process technology and 
innovator margins. Coupled with the ongoing diversification in our pipeline, they are 
the engines of the next leg of growth in the business. Customers increasingly see PI 
not just as a manufacturing partner but a trusted scientific partner who is capable 
and can help them to address their needs and compete. This is a position earned 
over decades, not something that can be taken away by short-term challenges.  
Our domestic business continues to hold its ground with strong year-on-year growth 
of 19% despite the challenging market dynamics, supported by a portfolio of 
differentiated high-value crop protection solutions and strong market position across 
key brands. Our focus remains on expanding market share and capitalizing on the 
ever-changing market opportunity through robust agile go-to-market and brand 
strength, with flagship brands continue to maintain leadership positions.  
Biologicals deserve a specific mention here. Our domestic portfolio has grown by 
45% and our global portfolio has seen more than 250% growth this quarter as 
farmers continue to adopt sustainable solutions. We have been building this platform 
potentially for two decades. What began as India opportunity now is a global one, 
strengthened by our PREtec peptide technology. Globally, thousands of field 
demonstrations across crops, climate and geographies keep confirming what we 

 
Page 4 of 21 
 
 
believed early: biologicals will sit alongside with chemistry at the center of the next 
generation of crop protection and PI intends to capture both.

years ago, we made a decision that was no Indian agrochemical companies ever 
made before: to invest in discovering our own molecules. It was expensive, it was 
slow and for most of that time it showed up only as a cost. This quarter showed up 
as something else. 
Pioxaniliprole branded as Pioxazon, our first new chemical entity has received a 
registration in India and has been launched as Pioxazon:  an insecticide that targets 
some of the most economically damaging pests in rice, corn and Bengal gram, while 
we continue to expand our labels for different crops. Regulatory filings are 
progressing in other geographies across the world, and we are preparing a path for 
global commercialization in the coming years. 
A molecule is a product, but the more important fact is our ability to discover molecule 
is now a platform. That platform now exists, in India, inside PI. It covers discovery, 
chemistry, biology, formulation, toxicology, agronomy, process development, 
manufacturing, end-to-end capability. The first molecule proves the platform works. 
We are expecting to bring another two to three chemical and biological molecules in 
the global arena in the next few years, opening up a significant opportunity led by 
innovation to leverage global partnerships. That is what makes PI different from 
every other company in the sector. We are not manufacturers or marketeers of 
molecules, we are now an innovator for the growers, both Indian and global. We will 
continue to bring innovation from India to the world with our partner-centric model.

patiently, is behind our newer platforms. These are the businesses that make the 
future and we are building them with the same discipline as we built CSM for three 
decades and the brand business in India. Capability first, customers alongside, scale 
when the economics are proven.

conservatively, protect our cost positions, keep the balance sheet strong and keep 
investing in building our future moats.

that has reset when it has to and is rebuilding a younger, harder, better margin 
molecule. A biological platform that is now global.  New platforms in pharma and 
electronic chemical coming to life. And for the first time, an innovation engine that 
has proved that it can take a molecule from an idea in Udaipur lab to the farmers in 
the field in India and going to the world.

company, creating original science and intellectual property from India for the world.

Siddharth Rangnekar: Good afternoon and thank you for joining us on the PI Industries Q2 and H1 FY27 
earnings conference call. Today we are joined by senior members of the 
management team including:  
• 
Mr. Mayank Singhal, Executive Vice Chairperson and Managing Director  
• 
Mr. Sanjay Agarwal, Group Chief Financial Officer  
•

• 
Mr. Jagresh Rana, Global CEO of PI AgSciences

have Mr. Agarwal sharing his views on the company's financial performance.

call could be forward-looking in nature. A disclaimer to this effect has been included 
in the investor presentation that is available on the stock exchange website and has 
been mailed to you separately earlier.  
With that, I would like to invite Mr. Singhal to share his perspectives with you. Thank 
you and over to you, sir.

Mayank Singhal: 
Good afternoon, everybody and thank you for joining the call today. This has been a 
difficult quarter in a difficult year for the industry. The global crop protection cycle is 
at low points, and we are feeling like everyone in the business. What I want to do 
instead is to tell you what we are doing about it and why we believe PI comes out of 
this cycle stronger, more differentiated and more valuable. 
PI has been through cycles before. In each one, we have made the same choice. 
Keep investing in the capabilities that matter, take the hard decisions earlier than 
later and come out the other side with a better business. This is exactly what we are 
doing now. We have a strong track record of identifying emerging opportunities early, 
investing ahead of the curve and translating differentiated capabilities into scalable 
businesses. 
PI has always taken opportunistic and unique approaches to business. We start with 
innovative led agri-distribution, moved into CSM three decades ago and now I am 
proud to say, with our investment in R&D beginning 12 years ago, we are now India's 
first and only agchem innovator. With this long-term vision, we have consistently 
delivered stronger execution and value creation. 
We see similar potential in the platforms we are building today across the pharma 
CRDMO, global biologicals and specialty & electronic chemical manufacturing driven 
by continued innovation, capability development and customer engagement. These 
platforms are in the build-out phase, and we are confident these investments will 
increasingly contribute to our growth in time to come. 
PI's core is reflected in our innovation, manufacturing and marketing excellence 
through a decade of experience. We have been able to build the best-in-class assets, 
leveraging differentiated technologies and assess newer areas of the market. We 
talk a lot about innovation. We do so as the only Indian ag innovator. We continue to 
invest in deploying and building a moat around scientific talent, infrastructure, 
technology platform and product portfolios. These investments propel us into a 
differentiated category from molecules to markets deepening customer engagement 
and helping us build multi-engines for future growth.  
Turning to the global crop protection market, channel stocks are back to normal 
levels, and that part of the correction is behind the industry. Uneven weather across 
the key geographies, rising input costs, tight channel credits meant growers bought 
late, bought less and bought cheaper. Generic pricing pressure compounded that.  
None of this changes the structural picture. The world has to feed more people with 
less land, less water, tighter regulations on what can be used. That is the only 

 
Page 3 of 21 
 
 
possibility with innovation in products and with supply chains that partner can trust. 
Those are the two things PI spent decades building.  
In India, the season was defined by the weakest monsoon in over a decade with 
prolonged dry spells, delayed sowing and, as a result, lower pest pressure. Kharif 
acreage was flat and the season was lacklustre. Going into rabi, soil moisture and 
reservoir levels are below last year in several rain-fed belts, so we are planning for 
a cautious Rabi and will respond to how the season actually develops.  
On the brighter side, prices of major commodities have firmed up from their lows, 
which, if sustained, points to better farm economics in the next season. 
Now let me take you to the PI businesses. Let me address our export business.  
The environment remains hard: subdued crop economics, elevated input costs, 
genericization arriving faster than the industry expected and pricing pressures 
across the board. Considering the global market situation, we took pragmatic pricing 
decisions in order to compete for a higher volume that comes with genericization. 
Conversely, we have commercialized 20 plus molecules in the last three to five years 
in different parts of the life cycle, carrying differentiated process technology and 
innovator margins. Coupled with the ongoing diversification in our pipeline, they are 
the engines of the next leg of growth in the business. Customers increasingly see PI 
not just as a manufacturing partner but a trusted scientific partner who is capable 
and can help them to address their needs and compete. This is a position earned 
over decades, not something that can be taken away by short-term challenges.  
Our domestic business continues to hold its ground with strong year-on-year growth 
of 19% despite the challenging market dynamics, supported by a portfolio of 
differentiated high-value crop protection solutions and strong market position across 
key brands. Our focus remains on expanding market share and capitalizing on the 
ever-changing market opportunity through robust agile go-to-market and brand 
strength, with flagship brands continue to maintain leadership positions.

45% and our global portfolio has seen more than 250% growth this quarter as 
farmers continue to adopt sustainable solutions. We have been building this platform 
potentially for two decades. What began as India opportunity now is a global one, 
strengthened by our PREtec peptide technology. Globally, thousands of field 
demonstrations across crops, climate and geographies keep confirming what we

slow and for most of that time it showed up only as a cost. This quarter showed up

progressing in other geographies across the world, and we are preparing a path for 
global commercialization in the coming years.

twenty‑nine existing labour laws into a comprehensive framework governing employee benefits during and after employment. The Ministry of Labour and

evaluation, and considering the guidance issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, the Company has concluded that the estimated impact on
its existing obligations is not material. The Company will continue to monitor the finalisation of central and state rules and further governmental
clarifications, and will recognise any necessary accounting impact arising from such developments in due course.

The Board of the Directors of the Company at its meeting held on May 20, 2025 and the shareholders of the company at Extraordinary General Meeting held
on June 13, 2025 has approved the allotment of up to 20,13,885 convertible warrants each convertible into, or exchangeable for, one fully paid up equity share
of the Company, having a face value of Rs. 2, within the period of eighteen months in accordance with the applicable laws at a price of Rs. 864 aggregating up
to Rs. 173.99 crores ("issue proceeds").
During the previous year ended March 31, 2026, the Company has received 25% of the issue proceeds i.e., Rs. 43.50 crores (Upfront monies) on June 23,
2025 and June 24, 2025.
On November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified four labour codes—the Code on Wages, 2019; the Industrial Relations Code, 2020; the Code on
Social Security, 2020; and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (collectively, the “Labour Codes”)—which consolidate
twenty‑nine existing labour laws into a comprehensive framework governing employee benefits during and after employment. The Ministry of Labour and
Employment has also issued draft Central Rules and FAQs to facilitate assessment of the financial implications of these changes. Based on management’s
evaluation, and considering the guidance issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, the Company has concluded that the estimated impact on
its existing obligations is not material. The Company will continue to monitor the finalisation of central and state rules and further governmental
clarifications, and will recognise any necessary accounting impact arising from such developments in due course.
On June 10, 2026, the Board of Directors approved the Scheme of Arrangement between Astra Microwave Products Limited (the “Demerged Company”) and
Astra Space Technologies Private Limited ( the “Resulting Company”) and their respective shareholders and creditors, under Sections 230 to 232 and other
applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and applicable SEBI regulations, providing for the demerger of the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology
Business of the Company on a going concern basis. The Scheme would become effective after receipt of all requisite approvals as mentioned in the Scheme.
Pending receipt of necessary approvals, no effect of the Scheme has been given in the standalone financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

FINANCIAL OFFICER 
MODERATOR: ASIAN MARKETS SECURITIES LIMITED 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen):  
Good evening, everyone. Am I audible? Kamlesh? 
 
Moderator: 
Yes, yes, please. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Good evening, everyone. I'm Indranil. I'm the CFO of Elgi and apologies to all of you. Really sorry. Dr. 
Jai is trying to get in the call still, but he's requested us to go ahead. So, I'll be initiating the 
presentation. Can we move to the next slide, please? Yeah, so as we start the year, we've had a good 
quarter. Growth over previous year is at 17%. Out of the 17% growth, around 4% is driven by foreign 
exchange and the EBITDA and consequent to that 17% growth, our EBITDA has grown year on year by 
28%. Can you move to the next slide? This is our sales mix, Compressors kind of continue to drive 92% 
of our overall revenues. The mix has not changed, but when it comes to India and Rest of the World 
(ROW), in particular, in this quarter, India has overperformed over ROW markets and that's how you 
see a mix of 52% and 48%, I'll talk through a little bit more around that in my subsequent slides. If you 
take a look at the geographical sales trend, India has shown tremendous improvement both year on 
year and sequential quarters. So is the case with North America. Sequentially, we are able to maintain 
a higher trajectory of revenue and there has been significant growth over previous year. In Europe, 
our industrial business has seen growth year on year, but our portables business in Italy has seen 
muted performance primarily because of economic downturn in various markets of Europe. As far as 
Australia is concerned, we have seen good growth in our units business, whereas service has remained 
slightly muted. Can we move to the next slide? So, this is our EBITDA reconciliation, if you start with 
the reconciliation due to the volume growth of 17%, our EBITDA should have gone up by Rs. 650 
million, we have seen an impact of increase in material costs throughout the year that started 
progressively going up in the second quarter of the year and that's how you see an impact of Rs. 170 
million inspite of increase in volume, the resulting contribution had its impact on the EBITDA. We 
benefited due to foreign exchange compared to our results of the previous year, both in terms of INR 
dollar and INR euro has remained positive, that has given us a positive benefit on the bottom line and 
we've had increase in other expenses, as we mentioned, which comprises of increase in employee 
cost and increase in other fixed expenses in relation to our overall business. So, this has landed up in 
our overall EBITDA of Rs. 1850 million. This is the overall performance, P&L for the quarter, starting 
previous year and sequentially the previous quarter. If you largely see, the EBITDA is actually grown 
from 14.9% to 16.3%. We also had called out earlier during the quarter that we will be receiving a 
tariff refund from the US and that's something which is baked in here and overall, after considering 
the impact of that, we landed up with an overall PBT of 15%. Our net cash continues to grow. This 
quarter we have added around, close to Rs. 200 million of cash, Of course, this is a quarter in which 
we also paid out dividend, so, excluding the impact of dividend, that's seen on the right-hand side, the 
cash profit from April to September has been healthy, Rs. 337 crores and we've invested in net working 

capital, which is largely an account of inventory. We continue to pay taxes largely in India and our 
Capex program is in line with our MK2 program that is ongoing. So, with that, we'd like to end the 
presentation and then open the forum for Q&As. 
 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Sir, for your comments. I'll wait for a minute, for the question, question queue to assemble 
and then probably open the first line. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
And is Dr. Jay able to join or Anvar able to join? Can you check? 
 
Moderator: 
Just a second, Sir. Sir, Anvar is there and I don’t see Jay sir yet. 
 
Should I take in the first question? 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Sure. 
 
Moderator:  
Participant, please restrict yourself to two questions each, probably, if we have time later on, we will 
probably allow more questions. 
 
Sir, first question is from the line of Mr. Harshit Patel. Harshit, you may unmute yourself and go ahead 
with the question 
 
Harshit Patel: 
Hi, am I audible? 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Yes, Harshit, you are audible. 
 
Harshit Patel: 
Thank you, so last quarter, Jairam Sir had mentioned that you had assumed about 9% rise in material 
costs for FY27 and said that the price corrections would mainly show up towards the end of Q2 and 
the effect will be fully visible in the third quarter.  
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Harshit, you can continue with the question.  
 
Moderator: 
Harshit, you may continue with the question. Jairam sir also seems to have joined the call. 
 
Harshit Patel:   
Ok, perfect. Hi Sir. 

Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Hi, I apologize to everyone. I apologize to everyone for this technical issue. I'm a bit in a remote area 
and this is having some issues, sorry, I apologize. 
 
Harshit Patel:   
No problem, sir. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Go on, Harshit. 
 
Harshit Patel:   
Sir, last quarter, you had mentioned that you had assumed a roughly 9% rise in the material cost for 
the full FY27 and you had also said that the price corrections would mainly show up towards the end 
of Q2 and the effect will be more pronounced in the third quarter. Now we have seen that the gross 
margins have recovered about 60 basis point on QoQ basis to about our usual range. Would you be 
able to share how much of the planned price corrections are now in the market and where do you see 
the gross margin settling in the second half of the year? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Harshit, it's a fair question. I'm unable to give you a very clear answer, but I will attempt to give you 
an answer, which as we are looking now. So even as we speak, our metal commodity prices are 
continuing to increase. So, what we are doing is continuing to react to it, but unlike, you know, a 
consumer product where we can increase prices immediately and see the results very quickly, we are 
not in that situation. So, the price increases that we experienced up to, let's say July / August, when 
we had our first quarter sales calls, we had pushed that all in, but subsequently there have been 
further increases and that we have also made some corrections in those crises and we expect to see 
some of that coming in the third quarter. So, whatever we had an issue in the first quarter, what was 
visible we've been able to absorb and correct in the second quarter. But what happened in the second 
quarter, we have not been able to reflect in our second quarter. Does it, does it answer your question? 
 
Harshit Patel:  
Yes sir, that does, thank you. Thank you for that. 
 
Secondly, you had guided Europe to be profitable, marginally profitable in FY 27 and with break even 
as the worst possible case and also expected Australia to be back on track by third quarter or fourth 
quarter after the reorganization that we are doing right now. So where do these two things stand 
currently, based on the update that you had previously given? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, I continue to maintain that we are on track for whatever we had guided. As far as Europe is 
concerned, we will be marginally profitable. Break-even is the worst case, but we are quite confident 
that we will have some profit. That is provided there are no further geopolitical conflicts and 
disruptions that happen, because Europe seems to be the most affected when these conflicts come in 
and the same thing with Australia, we have done our reorganization, we are putting it back in place. 

So, we're quite confident that it's on track third quarter and fourth quarter we will see some good 
return. 
 
Harshit Patel: 
Perfect. Just a small bookkeeping question, I think, going by your press releases, you have announced 
a tariff refund of about Rs. 40 crores received in August as well as September. So how does the 
accounting of this refund where? where we have accounted for them in our P&L? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, I will let Indranil to give you the details of that. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Yeah, so at a directional level around 50 to 60% of this has been recognized in the current quarter and 
balance is still lying in inventory because as we sell the inventory is when we will realize them in 
quarter three and quarter four. 
 
Harshit Patel: 
Understood. So, this are directly booked in our revenue, this 50 to 60% of Rs. 40 crores that you have 
mentioned. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
They are booked as a credit into material cost. 
 
Harshit Patel: 
Understood. Perfect. Thank you very much for answering my questions. I will come back. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
So, to that extent you should normalize the material cost reduction from quarter one to quarter two. 
 
Harshit Patel:  
Understood. This is well understood, thank you very much. 
 
Moderator:  
Thank you Harshit. Next question, we'll take it from the line of Ankur. Ankur, you may unmute yourself 
and go ahead with your question. 
 
Ankur Periwal: 
Hi Dr, Jay, am I audible? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Yeah, Ankur, you are. 
 
Ankur Periwal: 
Thank you, thank you sir, thanks for the opportunity. My first question on the revenue growth side. 
So, India saw a very good sort of you know jump in this quarter continuing the trend what we saw in 

Q1. If you could highlight this is largely the benefits of Demand=Match there or and you know 
parallelly how is the feedback on a new launch on your side? What's the feedback there on the 
ground? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So multiple things Ankur, the growth has been one, definitely Demand=Match increased our 
conversion ratios, when we are in front of the customer, but so that's definitely contributed. The 
second is you know we have, we started a go to market project about two and a half years ago and it 
got fully crystallized only in this financial year and the effect of that is also more, our inquiry levels 
have gone up by virtue of being able to cover a lot more customers as part of that go to market 
process. And the third of course is the buoyancy in the Indian economy itself. The demand patterns 
have gone up. It has been very positive. So, I'm not able to split this into these three buckets, but all 
these, two of them are internal to the company and one is external to the Company and all have 
contributed. 
 
Ankur Periwal: 
Sure, Sir, thanks for that. Secondly on you know the global markets, how is the outlook there especially 
in Europe given you know our expansion there in Germany, will we be using the same distribution 
network or there will be further investments in creating that network which may result in some 
overheads increase? And parallelly your thoughts on the gross margin or the EBITDA margins in the 
global markets, Europe and US specifically? Thanks. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Ok, So, Europe is not going to be a short-term play, it's going to be a medium-term play. The economies 
are in pretty bad shape. All the countries are in pretty bad shape. Even though we are entering 
Germany, German economy is also in very in, in not so good condition. But the fact that we are zero 
in Germany is going to give us some sort of a growth, overall in that context, in terms of increasing 
cost, we are not increasing cost. Whatever cost is required to do business in Germany is already baked 
in and getting reflected in our current P&L. We don't see any great increase in cost if at all, there will 
be certain revenue producing roles that will get added, but not anything of significance. In terms of 
EBITDA margins, in the US, it's very healthy, especially for our industrials. I don't want to talk about 
EBITDA broken up into our four business verticals that are there. But if I focus on industrials, which is 
really what the core business of Elgi is, it is a very positive, very strong EBITDA that we have. And we 
expect that to continue to grow both in the US and in Europe, because increasingly we are getting 
more and more of our revenue from aftermarket, which is more profitable. And as we get more 
machines installed in the field, the aftermarket becomes more robust for us. So, I think overall, there 
is a positive outlook for EBITDA. But having said that, the commodity price challenges continue to 
remain. West Asia conflict cost, I mean the conflict is causing it escalation and cost is something that 
we have not baked in, but we have stepped back and taken a larger view of it and we have, we are 
creating some initiatives within the Company to really take cost out both in our material and variable 
cost, but also on some of our fixed cost to be able to protect against any further unforeseen cost, cost 
escalation. 
 
Excuse me. Yeah. 
 

Ankur Periwal: 
Sure, Sir. Just as a follow up to that, so if I do a consol minus standalone, you know P&L working, the 
subsidiary markup, you know EBITDA margin has improved significantly this quarter. So, is this a 
benefit of you know, those initiatives that you highlighted that we have taken or those are yet to play 
out? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
No, those are yet to play out. Definitely yet to play out. The percentage increase is a more a volume 
driven contribution, Ankur. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Sorry, this also has a bit of tariff refund baked in the subsidies. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Yeah, sure. 
 
Ankur Periwal: 
Indranil, if you can just highlight what could be the tariff allocatable to the, let's say the international 
market or I mean 40% number  
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
I mentioned the number, 50 to 60% directionally. 
 
Ankur Periwal: 
OK, sure. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Not like to call out the overall number, but 50 to 60%. 
 
Ankur Periwal: 
Sure, that's helpful. I'll get back into the queue, thank you. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Thanks. 
 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Ankur. The next question we'll take is from the line of Paresh Chaudhari. Paresh, you may 
unmute yourself and go ahead with your question. 
 
Paresh Chaudhari: 
First of all, congratulations on a good set of numbers, Sir.  
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Thank you. 
 

Paresh Chaudhari: 
My first question is with regards to oil free segment. We mentioned in our annual report that we had 
a strong order book for FY 27. So, given that we are in the middle of the year, how do you see the 
incremental demand and are there any particular end segments which you would like to call out, which 
are driving the demand? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, oil free is primarily driven by pharma, food processing, very specialized industry verticals that have 
a demand for oil free machines. All of these verticals are doing well in terms of their investment plans. 
So, we expect that there will be a continuing support for our oil free machine as in addition to that, 
we have carved out oil free products as a separate vertical in our sales organization to bring more 
focus to it. So, we expect that that will continue to push and provide that kind of attention to that 
product. 
 
Paresh Chaudhari: 
Yes sir, and so, my second question would be on our MK2 campus. So, first part of it would be the 
updates on the progress and the second part would be, Sir, what would be the top line benefits? Like 
do we intend to do more localization post campus consolidation? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, Paresh, the purpose of MK2 is twofold. One was to move a city campus progressively to our main 
campus outside the city and we had earmarked about Rs. 600 crores over a period of four, five years. 
What we have done is the first phase is moved, created a facility for our global parts service, what we 
call as our global support centre, which is a fully automated parts warehouse that serves all our 
operations globally. So, that has gone on stream even as we speak and that was the first phase. The 
second part of phase one was to move our diesel machines, portable compressors from our city 
factory to that, for which the basic work has started. We have got all the approvals and that will be 
completed by the first quarter of 2028 calendar year, so, and then we will look at the rest of it being 
invested in. 
 
Paresh Chaudhari: 
Thank you so much, Sir. I'll call back in the queue. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
I apologise for my throat. 
 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Paresh for your question. Participants, if you have any other question, you may please 
assemble in the queue or you may drop it even then the chat box, we'll take it from there. So, the next 
question is from the line of Manish. Manish, you may please unmute yourself and go ahead with the 
question. 
 
Manish: 
Yeah, thank you so much sir. Sir, couple of questions. 
 

Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Hi Manish. 
 
Manish: 
Hello sir. Sir, Mr. Sen alluded in the opening remarks that in Europe, Italy has been facing challenges. 
So, probably what I see is, for last two years, Italy operation has been incurring minor losses. Earlier 
they were doing extremely well. So, was it also due to there was some change where we stopped 
exports to US and then it has taken much toll on it? Maybe you can clarify that number one and 
number two, we have purchased the land in Italy, so what is it pertaining to and if you can clarify that? 
That was first set of question and then US seems to be doing well and you did mention profits are 
growing. So how should we look at that, US has compounded more than 15% for last 6-7 years? So, 
we expect it to continue at that run rate and probably steep better margins because I think Elgi USA 
is profitable, but I'm not sure about Patton’s. So yeah, these were my first set of questions. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Yeah, so, what Indranil referred to Italy was for the industrial side and what you're referring to is a 
Rotair operation, right? The Rotair operations are the one that got challenged because of export to 
the US, yeah. And the tariff that got imposed on the products that were going out of Rotair to the US 
market. Now on the industrial side, Italy was never a problem, but the overall economies of various 
countries in Europe are under challenge and that's the reason why we are facing it. It's a trickle-down 
impact of the economies in impacting investment and investment onward affecting the procurement 
of compressors. So, that's why I said Europe is a medium-term thing in terms of waiting for the 
economies to improve, but having said that, we are working on specific initiative because our share of 
the market in most of these countries is so low that even if the industrial activity is weak, there is 
opportunity for us to grow, which is really what we are focusing on. 
Coming to the US, US has been a very strong story and yes, you're right, the positive aspects of our 
North America operations are our industrial business. Pattons is still a challenge, but it's slowly and 
slowly coming out of the woods. We are beginning to see service incomes improving. We are beginning 
to see equipment sales going up. So, we are quite confident that our distribution operations, it's both 
Pattons as well as Michigan Air doing well in the not-too-distant future, they will be in a very good 
situation. That's what our expectations are. 
 
Manish: 
Ok and on the profitability, Sir. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
on the profitability of Europe, we have done quite a bit of restructuring, we have taken a lot of cost 
out. So, like I said, we are looking to be profitable this year and as we grow our top line in Europe, our 
profitability will increase, our aftermarket will kick in. So, overall, I don't see any challenges to our

Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Thank you. 
 

Paresh Chaudhari: 
My first question is with regards to oil free segment. We mentioned in our annual report that we had 
a strong order book for FY 27. So, given that we are in the middle of the year, how do you see the 
incremental demand and are there any particular end segments which you would like to call out, which 
are driving the demand? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, oil free is primarily driven by pharma, food processing, very specialized industry verticals that have 
a demand for oil free machines. All of these verticals are doing well in terms of their investment plans. 
So, we expect that there will be a continuing support for our oil free machine as in addition to that, 
we have carved out oil free products as a separate vertical in our sales organization to bring more 
focus to it. So, we expect that that will continue to push and provide that kind of attention to that 
product. 
 
Paresh Chaudhari: 
Yes sir, and so, my second question would be on our MK2 campus. So, first part of it would be the 
updates on the progress and the second part would be, Sir, what would be the top line benefits? Like 
do we intend to do more localization post campus consolidation? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, Paresh, the purpose of MK2 is twofold. One was to move a city campus progressively to our main 
campus outside the city and we had earmarked about Rs. 600 crores over a period of four, five years. 
What we have done is the first phase is moved, created a facility for our global parts service, what we 
call as our global support centre, which is a fully automated parts warehouse that serves all our 
operations globally. So, that has gone on stream even as we speak and that was the first phase. The 
second part of phase one was to move our diesel machines, portable compressors from our city 
factory to that, for which the basic work has started. We have got all the approvals and that will be 
completed by the first quarter of 2028 calendar year, so, and then we will look at the rest of it being 
invested in. 
 
Paresh Chaudhari: 
Thank you so much, Sir. I'll call back in the queue. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
I apologise for my throat. 
 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Paresh for your question. Participants, if you have any other question, you may please 
assemble in the queue or you may drop it even then the chat box, we'll take it from there. So, the next 
question is from the line of Manish. Manish, you may please unmute yourself and go ahead with the 
question. 
 
Manish: 
Yeah, thank you so much sir. Sir, couple of questions. 
 

Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Hi Manish. 
 
Manish: 
Hello sir. Sir, Mr. Sen alluded in the opening remarks that in Europe, Italy has been facing challenges. 
So, probably what I see is, for last two years, Italy operation has been incurring minor losses. Earlier 
they were doing extremely well. So, was it also due to there was some change where we stopped 
exports to US and then it has taken much toll on it? Maybe you can clarify that number one and 
number two, we have purchased the land in Italy, so what is it pertaining to and if you can clarify that? 
That was first set of question and then US seems to be doing well and you did mention profits are 
growing. So how should we look at that, US has compounded more than 15% for last 6-7 years? So, 
we expect it to continue at that run rate and probably steep better margins because I think Elgi USA 
is profitable, but I'm not sure about Patton’s. So yeah, these were my first set of questions. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Yeah, so, what Indranil referred to Italy was for the industrial side and what you're referring to is a 
Rotair operation, right? The Rotair operations are the one that got challenged because of export to 
the US, yeah. And the tariff that got imposed on the products that were going out of Rotair to the US 
market. Now on the industrial side, Italy was never a problem, but the overall economies of various 
countries in Europe are under challenge and that's the reason why we are facing it. It's a trickle-down 
impact of the economies in impacting investment and investment onward affecting the procurement 
of compressors. So, that's why I said Europe is a medium-term thing in terms of waiting for the 
economies to improve, but having said that, we are working on specific initiative because our share of 
the market in most of these countries is so low that even if the industrial activity is weak, there is 
opportunity for us to grow, which is really what we are focusing on. 
Coming to the US, US has been a very strong story and yes, you're right, the positive aspects of our 
North America operations are our industrial business. Pattons is still a challenge, but it's slowly and 
slowly coming out of the woods. We are beginning to see service incomes improving. We are beginning 
to see equipment sales going up. So, we are quite confident that our distribution operations, it's both 
Pattons as well as Michigan Air doing well in the not-too-distant future, they will be in a very good 
situation. That's what our expectations are. 
 
Manish: 
Ok and on the profitability, Sir. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
on the profitability of Europe, we have done quite a bit of restructuring, we have taken a lot of cost 
out. So, like I said, we are looking to be profitable this year and as we grow our top line in Europe, our 
profitability will increase, our aftermarket will kick in. So, overall, I don't see any challenges to our 
profitability in the current cost structures that we have. The same thing I would say in North America 
we don't see any margin driven either profit increase or compression, but we see a volume driven 
profit escalation that we expect in the future. 
 
 
 

Manish: 
Ok Sir and so there was a couple of clarification. One on the standalone in the quarter 2, we see that 
standalone other income is Rs. 47 crores, was it Rs. 24 crores, while in consolidated it is lower at Rs. 
21 crores, was it Rs. 51 crores. So, there are two things. One is last year, what I see in annual report 
there was a gain on sale of property of Rs. 39 crores. So, was it there in quarter 2 of last year and that 
is why the other income was there entirely in quarter 2? And then second question, why the other 
income is high in standalone and lower in consolidated? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
I will let Indranil answer that. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
Yeah, so, your understanding on the first part on last year is correct. We had sale of property last year. 
This year on standalone we have dividend from our subsidiary which gets eliminated in consolidated. 
That's why you see it in other income in standalone. 
 
Manish: 
Ok, ok and also on, on maybe I had sent some queries in from the annual report. This was pertaining 
to some interval intercompany charges, like royalties charged to subsidiaries and market development 
fees paid to some subsidies. So, maybe if you can reply to that query or if you want to take it in the 
call, I'm ok with either of that. 
 
Management (Mr. Indranil Sen): 
We can respond to that separately, but for the benefit of everyone, these charges are in line with our 
overall transfer pricing arrangements, vetted with tax laws of both jurisdictions. So, but I will respond 
to you separately. 
 
Manish: 
Ok and sir, last question on the Vayu launch in India. So, this is the one we were targeting for the 
smaller compressors and probably competing with Chinese imports, is this one we were targeting if 
you and how do we see the progress post launch, Sir? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, you're right, this is Vayu, is our brand to take on the low-cost compressors that have come in from 
China. We, as per our plan, we were to do close to 35% coverage of the geography by September 
which we have accomplished. Our plan is to do the complete coverage of the country by end of January 
and February or January / February time frame and we are on track to make that happen. The initial 
launch has been outstanding, the order book and the sale has been far higher than what we had 
anticipated. So, we are going in the right direction there. 
 
Manish: 
And how big is the market, Sir? 
 
 
 

Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, I don't know, I don't want to talk about the value, Manish, but in volume terms, it's about 25 to 
30% of the numbers in oil lubricated screw compressors. 
 
Manish: 
Ok, Sir, I have few more questions. I'll come back in the queue. Thank you, sir. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Yeah. 
 
Moderator: 
Participants, if you have any question, do keep raise hand option up or you may drop it in your chat 
box, and we'll take it up from there. Sir, we'll assemble for, we'll wait for a couple of minutes for the 
queue to assemble. 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
Ok, sure. 
 
Moderator: 
Sir, we have a follow up question from Ankur. Ankur, you may please unmute yourself and go ahead 
with your question. 
 
Ankur Periwal: 
Yeah, hi Sir, thanks for the opportunity. On the global markets, if I look at, you know, Q1 and even Q2 
numbers, others which I believe you know, includes Middle East here, the growth has been slightly 
softer versus you know what we had seen a much sharper ramp up in the earlier years. Is this largely 
because of the disruption here? And how do you look at, you know, the growth here within Middle 
East, which has grown well keeping the and any other global markets wherein we are looking to wrap 
up our operations? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, Ankur, if you at a very broad level, half of our revenue is outside India and if you look at that half, 
there are 4 geographies that are primarily or three geographies that are primarily driving that 50%. 
It's North America, Europe and Australia. Now if you look at these three geographies compared to the 
prior years, both Europe and Australia have been a little subdued. So that's one reason why you're 
seeing a certain sluggishness in the global market. Now if you go to the second-tier markets which are 
contributing to that 50%, you will see Brazil and you will see Middle East and Africa as two large 
contenders in the second year. Now, Brazil compared to last year, even though it's been, it's grown 
well, but compared to last year was a bit of a bonus here by virtue of all the elections and everything 
that has been, there has been a certain pause there that has been lower than what we had last year, 
better than planned, but lower than last year. The same thing if you come to Middle East, Africa has 
done very well. Certain parts of even Middle East have done well, but of course, the disruption and 
the war have definitely put a, you know, kind of a dampener on the thing. So, that's the reason. So, 
once these things are getting cleared, I think those markets will come back. 
 

Ankur Periwal: 
Sure, Sir, just a follow up, from a margin perspective, does these Tier 2 markets, you know, how do 
they stand versus let's say, US or a Europe? Europe are, you know, obviously we are not making as 
much money there, but let's say versus US, will they be largely in the similar ballpark range? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, at a gross margin, yeah, at a gross margin level, these countries are very similar to India, yeah. So 
that's, I don't want to get into very specific percentages, Ankur, but they are not, the price points in 
these markets are not as high as Europe and the US or Australia. 
 
Ankur Periwal:  
Yeah. Sure, sir. That's helpful. That's it from my side. Thank you. 
 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Ankur. Sir, next question we'll take is from the line of Vipul Kumar. Vipul, you may unmute 
yourself and go ahead with your question. 
 
Vipul Kumar Shah: 
Hi, thanks for the opportunity. Sir, my question is regarding margin for our Vayu range. Will it be 
converging to our traditional range or it will be higher or lower when it reaches certain scale? 
 
Management (Mr. Jairam Varadaraj): 
So, at a gross profit level, Vipul, it will be lower than the Elgi range, right? And that's to be expected. 
And we have kept that in mind while architecting the overall cost of the operation and that business 
as a vertical. Once we get the planned volume at an EBITDA level, we may not be as high as the 
standalone market, but definitely not very far away, especially when the aftermarket kicks in and the 
profitability of the aftermarket gets reflected in the business. So, I think it will not be as profitable as 
Elgi, but definitely not too far. The gap will not be very high. 
 
Vipul Kumar Shah: 
Ok, thank you, sir. 
 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Vipul, for your question. Participants, in case if you have any more questions, you may 
please use raise hand option or you may drop it into the chat box. Sir, I see no further questions being 
up there. So, I would open the line to Kamlesh Ji. Kamlesh Ji, you may please have the management 
speak about the closing remarks. 
 
Manish, you had some questions, yeah Manish, go ahead. Hi, Manish, you can unmute yourself and 
go ahead with the question. 
 
Manish: 
Yes, yes, I will go ahead. Just one question, sir, like in our go-to-market strategy, like what probably is 
reflecting in terms of expenses from what we see in annual report is the information system expense 
have in standalone doubled last year from Rs. 15 odd crores to Rs. 32 crores while in Consol also it has 

gone up to Rs. 42 crores. So, is it pertaining to only go to market strategy and or it is also to do with 
our IT system which we were probably implementing across and maybe having a global support service

These unaudited Financial results have been prepared in accordance with the Indian Accounting 
Standards prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act. 2013 read with relevant rules thereunder 
and in terms of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 
2015 and amendments thereto. 
4 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) vide G.S.R. No. 463 (E) dated 5th June 2015 as amended vide 
notification No. 1/2/ 2014-CL-V dated 23 February 2018 has exempted the Government companies 
engaged in defence production from the requirement of Segment Reporting 
5 
A Final dividend of ~ 0.40 per equity share for the financial year 2025-26 has been approved by the 
shareholders in the Annual General Meeting held on 28 September 2026. 
6 
As required under Regulation 33 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 
2015. Statutory Auditors have conducted a limited review of the above financial results for the quarter and 
period ended 30th September 2026 
7 
The above statement of financial results were reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the 
Board of Directors at their respective meetings held on 12 November 2026 
8 
Inventories include ~ 8327.07 lakhs (~ 8327.07 lakhs as of 31 March, 2026) which are non-moving for 
more than 5 years, procured by the company based on firm orders/LOI that were subsequently short 
closed by the customer which is backed by advances of ~ 36,234.42 lakhs received against these 
contracts. Although the company's accounting policy requires provision for redundancy to be made in 
respect of inventory not moved for more than 5 years. no provision for redundancy were considered 
necessary, in view of advances received against these firm orders/LOI being in excess of the assets 
acquired including these inventories and expenditures incurred thereon. 
9 
The Company has invested in Advanced Materials (Defence) Testing Foundation and Electronic Warfare 
(Defence) Testing Foundation which are not-for-profit companies registered under Section 8 of the 
Companies Act, 2013. Though these entities are associates, these entities are not considered for 
preparation of consolidated financial statements as the company does not have rights to variable returns 
from its involvement, other than equity investment 
10 
The previous period figures have been regrouped and reclassified wherever necessary to make them 
comparable with current period figures.

introduce IKS to you all. You know we are in the business of enabling providers to deliver better, 
safer care, predominantly impacting their cost of care, quality of care, and access to care

message is resonating dramatically. Certainly with the TruBridge install base, which is where

that's trending.

it's the people that make everything happen. Happy to note that we went in knowing that the 
people and culture dimension of TruBridge was a scenario where this was a company that was 
moving from a lifestyle company to truly an execution-oriented, intense organization. 
That transition was underway, but not complete. I think looking in, I think that has gotten 
validated, and I think there has also been some very interesting developments as we started 
integrating. Three of the top five executive leaders of TruBridge have now assumed executive 
leadership roles in the combined entity. Chris Fowler, who is one of their senior most executives, 
was CEO of TruBridge, has been there 25+ years.

TruBridge book that is now part of the acute business unit or the hospital business unit within 
IKS. He certainly believes in our vision. Many of you got a chance to meet with him when we 
did our last quarter's earnings release. 
He was in India, and so continues to be a key pillar for driving success in the joint platform. 
Amaris, who now is our Global CHRO, was the CHRO of TruBridge, and so that was a very 
important decision to make her Global CHRO of the combined entity. As you can imagine, that

gives the TruBridge people tremendous confidence on their representation and importance in the

David Harse, who used to run the TruBridge EHR business, which I think is the crown jewel of

the other key dimensions that we had as an assumption going in was that the EHR business is

into a context layer and make it an AI training moat. We had gone in with the assumption that

TruBridge financial health business appears to be stronger than we saw from the outside in. Last

that front. All in all, good learnings. Obviously, there's a lot of work to do as it relates to

If you really think about the logical architecture, not the physical architecture, but the logical

Nava Reports Highest Quarterly Revenue of ₹1,252 Crore,  
PAT Surges 127% YoY to ₹403 Crore; Renewable Energy Gains Traction 
 
Hyderabad, November 12, 2026: Nava Limited, the flagship company of the diversified multinational 
group spanning metals, energy, mining and commercial agriculture, announced its financial results for the 
second quarter ended September 30, 2026. 
The quarter Results are marked by highest-ever revenue of ₹1,252 crore, a growth of 30% year-on-year.  
Consolidated Profit After Tax (PAT) more than doubled at ₹403 crore, a growth of 127% year-on-year, with 
energy in the forefront supplemented by contributions from other businesses and positive deferred tax 
adjustment. 
The group’s foray into renewable energy gained traction with the graduated commissioning of 100 MW 
solar power project in Zambia ushering in a new phase of growth. 
The Avocado plantation project, the integrated Sugar project, mineral exploration for Manganese, Lithium 
etc., continue to make good strides during the quarter. 
The quarterly performance denotes sustainability with continued up-streaming of dividends and 
substantially improved financial position by recovery of arrears from the Utility in Zambia.

Business and Strategic Developments 
Energy: 
The energy segment delivered strong performance, supported by healthy PLFs in domestic operations. 
The commissioning of the 100 MW solar project in Zambia also marks a significant milestone, opening a 
promising new avenue for future growth and expansion in renewable energy. 
MEL's Phase II 300 MW power expansion continues to progress, with full commissioning targeted for July 
2027.  
Mining: 
In Côte d'Ivoire, exploration activities at Nava's 360 sq. km manganese concession continue to advance, 
with promising initial results. Exploration for lithium and other minerals in Zambia, is ongoing.  
Agribusiness:  
Nava Avocado Limited 
Nava's avocado is set for its first commercial harvest and sales from November 2026 to March 2027, 
utilizing the state-of-the-art packhouse and aided by GlobalG.A.P. and SMETA accreditations for 
international market access. 
Kawambwa Sugar Limited 
The integrated Sugar project implementation is on track for commercial operations from FY 2028-29, with 
progress in sugarcane cultivation, irrigation infrastructure and construction activities. Nava has continued 
to leverage its rich experience in this business to pursue best cost and project management practices in 
all facets. 
Commenting on the performance, Ashwin Devineni, Managing Director & CEO, Nava Limited, said: 
"Nava’s record quarterly and year-to-date operating revenue reflects the strength of our diversified 
businesses and the sustained performance of our core operations. The robust year-on-year growth in 
profitability, supported by our energy and mining businesses, reinforces the resilience of our operating 
model. 
Beyond financial performance, this quarter marks meaningful progress in our long-term growth strategy. 
The commissioning of our 100 MW solar project in Zambia represents an important milestone in our 
renewable energy journey, while the substantial recovery of outstanding receivables from ZESCO further 
strengthens our financial position. With our 300 MW power expansion progressing and our agribusiness 
ventures approaching key commercial milestones, we remain focused on disciplined execution, operational 
excellence and building a diversified portfolio that creates sustainable long-term value." 
About Nava Limited 
Founded in 1972, Nava Limited is a publicly listed multinational corporation with interests in metals, 
energy, mining, healthcare and commercial agriculture. The Company operates one of India's leading ferro 
alloys businesses and Zambia's largest mine-to-mouth power plant. Nava is expanding its global presence 
through investments in renewable energy and commercial agriculture, with a focus on building a 
diversified and resilient portfolio.

Independent Auditor’s Review Report on Consolidated Unaudited Quarterly Financial Results and Year 
to Date Results of the Company pursuant to the Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (as amended) 
 
To the Board of Directors of NAVA Limited 
 
1. We have reviewed the accompanying statement of unaudited consolidated financial results (‘the Statement’) 
of NAVA Limited (‘the Holding Company’) and its subsidiaries (the Holding Company and its subsidiaries 
together referred to as ‘the Group’) and its associate (refer Annexure 1 for the list of subsidiaries and 
associate included in the Statement) for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 and the consolidated year to 
date results for the period 1 April 2026 to 30 September 2026, being submitted by the Holding Company 
pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (as amended) (‘Listing Regulations’).  
  
2. This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Holding Company’s management and approved by the 
Holding Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and 
measurement principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standard 34, Interim Financial Reporting (‘Ind AS 
34’), prescribed under section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘the Act’), and other accounting principles 
generally accepted in India and is in compliance with the presentation and disclosure requirements of 
Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement 
based on our review. 
 
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE) 
2410, Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity, issued by 
the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. A review of interim financial information consists of making 
inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and 
other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with 
the Standards on Auditing specified under section 143(10) of the Act, and consequently, does not enable us 
to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit. 
Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion. 
 
We also performed procedures in accordance with the circular issued by the SEBI under Regulation 33 (8) 
of the Listing Regulations, to the extent applicable. 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
Chartered Accountants 
4. Based on our review conducted and procedures performed as stated in paragraph 3 above, nothing has 
come to our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying Statement, prepared in accordance 
with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in Ind AS 34, prescribed under section 133 of the 
Act, and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the information required 
to be disclosed in accordance with the requirements of Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations, including 
the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement. 
5. We draw attention to the Note 5 to the accompanying Statement of the Holding Company, which 
describes the uncertainty related to the outcome of the lawsuit filed by and against a subsidiary 
Company, Brahmani Infratech Private Limited. Pending final outcome of the aforesaid matter, which is 
presently unascertainable, the Holding Company has considered the claims filed, as described in the 
said note, as contingent liability/contingent assets as at quarter end 30 September 2026 and accordingly, 
in view of the management, no adjustment is required to the accompany Statement in respect of this 
matter. Our conclusion is not modified in respect of this matter. 
 
6. The Statement includes the interim financial information of seven subsidiaries, which have not been 
reviewed/audited by their auditors, whose interim financial information reflects total assets of ₹3,204.32 lakhs 
as at 30 September 2026, and total revenues of ₹24.28 lakhs and ₹222.58 lakhs, net loss after tax of 
₹(279.77) lakhs and ₹(729.25) lakhs, total comprehensive loss of ₹(643.82) lakhs and ₹(914.83) lakhs. for 
the quarter and year-to-date period ended 30 September 2026 respectively, net cash outflows of ₹(1,041.77) 
lakhs for the period ended 30 September 2026 as considered in the Statement. According to the information

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Ratnamani Metals & Tubes Limited Q2 
FY27 Earnings Conference Call hosted by Monarch Networth Capital. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference 
call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note 
that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Sahil Sanghvi from Monarch Networth Capital. Thank 
you, and over to you, sir. 
Sahil Sanghvi: 
Yeah, thank you, Yousuf. Good evening to everyone. On behalf of Monarch Networth Capital, 
we welcome you all to the 2Q FY27 earnings conference call of Ratnamani Metals & Tubes. 
We are delighted to host the management of Ratnamani, and from their side, we have Mr. 
Manoj Sanghvi, the Chief Executive Officer, and Mr. Vimal Katta, the Chief Financial Officer. 
 
Without taking much time, I'll hand over the call to Mr. Manoj Sanghvi for the opening 
remarks. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Manoj Sanghvi: 
Yeah, thank you, Sahil. Good evening, everyone. I warmly welcome you all and thank you for 
joining us for our performance update for the quarter and half year ended 30th September. For 
Q2 FY27, consolidated revenue from operations grew by 13% to INR1,348 crores compared to 
INR1,192 crores in the corresponding quarter last year. 
 
Consolidated EBITDA stood at INR220 crores with a margin of 16.3%. PBT was INR174 
crores, and PAT was INR133 crores. At the standalone level, revenue from operations grew by 
18% to INR1,104 crores. EBITDA stood at INR139 crores with a margin of 12.6%, while PBT 
and PAT were INR106 crores and INR80 crores respectively. 
 
On the profitability front, we have been able to maintain our gross margin, and overall cost 
structure has remained largely stable. The key exception has been freight and forwarding 
expenses, which have increased significantly due to the prevailing geopolitical uncertainties 
and their impact on global logistics. 
 
This increase has put pressure on our overall profitability. On the business front, we have 
witnessed an improvement in overall carbon steel division sales volume. Our standalone 
business continues to remain debt-free, and the order book has increased to over INR2,600 
crores, around 30% higher than the previous quarter. 
 
During the quarter, we have made good progress in specialized product segments. In the 
fertilizer sector, we have received approval to supply stainless steel seamless U-tubes for 
carbamate condensers from a leading global technology licensor and engineering company. In 
the nuclear and aerospace segments, we've secured several important orders and development 
opportunities. 
 
This includes order for HP heater cold finished tubes and hairpin heat exchanger seamless 
tubes for nuclear projects, along with a development order for steam generator tubes from 
Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited. We have also entered into a global supply frame 

 
 
Ratnamani Metals & Tubes Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
Page 3 of 12 
 
agreement for aerospace tubes and successfully supplied a critical seamless tube in the size of 
138 by 1 mm. 
 
On the capacity front, Spiral Mill-3 to manufacture pipes up to 18 meters with an annual 
capacity of 100,000 tons has been commissioned. We have also commissioned our external 
3LPE coating plant with an annual capacity of 25 lakh square meters at Odisha. Further, 
Ratnamani's standalone credit rating has been upgraded to CRISIL AA+/Stable. 
 
Now, I would talk a little about subsidiary performance. Coming to Ravi Technoforge, 
quarterly revenue increased to INR99 crores from INR96 crores in the corresponding quarter 
last year. EBITDA was INR12 crores with a margin of 11.8%. 
 
At Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions, quarterly revenue increased to INR157 crores from 
INR110 crores. EBITDA stood at INR86 crores with a margin of 54.7%, while PAT was 
INR65 crores. RFSS has secured a new export order worth approximately INR2,700 crores, 
taking its order book to over INR3,000 crores. 
 
A part of its expansion project has been commissioned, and production of induction bends is 
expected to commence next quarter. Its credit rating has also been upgraded to CRISIL AA. 
Thank you.

number of types or tonnage or something?

It is a five-year frame agreement with some value which they have indicated. That value, of 
course, maybe year one can be X, year two will be 1.2X, 1.3X. Slow and steady, there will be 
an increase.

I see. All right. Okay. Great. Secondly, you said the broader volume growth this quarter was 
driven by carbon steel, then there was this freight increase. I am saying from a gross margin 
point of view, if you maintain this, then I am just trying to figure out if carbon steel was a 
higher proportion in overall, then why did it not have as much an impact on gross margins?

All right. Thank you.

Yeah.

eClerx announces acquisition of RegEdge  
NEW YORK, US and MUMBAI, INDIA – Nov 12, 2026 – eClerx Services Ltd. (NSE: ECLERX; BSE: 532927), 
a global leader in AI-powered analytics, digital operations, automation and business process 
management, today announced the acquisition of RegEdge. 
RegEdge is a boutique consulting firm that helps financial institutions strengthen compliance programs, 
transform regulatory operations, and manage risk across the full trade lifecycle. With this acquisition, 
eClerx will further deepen its risk and regulatory capabilities, bringing together AI, technology and global 
delivery expertise to help clients navigate complex regulatory requirements more effectively. 
Kapil Jain, CEO & Managing Director, eClerx, said, “Strategic acquisitions are an important part of how 
we expand our capabilities, deepen our domain expertise, and pursue new growth opportunities. We are 
pleased to welcome the RegEdge team to eClerx, and look forward to creating greater value for our clients.” 
Harshad Pitkar, Founder and CEO, RegEdge, said, “RegEdge was founded on the belief that navigating 
regulatory complexity requires more than advisory expertise; it calls for a hands-on approach and practical 
solutions that work within the realities of financial institutions. Becoming part of eClerx enables us to take 
our expertise and proprietary solutions to a wider range of institutions, while helping clients further 
strengthen their compliance programs, improve operational effectiveness and respond with greater agility to 
an evolving regulatory environment.” 
About eClerx 
eClerx provides AI-powered analytics, digital operations services, automation, and business process management 
to help clients unlock growth and drive business outcomes. eClerx partners with Fortune 500 enterprises across 
financial services, telecom, media & entertainment, luxury, retail & fashion, and manufacturing. A publicly listed 
company, eClerx operates across 17 countries with over 23,300 employees, serving clients globally across the 
Americas, APAC, and EMEA. 
About RegEdge 
RegEdge is a risk and regulatory consulting firm founded in 2019 and headquartered in United States. The 
company helps financial institutions address regulatory, risk and compliance challenges across trade and 
transaction reporting, surveillance, financial crime compliance, regulatory change, and risk and controls.
