Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited Q2 
and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call hosted by Elara Securities (India) Private Limited. As 
a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity 
for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this 
conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. 
Please note that this call is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Nemish Sundar from Elara Capital. Thank you, and over 
to you, sir. 
Nemish Sundar: 
Thank you. On behalf of Elara Capital, we welcome you all to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call of Schneider Electric Infrastructure. We would welcome the management 
represented by Mr. Udai Singh, MD and CEO, Mr. Omkar Prasad, CFO, and Mr. Mohit Agarwal, 
Head of Investor Relations. 
We will now have the opening remarks from the management, post which we will have a 
question-and-answer session. Thank you. And over to you, sir. 
Udai Singh: 
Thank you so very much, and good afternoon to all of you, and thank you so much for joining. 
I am sure you would have got the presentation which we had uploaded today morning, and I 
would like to take you along those slides which we shared in the morning. And if I may request 
to go to Slide number 2, where we have shown you trophies which we are very proud of to share 
what your company has been doing and the way the company has been getting recognized in the 
quarter which went by. 
Just to tell you about what these awards have been, the extreme left which you see is the Golden 
Peacock Award, and I am sure you are aware about the Golden Peacock, which is the Institute 
of Directors constituted in 1991, supposed to be one of the very revered set of people who 
recognize corporations. There, we won an award for excellence in corporate governance, and 
this is something which really speaks about what your company has been doing in this area. 
Second award is equally important, where we got awarded and recognized by Indian Chamber 
of Commerce for excellence in sustainability manufacturing. Now, these two awards really is a 
true testimonial of how your company has been performing in these areas, and which therefore 
has also resulted, and I would like to speak to you about the third image which you see on the 
extreme right, is the CRISIL rating on ESG. We have done wonderfully well here. We actually 
have got reassessed by CRISIL on ESG, and we emerged as a strong player in this area as well. 
I would also like to take you to the subsequent page, which again speaks about how we have 
been getting recognized in the industry. If you look at, there are two pictures which you see. It 
is a summit held at Delhi, Bharat Electricity Summit, where we were awarded by two prestigious 
awards in the POWERGEN India & Indian Utility Week, which was held in last quarter. 

 
 
Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 17 
 
Public 
If you see, one award was Digital Transformation Partner in the area of distribution, wherein 
essentially what we have been trying to do is, in West India, we are trying to really modernize 
the grids with one of the best solutions which we have for better resilience, better transparency, 
and better control of the grid. 
On the right, which is the second recognition, is on the Energy Technology Partner of the Year. 
This is one mega job which we are executing in Gujarat for one of the semiconductor setups. I 
would now take you to the next slide, if I may request you to page four, which tells you as to 
how your company has been seeing the India story, which is panning in front of us, where we 
really see that there is sustained demand despite few headwinds which we have been witnessing. 
Overall, we have been seeing that this actually has been. The panorama in front of us has been 
good. Few macro snapshots, if you look at the slide at the top left, are primarily which are very 
supportive, is the GDP, which, I'm sure you are aware, we were at 7.8 the quarter which went 
by. The expected projection is anywhere between 6.5 and seven, which tells us that the capex 
infusion will keep on happening, and which is something which is a positive side for the 
company. 
At the same time, we have been also seeing in terms of the private capex, which stands at about 
INR1 trillion. The good news is that major contributor, which is roughly three-fourth of this, is 
in manufacturing area and electricity, where we come as a major player. Of course, the demand 
of electricity, if you remember in 2014, it was about 950 kilowatt hour. Now is touching close 
to about 1,460, and very soon is expected to go to about 2 megawatt hour per capita in 2030.  
Now what does it mean? This means that there will be more electricity demanded, there will be 
more electricity produced and distributed, which means that the company is on the right path. I 
would be wrong if I don't speak about few headwinds which the company has been seeing, and 
we are trying to see and trying to use all of our levers, whatever possible, how do we mitigate 
these headwinds which we have been seeing, where the rupee stands devaluated, copper, 
aluminum, steel have all gone double digit up, and also the repo rate has also sort of become 
slightly non-conducive. 
Nevertheless, what I would like you to focus on are four basic pillars, and these four basic pillars 
are the ones which are really setting up the mega trends in India. I would call them out as energy 
transition, AI and digitalization, urbanization, and Make in India. Why we have picked up this? 
We have picked up this because there is a capital which is getting infused, there are programs 
by Government of India which is actually being launched to support these initiatives. 
For example, if I take the energy transition, the non-fossil fuel, which actually stands at 300, is 
likely to cross 500 in coming years. I am sure you must have read an article in news day before 
where India wants to put up about 90 GWh of energy storage systems. There are schemes which 
are favoring this growth, like Pradhan Mantri Surya sarovar yojana, the RDSS, the newly 
launched Energy Stack, the Green Energy Corridors, and of course, the viability gap funding for 
energy storage systems, and interstate transmission waivers are these areas where we can really 
see this sector's boom. 

 
 
Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 17 
 
Public 
At the same time, if you look at AI and digitalization, we have the 1.5, 1.6 gigawatt of data 
centers, which is already up and working. Now we also see, and the sources tell us, that there 
are plans in the country to take it to about seven and eight in next three to four years, which is 
extremely important for us because a country like we are, we would consume this sort of data. 
These steps are also being supported and getting mandated by government by Acts like DPDP, 
like the policy which is still in draft stage, but is likely to get rolled out on the national data 
center. The tax incentives and holidays which are being given to people who are actually 
developing these data centers, and so on and so forth. 
Two another important pillars, as I said before, urbanization. We are talking about more and 
more people moving into towns and cities, which means that more and more ACs, more and 
more infrastructure, more and more hotels, residences, offices, more electricity. Of course, this 
is all being again supported, as I said before, by the government's initiative in terms of making 
smart cities, the infusion in areas of rail infrastructure, where we speak about Vande Bharat 
trains, which is likely to go up from 82 to 400. 
The EV penetration, which is likely to touch 30%, and the schemes like FAME I and FAME II, 
and also the PM E-DRIVE is all being supported. Last but not the least is the Make in India 
program of government. This is essentially is to drive self-resilience in our sense. This is also to 
boost export out of India. 
On a long term, we see that the manufacturing sector, which is today contributing to about 15%, 
is likely to go to about 25% in times to come, say, by next about four years. This is again 
important, and government is very much conscious about it, and certain programs which you 
must read on the slide are the ones which are going to drive this. We at the company of yours, 
what we have decided to do is adopt and stick to three strategic pillars. 
These three pillars are to be a technology leader. Be a technology leader and give those 
technologies to our customers and other stakeholders, which are really a true differentiator. 
Second, to have a very high level of customer differentiation. When I use this term customer 
differentiation, the idea is to keep and do things keeping customer at the core. 
Whatever is required, desired by customer at their sites, offices, is what we should be doing at 
our best. The last is being really cost competitive. We are the ones which are focusing and trying 
to do more and more things inside of India and making the supply chain pretty effective and 
staying cost competitive. 
With this, I would also be very happy to share a few wins which we have actually done in the 
quarter which went by. I would like to take your attention to page six, where we are talking about 
how we are working on the new waves of growth, the new emerging segments. New emerging 
segments, in our opinion and everybody opinion, is data centers, is semiconductors, and also 
continued pitch on the renewables. 

 
 
Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 17 
 
Public 
These three things which you see are essentially semiconductor, where we have supplied the 
entire powertrain, which includes the switchgear, which includes the transformer. The second 
one is data center is a unique thing which we have done, which is a skid-mounted station. Skid-
mounted stations are becoming the order of the day because it cuts the commissioning time. 
It is a plug-and-play solution, and that's something which we have uniquely done at this data 
center in West India. Renewables is where I would be not hesitant to say that we have been 
trying to do whatever we could at the distribution, including the inverter duty transformers, and 
this is one of the case like that, where we have been supplying this in the plant run by 
government. 
I would also take you to the next page, which is page seven, where, if you recall what I said is, 
how do we leverage the Make in India program of government? This is something which you 
do, is where we are seeing and reaching out to these manufacturing setups and plants with the 
products which we are making all by ourselves in India. 
Few things which I will mention, and if you would notice that this all across, this really 
transverse. We have been seeing and doing and reaching out to people in metal space, in the 
material, which is nothing but people who are making glass, in automotives, in defense, and also 
in the batteries. 
If you look at what we have been also trying to do is trying to give which way with which we 
can create value, whether it's AIS panels and metals in a plant in north, whether it's an E-house, 
which is nothing but the E-building, where we have actually been doing this in a setup which 
makes glass in south. 
Whether there's a compact station which we have been supplying to West India, near Bombay, 
and of course, defense, which is to a company which is making and supplying equipment to 
Indian Army. The last being the EV battery manufacturer where we've been supplying all those 
solutions which we manufacture in India by ourselves and supply. 
Now, nevertheless, just to tell you the last, just to reinforce as to what we've been trying to do 
and trying to be present at all places, is how are we powering the upcoming urban infrastructure, 
and what is the help which we're trying to really modernize and transform this in the country? 
Three cases which we have mentioned, if you look, one is a thermal power plant, other one is a 
metro in Bombay, and the third one is what we are trying to do in terms of uplifting the water 
infrastructure in state of MP. 
Now, these were, again, you would notice that these are all across where in the thermal power 
plant, we have been supplying the panels, we are supplying the protection systems, including 
relays and other SCADAs. We have been talking about the similar thing where, as I said before, 
automation panels, the entire controls of mass rapid transport in Bombay. 
The highly technical breakers in this segment, which we are seeing on the extreme right in 
metals, in water. While I have shared this with lot of proud, we would also at the same breath, 

 
 
Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited

we would like to also speak about what we have been doing in terms of enhancing our brand and 
doing work in areas of CSR and sustainability. If you notice what we have been trying to do is 
trying to really drive and sensitize stakeholders in India with our thought leadership programs. 
If you see, we have been there where we should be there, whether it's Bharat Electricity, 
POWERGEN India, the Semicon Summit held in Yashobhoomi in Delhi, the CII 6th Power 
Conclave, and also engagements and interactions with the European Union Chambers. We have 
been also really trying to drive these thought leadership programs by multiple channels, by either 
releasing, going to the press and making something which is relevant for us and the country, or 
trying to see as to what we can do in terms of driving sustainability. 
Like, if you look at the picture which is at the center on the bottom row, is where we are trying 
to see as to how we have been trying to do and asking to carry out pilots by some DISCOMs of 
equipment which doesn't have SF6, which is an extremely green gas in terms of having very 
high potential of greenhouse emission. 
Then what can we do in terms of really modernizing and supporting and diversifying grids, 
because if we are reaching on July, I'm sure you are aware, on 16th of July, the country touched 
270 gigawatts of peak demand. How do the existing grids can be modernized is something which 
is an article which was given in the Business Standard. 
The idea of me sharing this at this point in time with all of you is that we are trying to be sharing 
the advancements because we are one of the most advanced technology partner of our customers, 
and to telling them as to what India needs. In which ways will it be needed? How will that be 
done, and what use will it bring to the customers and all stakeholders, the users, everyone? 
I would also like to share one more thing, and I would request you to go on page 11, where we 
launched one of the most advanced breakers made globally. This is the breaker which we are 
now started production in our Kolkata plant. 
We unveil this breaker in Kolkata, and you see some pictures where we had called our partners, 
stakeholders, some 150-odd people came in, and were part of this launch where we unveil this 
breaker. I would just, on a very summary note, would like to speak about what this breaker is all 
about. This is something which is on Page 12, and why I say that this is one of the most advanced 
globally ever produced is, number one, it is a fully digitalized and sensorized breaker. 
It has a life which is twice the industry available breakers. It is 2x more operations. Of course, 
because it is super sensorized, it has got 40% lesser maintenance cost. This is a breaker which is 
really a trendsetter, as I would say, in times to come. We are pretty confident that this breaker, 
which is being produced in your plant in Kolkata, will actually drive the trend. I come to the last 
slide of my presentation before I hand over to my colleague, Mr. Omkar, is to tell you about 
what we have been doing in areas of sustainability. 
If you look at, and I am talking about slide 13, where you see that we are already 100% our 
energy sourced by renewables in the sites. We unfortunately had one accident, minor accident 

 
 
Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026

Public 
in last month. The gender diversity is something which we have been focusing, because it is 
important, because it is critical for organizational development, and we have moved the needle 
to close to 20%. 
At the same time, I am very happy and proud to share that we have been trying to work along in 
state of Gujarat in developing the skill. Just to tell you, in last two years, we have actually trained 
close to 1,900 youth, which are trained through our 16 skill centers. We have also been trying to 
help the community centers, the CSCs, the PHCs, and Anganwadis, and we have actually then 
close to about 320,000 people have been benefited for the programs which we have done. 
These numbers which you see is last two and three years number. Of course, as I said before, we 
have actually been awarded and getting recognized in the forums and platforms which are 
relevant and pertinent for us in the country. With this, I thank you so very much for patiently 
hearing, and I would request my colleague, Omkar, to take you through the financial 
performance of the quarter and the half year which went by. Over to you, Omkar. 
Omkar Prasad: 
Thank you, Udai. Thank you very much. And good afternoon, everyone. I just give the financial 
update. I will start with highlights in there in the Page number 15. We will start with the order 
for H1. If you look at the solid growth in terms of 25%, because you must have seen Q1, we 
were trailing in the orders, and in Q2, we were able to pick up the order, which is like-to-like 
comparison is more than 50% plus. 
So, we have closed the orders in this quarter is INR1,265, and the next one become INR2,180, 
which is actually the good growth. In this, in solid growth, in effect, the contribution is coming, 
as Udai highlighted, is emerging segment, with the good contributions in this order backlog. 
Moving to the sales, as we discussed in the Q1 earning calls, that we had a lagging in the 
execution in the Q1 due to the dependency on the customer to be able to accelerate the sales in 
this quarter. And in this quarter, we able to achieve close to 20% growth Y-o-Y, touching around 
INR780 crores. And H1, we are close to 12.5%, which is INR1,400 crores. 
EBIT, again, I will say from sequential quarter, we have been able to improve. You must have 
seen the Q1, due to the negative operating leverage, there was a profit, was there only close to 
4% of the Q1. In Q2, able to do with 7.2%, and overall H1 is 6.2%. In all these, just to also 
confirm that in KMVC capacity expansion, which we got approved last week from the Board, 
we started partially the capitalizations. 
So, there is an increase in depreciation you will see in the next slide, number 14. Slide number 
16, where we have a Q2 performance. So, coming to the sales, we said that we grown 20%. 
Other income, when you look at, this is the income, we also include the income coming from 
the deposit what we have, the cash we have from the bank. Material cost to be a stress even in 
this quarter. 
While we on top up on all the measures what we are taking it, we try to keep it all the probable 
protections through our customer pricing. But this continued to be pressure. If you look at like-

to-like, even in preceding quarters, the cost of commodity like copper and transformer oil has 
increased. There was a slight relief on silver, which is very lesser consumption at our entity. 
Copper and the transformer oil continue to be increased even to sequential quarter and also like 
previous year, same quarter. Employee cost, while you look at the number in terms of 25% 
growth, let me tell you that in the Q1, which the way we explained, the increase is as per the 
inflations. Plus, what we have here, the headcount increase coming from the certain engineering 
cost, engineering people, whether they are working for us and also working for the group, and 
we are recharging this cost. 
That increase is giving, but the overall employee cost is increased only in proportion to the 
inflations what we have. In other expense, if I tell you the two things, one, while you see 22% 
increase, again, there is an increase in line with inflations. Plus, we have a certain cost which get

policy we do every quarter. So, that has increased in this Q2 results. Depreciation we talk about, 
so KMVC plant is the major one we started capitalizing it. Finance cost, again, this is just to 
confirm you, no incremental borrowing. The finance cost is increased just because the change 
in the rate what we are paying based on the RBI rate and the declare. 
Last year, there was a gain because of RBI modified rate what they charged, and this year there 
is an impact because 6.1% becomes 6.7% interest rate, what I understand. No exceptional item, 
tax expense, nothing to call out. Our ETR remains same. Overall, the profit we close, PAT, we 
close at INR30 crore compared to INR52 crores. Largely, the 43% drop you see, one obviously 
is coming from material cost, and all the other expenses, we expect that in H2 we will be able to 
leverage it through the operations and revenue for sure. 
Next quarter, when we say the Page number 17, this is the H1 results, where you see the sales 
grow 12.5%. Material cost, again, because Q1 you saw that it was under stress, Q2 continue to 
be stress. We try to take all the mitigating actions, how we can pass on this to customer pricing.

coming quarter for sure. 
Employee costs and other expenses and depreciation, nothing to specific call out, which I 
explained in Q2. More or less direction in the same regions we have, the cost has increased. We

or we can have some benefit from the operations. So that is all. 
And then, I hand over to operator to take your questions. Thank you.

Business Highlights for Q2FY27: 
Emerging Markets: 
• Caplin continues steady and consistent growth in Latin America across all geographies and segments.
• Central America update – Company has won tenders to the tune of $5.3 million to be supplied over the
next 3 Quarters. Around 70% of that is Oncology products, which move more through Tenders.
• Chile Update – Caplin continues to show strong growth in Chile in both Private and Tender market sales.
Company has won new tenders to the tune of $5 million to be supplied over the next 18 months. Company
has 6 products accepted by the 3 largest Pharmacy Chains in the country, for annual supplies.
• Mexico Update – Company has started commercial sales of Oncology products in Mexico recently.
Company has received 4 new product approvals this Quarter, with a further 13 products under active
review with COFEPRIS. The company is working on a pipeline of 110+ products to be filed in the next 18
months, in addition to the 33 approvals received. The company is in the midst of due diligence for a
potential acquisition of a Distribution company in Mexico.
• Oncology Unit update – Caplin One Labs oncology facility in Kakkalur, completes Exhibit Batches for 4
Injectables and OSD products. Additionally, submission batches for 16 products are planned in the next
12 months, for LatAm, US and EU markets. The company is in the midst of due diligence for around 12+
Oncology ANDAs that are approved or filed for approval, for potential acquisition. 
• API unit at Vizag for General Category products: Commercial license received for the unit, with first
commercial product supplied to parent company from this site. First DMFs expected to be filed from this
unit within FY27.
• Caplin’s Oncology API unit in Thervoy, TN, will be completed by CY27, with first DMFs filed from this plant
in the following year.
• Company’s new project involving OSD and Dermatology divisions in Pondy continues progress at full
swing. The facility is aimed at expansion of capacities by over 2X of the existing capacities. This facility is
aimed at meeting growing capacity demand in existing markets and also entry into Regulated markets for
these dosages.
• Amaris Clinical update – Multiple OSD and Softgel products pivotal BE studies completed recently, from
internal R&D pipeline. To cater to additional demands from internal pipeline products, Company starts
expansion activities at Amaris Clinical to increase capacity up to 120 Beds. Project is expected to be
completed by end of FY27.
US & Regulated Markets:
• Caplin Steriles Limited (CSL) continues steady growth across all parameters. Split between B2B and B2C
revenues currently at 60/40, as the company’s front end gains momentum.
• CSL has filed 120+ products (of which 75 are approved) in multiple Non-US markets, such as Canada, EU,
Australia, Mexico, Brazil, South Africa, Saudi, UAE etc. Plans in place to file 60+ products in these regions
in the next 18 months. Meaningful revenue is expected out of these markets in FY27 / FY28.
•
Company has launched 40 products in the US till date, with plans to launch 10 more products in FY28.
•
CSL completed Exhibit Batches for 2 Pre-Filled Syringe products from this site. Company has another 12 
Pre-Filled Syringe products under active development, which will be filed in FY28.

•
Company has completed movement from physical Logbooks to electronic Logbooks and move underway
towards electronic Batch Manufacturing and Packing Records within the next few months. Company has
already achieved total automation in Quality Control and Microbiology areas at the site.
•
To cater to the growing capacity needs at CSL, company’s COL-II facility construction will be completed
by Aug ’27 to house 5 Injectable, Ophthalmic and BFS lines. Provision to add 3 more lines also included in
the construction.

Q2 FY27 Press Release 
Business Highlights for Q2FY27: 
Emerging Markets: 
• Caplin continues steady and consistent growth in Latin America across all geographies and segments.
• Central America update – Company has won tenders to the tune of $5.3 million to be supplied over the
next 3 Quarters. Around 70% of that is Oncology products, which move more through Tenders.
• Chile Update – Caplin continues to show strong growth in Chile in both Private and Tender market sales.
Company has won new tenders to the tune of $5 million to be supplied over the next 18 months. Company
has 6 products accepted by the 3 largest Pharmacy Chains in the country, for annual supplies.
• Mexico Update – Company has started commercial sales of Oncology products in Mexico recently.
Company has received 4 new product approvals this Quarter, with a further 13 products under active
review with COFEPRIS. The company is working on a pipeline of 110+ products to be filed in the next 18
months, in addition to the 33 approvals received. The company is in the midst of due diligence for a
potential acquisition of a Distribution company in Mexico.
• Oncology Unit update – Caplin One Labs oncology facility in Kakkalur, completes Exhibit Batches for 4
Injectables and OSD products. Additionally, submission batches for 16 products are planned in the next
12 months, for LatAm, US and EU markets. The company is in the midst of due diligence for around 12+
Oncology ANDAs that are approved or filed for approval, for potential acquisition. 
• API unit at Vizag for General Category products: Commercial license received for the unit, with first
commercial product supplied to parent company from this site. First DMFs expected to be filed from this
unit within FY27.
• Caplin’s Oncology API unit in Thervoy, TN, will be completed by CY27, with first DMFs filed from this plant
in the following year.
• Company’s new project involving OSD and Dermatology divisions in Pondy continues progress at full
swing. The facility is aimed at expansion of capacities by over 2X of the existing capacities. This facility is
aimed at meeting growing capacity demand in existing markets and also entry into Regulated markets for
these dosages.
• Amaris Clinical update – Multiple OSD and Softgel products pivotal BE studies completed recently, from
internal R&D pipeline. To cater to additional demands from internal pipeline products, Company starts
expansion activities at Amaris Clinical to increase capacity up to 120 Beds. Project is expected to be
completed by end of FY27.
US & Regulated Markets:
• Caplin Steriles Limited (CSL) continues steady growth across all parameters. Split between B2B and B2C
revenues currently at 60/40, as the company’s front end gains momentum.
• CSL has filed 120+ products (of which 75 are approved) in multiple Non-US markets, such as Canada, EU,
Australia, Mexico, Brazil, South Africa, Saudi, UAE etc. Plans in place to file 60+ products in these regions
in the next 18 months. Meaningful revenue is expected out of these markets in FY27 / FY28.
•
Company has launched 40 products in the US till date, with plans to launch 10 more products in FY28.
•
CSL completed Exhibit Batches for 2 Pre-Filled Syringe products from this site. Company has another 12 
Pre-Filled Syringe products under active development, which will be filed in FY28.

Q2 FY27 Press Release 
•
Company has completed movement from physical Logbooks to electronic Logbooks and move underway
towards electronic Batch Manufacturing and Packing Records within the next few months. Company has
already achieved total automation in Quality Control and Microbiology areas at the site.
•
To cater to the growing capacity needs at CSL, company’s COL-II facility construction will be completed
by Aug ’27 to house 5 Injectable, Ophthalmic and BFS lines. Provision to add 3 more lines also included in
the construction.
•

- CSU

Q2 FY27 Press Release 
Business Highlights for Q2FY27: 
Emerging Markets: 
• Caplin continues steady and consistent growth in Latin America across all geographies and segments.
• Central America update – Company has won tenders to the tune of $5.3 million to be supplied over the
next 3 Quarters. Around 70% of that is Oncology products, which move more through Tenders.
• Chile Update – Caplin continues to show strong growth in Chile in both Private and Tender market sales.
Company has won new tenders to the tune of $5 million to be supplied over the next 18 months. Company
has 6 products accepted by the 3 largest Pharmacy Chains in the country, for annual supplies.
• Mexico Update – Company has started commercial sales of Oncology products in Mexico recently.
Company has received 4 new product approvals this Quarter, with a further 13 products under active
review with COFEPRIS. The company is working on a pipeline of 110+ products to be filed in the next 18
months, in addition to the 33 approvals received. The company is in the midst of due diligence for a
potential acquisition of a Distribution company in Mexico.
• Oncology Unit update – Caplin One Labs oncology facility in Kakkalur, completes Exhibit Batches for 4
Injectables and OSD products. Additionally, submission batches for 16 products are planned in the next
12 months, for LatAm, US and EU markets. The company is in the midst of due diligence for around 12+
Oncology ANDAs that are approved or filed for approval, for potential acquisition. 
• API unit at Vizag for General Category products: Commercial license received for the unit, with first
commercial product supplied to parent company from this site. First DMFs expected to be filed from this
unit within FY27.
• Caplin’s Oncology API unit in Thervoy, TN, will be completed by CY27, with first DMFs filed from this plant
in the following year.
• Company’s new project involving OSD and Dermatology divisions in Pondy continues progress at full
swing. The facility is aimed at expansion of capacities by over 2X of the existing capacities. This facility is
aimed at meeting growing capacity demand in existing markets and also entry into Regulated markets for
these dosages.
• Amaris Clinical update – Multiple OSD and Softgel products pivotal BE studies completed recently, from
internal R&D pipeline. To cater to additional demands from internal pipeline products, Company starts
expansion activities at Amaris Clinical to increase capacity up to 120 Beds. Project is expected to be
completed by end of FY27.
US & Regulated Markets:
• Caplin Steriles Limited (CSL) continues steady growth across all parameters. Split between B2B and B2C
revenues currently at 60/40, as the company’s front end gains momentum.
• CSL has filed 120+ products (of which 75 are approved) in multiple Non-US markets, such as Canada, EU,
Australia, Mexico, Brazil, South Africa, Saudi, UAE etc. Plans in place to file 60+ products in these regions
in the next 18 months. Meaningful revenue is expected out of these markets in FY27 / FY28.
•
Company has launched 40 products in the US till date, with plans to launch 10 more products in FY28.
•
CSL completed Exhibit Batches for 2 Pre-Filled Syringe products from this site. Company has another 12 
Pre-Filled Syringe products under active development, which will be filed in FY28.

Q2 FY27 Press Release 
•
Company has completed movement from physical Logbooks to electronic Logbooks and move underway
towards electronic Batch Manufacturing and Packing Records within the next few months. Company has
already achieved total automation in Quality Control and Microbiology areas at the site.
•
To cater to the growing capacity needs at CSL, company’s COL-II facility construction will be completed
by Aug ’27 to house 5 Injectable, Ophthalmic and BFS lines. Provision to add 3 more lines also included in
the construction.
•

Business Highlights for Q2FY27: 
Emerging Markets: 
• Caplin continues steady and consistent growth in Latin America across all geographies and segments.
• Central America update – Company has won tenders to the tune of $5.3 million to be supplied over the
next 3 Quarters. Around 70% of that is Oncology products, which move more through Tenders.
• Chile Update – Caplin continues to show strong growth in Chile in both Private and Tender market sales.
Company has won new tenders to the tune of $5 million to be supplied over the next 18 months. Company
has 6 products accepted by the 3 largest Pharmacy Chains in the country, for annual supplies.

Company has received 4 new product approvals this Quarter, with a further 13 products under active
review with COFEPRIS. The company is working on a pipeline of 110+ products to be filed in the next 18
months, in addition to the 33 approvals received. The company is in the midst of due diligence for a
potential acquisition of a Distribution company in Mexico.

Injectables and OSD products. Additionally, submission batches for 16 products are planned in the next
12 months, for LatAm, US and EU markets. The company is in the midst of due diligence for around 12+
Oncology ANDAs that are approved or filed for approval, for potential acquisition.

commercial product supplied to parent company from this site. First DMFs expected to be filed from this
unit within FY27.

in the following year.

swing. The facility is aimed at expansion of capacities by over 2X of the existing capacities. This facility is
aimed at meeting growing capacity demand in existing markets and also entry into Regulated markets for
these dosages.

internal R&D pipeline. To cater to additional demands from internal pipeline products, Company starts
expansion activities at Amaris Clinical to increase capacity up to 120 Beds. Project is expected to be
completed by end of FY27.

Australia, Mexico, Brazil, South Africa, Saudi, UAE etc. Plans in place to file 60+ products in these regions
in the next 18 months. Meaningful revenue is expected out of these markets in FY27 / FY28.

Company has launched 40 products in the US till date, with plans to launch 10 more products in FY28.

         Aadhar Housing Finance Limited 
 
November 05, 2026

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Aadhar Housing Q2 FY 2027 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by Nomura. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in listen-only 
mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation 
concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by 
pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being 
recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Shreya Shivani from Nomura. Thank you, and over to 
you, ma'am. 
Shreya Shivani: 
Thank you. Very good evening to all. Welcome to the second quarter FY 2027 earnings call of 
Aadhar Housing Limited. On behalf of Nomura, I would like to thank Aadhar management for 
giving us the opportunity to host this call. From management side, we have with us Mr. Rishi 
Anand, MD and CEO, Mr. Rajesh Viswanathan, CFO, and Mr. Sanjay Moolchandani, Head of 
FP&A and Investor Relations. I will now hand over the call to Rishi sir for his opening 
remarks, and then we can open the floor for Q&A. Over to you, sir. 
Rishi Anand: 
Great. Thank you so much, Shreya, and a very good evening to all of you. Thank you for 
joining us to discuss Aadhar Housing Finance's Q2 and H1 FY 2027 performance. Before 
discussing our performance on Q2, I would want to take a moment and express my deepest 
condolences on the sad demise of our esteemed Independent Director and Non-Executive 
Chairperson, Shri Raj Vikash Verma, on the 16th October. 
 
His invaluable contribution and guidance have been integral to Aadhar's journey, and his 
insights and wisdom will deeply be missed across the organization. May he rest in eternal 
peace. Following this unfortunate event, and in accordance with the applicable regulatory 
requirements, Shri Deo Shankar Tripathi, previously Executive Vice Chairman of the 
company, has been appointed as Interim Non-Executive Chairman. 
 
I would also like to welcome Shri Nikhil Goyal, Managing Director, Blackstone, who has 
joined our Board as an Additional Director with effect from 12th of August 2026. With his 
experience in private equity and investments, including banking and financial services, we 
believe he will bring in valuable investment perspective to the Board and further strengthen 
our focus on disciplined growth and long-term value creation. 
 
Now, coming to company's performance. During the first half of FY 2027, we continued to 
build on our execution momentum with a focus on disciplined growth, calibrated risk 
management, and improving productivity across our branch network. Our approach remains 
consistent, expanding access to affordable housing finance while maintaining asset quality, 
profitability, and sustainable returns. Our AUM as of 30th September 2026 stood at 
INR32,643 crores, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 18%. 
 
Disbursement for Q2 FY 2027 stood at INR2,577 crores, representing a Y-o-Y growth of 22%. 
As all of you would recall, from Q1 FY 2027, we transitioned into recognizing disbursement 
on cheque realization basis instead of cheque handover basis. Hence, on a like-to-like basis, 
disbursement growth in H1 FY 2027 on a Y-o-Y basis is 21% and AUM growth is 20%. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
         Aadhar Housing Finance Limited 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 14 
 
Looking ahead, we remain committed to our medium-term guidance of 18% to 20% 
disbursement growth and 20% AUM and PAT growth for the full year. 
 
Our portfolio continues to remain fully secured and retail in nature, with home loans 
accounting to 73%, non-home loans accounting to 27% of our AUM. Our average ticket size 
stood at INR11.3 lakh, with a loan-to-value ratio at comfortable 61%. The salaried segment 
contributed 55% of our AUM, reflecting a diversified nature of our portfolio. 
 
Balance transfer outflows during the quarter two FY 2027 was at 5.1%, which improved by 40 
basis points as compared to Q2 FY 2026, supported by focused retention efforts and AI-driven 
customer engagement. On asset quality, our portfolio continues to remain well secured, 
supported by disciplined underwriting and strong focus on collections. Collection efficiency 
for the said quarter stood at 99%, while gross NPA stood at 1.34% as of September 2026, 
which is an improvement of 8 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis. 
 
We also remain mindful of external factors as we grow business, including geopolitical 
developments and on the strengthening El Niño conditions that can impact the borrower's cash 
flow, particularly in the semi-urban markets. Our approach to assess the risk at the customer 
and the branch level and respond appropriately without resorting to broad-based tightening of 
underwriting norms. 
 
In addition, we closely monitor customers' overall repayment obligations and credit exposures 
to ensure that lending decisions remain aligned with their repayment capacity. This is 
particularly important as we deepen our presence in underserved market while safeguarding 
portfolio quality. Our AUM is well diversified across geographies, with no single state 
accounting for disproportionate large share of portfolio. 
 
During the quarter, we expanded our footprint to Jammu, an important territory for us, by 
adding one branch there, taking our network to 632 branches across now 23 states and 
covering over 555 districts as of September '26. We continue to follow a calibrated demand-
based expansion approach with a focus on markets where we see sustainable demand and 
potential to build a productive business over a period of time. We also remain focused on 
improving our productivity of our existing branches. 
 
Our objective is to ensure that newer branches reach expected productivity levels within 
planned timelines, while the established branches continue to improve sourcing productivity, 
customer retention, and operating efficiency. During the quarter in question, I am proud to say 
that our credit profile was further strengthened with India Ratings and ICRA upgrading our 
long-term rating to AA+ stable. 
 
Now all the three rating agencies, that is India Ratings, CARE, and ICRA, have rated the 
company AA+ on a stand-alone basis. These rating upgrades recognize our scale, strong 
capitalization, and diversified access to funding. They also strengthen our position to optimize 
borrowing costs over a period of time, subject to prevailing market conditions. On technology, 
we continue to leverage AI and data analytics to strengthen business operations across the 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
         Aadhar Housing Finance Limited 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 14 
 
lending cycle, including origination, underwriting, portfolio monitoring, collection, and 
customer retention. 
 
We are also building in-house platforms across document intelligence, voice intelligence, 
decisioning intelligence, enterprise access, and management intelligence to improve 
information processing, decision-making, and support for our teams. As we scale, technology 
will be key to improving operating efficiency, strengthening risk management, and enabling 
growth without compromising on execution quality or governance. 
 
Coming to the industry, demand for affordable housing finance continues to be supported by 
structural need for home ownership and expansion of formal credit to underserved markets. 
We continue to see opportunities in Tier 2, Tier 3, and beyond in the emerging markets, where 
first-time home buyers and customers with informal income profiles require a specialized 
approach in housing finance. At the same time, competition is increasing, making it important 
for lenders to develop new catchments while improving productivity and customer retention in 
the existing markets. 
 
In the recent revision in RBI monetary policy, with 25 basis points increase in repo rate to 
5.5% and a shift towards calibrated tightening, marks a change in the interest rate environment. 
While the impact on borrowing cost and housing affordability will depend on the extent and 
timing of transmission, we remain mindful of its implication both for customers and lenders. 
 
In this environment, our focus will be to continue on prudent underwriting, disciplined 
funding, and margin management while catering to underlying demand for the affordable 
housing finance and maintaining the quality of our portfolio. Our approach is to protect 
spreads rather than chase yields. 
 
We continue to focus on emerging markets, maintain discipline in our Loan Against Property 
portfolio, and improve productivity per branch and per employee to support sustainable 
growth. Overall, H1 FY 2027 has been a quarter of steady execution. 
 
We remain confident of delivering our medium-term guidance of 20% AUM and PAT growth, 
sustained profitability, and industry-leading asset quality while staying alert on the 
environment around us. We expect our disbursement momentum to continue and are confident 
of delivering a 20% plus disbursement growth in the second half of the year. Aadhar remains 
committed to its mission of enabling home ownership for low-income families while 
delivering consistent and sustainable returns for its stakeholders. 
 
With that, I would now hand over to Rajesh, our CFO, to take you through the financial 
performance in detail. 
Rajesh Viswanathan: 
Thanks, Rishi. Good evening, everyone. I would like to take you all through the financial 
performance of quarter two FY 2027 and H1 FY 2027. In quarter two, our disbursements have 
grown at 22% on a year-on-year basis. Adjusting for the impact of Q1 shifting to recognizing 
disbursement on a check clearance basis, the AUM at 30th September has grown by a healthy 
20% on a year-on-year basis. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
         Aadhar Housing Finance Limited 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 14 
 
 
Our overall borrowings on 30th September stood at INR20,400 crores compared to INR17,600 
crores on 30th September 2025. The borrowing mix as at end of 30th September 2026 is 53% 
from banks, NHB share is 22%, NCD share is 15%, ECB is 7%, and others are 3%. Our 
incremental borrowings for quarter two FY 2027 stood at INR1,550 crores, which has come in 
at a competitive 7.5%. There was no fresh drawdown from NHB during the quarter two. We 
have 43 borrowing relationships. 
 
The exit cost of funds as of September 30, 2026, stood at 7.7%. In terms of fixed and floating 
nature of our book, broadly 75% of our assets and liabilities are floating in nature. This gives 
us the ability to reprice our assets whenever the change in interest rate happens and we get 
passed on by banks or other floating -rate liabilities. 
 
Undrawn sanctions as of September 30, 2026, is INR1,466 crores. Further, in this week, we 
have received a fresh sanction of INR1,000 crores from National Housing Bank. Liquidity at 
the end of quarter two FY 2027 stood at INR2,040 crores. The portfolio yield exit is 13.4% as

Conference Call hosted by Nomura. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in listen-only 
mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation 
concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by

you, ma'am. 
Shreya Shivani: 
Thank you. Very good evening to all. Welcome to the second quarter FY 2027 earnings call of 
Aadhar Housing Limited. On behalf of Nomura, I would like to thank Aadhar management for 
giving us the opportunity to host this call. From management side, we have with us Mr. Rishi 
Anand, MD and CEO, Mr. Rajesh Viswanathan, CFO, and Mr. Sanjay Moolchandani, Head of 
FP&A and Investor Relations. I will now hand over the call to Rishi sir for his opening 
remarks, and then we can open the floor for Q&A. Over to you, sir. 
Rishi Anand: 
Great. Thank you so much, Shreya, and a very good evening to all of you. Thank you for 
joining us to discuss Aadhar Housing Finance's Q2 and H1 FY 2027 performance. Before 
discussing our performance on Q2, I would want to take a moment and express my deepest 
condolences on the sad demise of our esteemed Independent Director and Non-Executive 
Chairperson, Shri Raj Vikash Verma, on the 16th October. 
 
His invaluable contribution and guidance have been integral to Aadhar's journey, and his 
insights and wisdom will deeply be missed across the organization. May he rest in eternal 
peace. Following this unfortunate event, and in accordance with the applicable regulatory 
requirements, Shri Deo Shankar Tripathi, previously Executive Vice Chairman of the 
company, has been appointed as Interim Non-Executive Chairman. 
 
I would also like to welcome Shri Nikhil Goyal, Managing Director, Blackstone, who has 
joined our Board as an Additional Director with effect from 12th of August 2026. With his 
experience in private equity and investments, including banking and financial services, we 
believe he will bring in valuable investment perspective to the Board and further strengthen 
our focus on disciplined growth and long-term value creation. 
 
Now, coming to company's performance. During the first half of FY 2027, we continued to 
build on our execution momentum with a focus on disciplined growth, calibrated risk 
management, and improving productivity across our branch network. Our approach remains 
consistent, expanding access to affordable housing finance while maintaining asset quality, 
profitability, and sustainable returns. Our AUM as of 30th September 2026 stood at 
INR32,643 crores, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 18%. 
 
Disbursement for Q2 FY 2027 stood at INR2,577 crores, representing a Y-o-Y growth of 22%. 
As all of you would recall, from Q1 FY 2027, we transitioned into recognizing disbursement 
on cheque realization basis instead of cheque handover basis. Hence, on a like-to-like basis, 
disbursement growth in H1 FY 2027 on a Y-o-Y basis is 21% and AUM growth is 20%. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
         Aadhar Housing Finance Limited 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 14 
 
Looking ahead, we remain committed to our medium-term guidance of 18% to 20% 
disbursement growth and 20% AUM and PAT growth for the full year. 
 
Our portfolio continues to remain fully secured and retail in nature, with home loans 
accounting to 73%, non-home loans accounting to 27% of our AUM. Our average ticket size 
stood at INR11.3 lakh, with a loan-to-value ratio at comfortable 61%. The salaried segment 
contributed 55% of our AUM, reflecting a diversified nature of our portfolio. 
 
Balance transfer outflows during the quarter two FY 2027 was at 5.1%, which improved by 40 
basis points as compared to Q2 FY 2026, supported by focused retention efforts and AI-driven 
customer engagement. On asset quality, our portfolio continues to remain well secured, 
supported by disciplined underwriting and strong focus on collections. Collection efficiency 
for the said quarter stood at 99%, while gross NPA stood at 1.34% as of September 2026, 
which is an improvement of 8 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis. 
 
We also remain mindful of external factors as we grow business, including geopolitical 
developments and on the strengthening El Niño conditions that can impact the borrower's cash 
flow, particularly in the semi-urban markets. Our approach to assess the risk at the customer 
and the branch level and respond appropriately without resorting to broad-based tightening of 
underwriting norms. 
 
In addition, we closely monitor customers' overall repayment obligations and credit exposures 
to ensure that lending decisions remain aligned with their repayment capacity. This is

Uzbekistan Airways Selects RateGain to Strengthen Pricing Agility Across Its Expanding 
International Network 
 
India, 12 November 2026: RateGain Travel Technologies Limited (NSE: RATEGAIN, BSE: 543417) today 
announced that Uzbekistan Airways, the national carrier of Uzbekistan, has selected AirGain, RateGain’s 
competitive fare intelligence platform for airlines. The platform will provide the airline’s revenue 
management team with a clear, real-time view of competitor fares across its network. 
 
The partnership comes at a defining moment for the airline. Uzbekistan Airways carried 6.6 million 
passengers across more than 49,000 flights in 2025, as it continued to expand connectivity across Europe, 
Asia, the Middle East and North America. It operates a fleet of 47 aircraft and is the only Central Asian carrier 
flying direct to New York. The airline plans to at least double its fleet by 2030, backed by orders for 36 new 
Airbus and Boeing aircraft, amid growing domestic competition from new entrants. Following a competitive 
tender, the airline selected AirGain for RateGain’s deep aviation pricing expertise, comprehensive market 
coverage across airline websites, online travel agencies, metasearch and GDS, and proven track record with 
carriers across Central Asia. 
 
Under the partnership, RateGain will work closely with the Uzbekistan Airways revenue management team 
to monitor every route in its network and translate that data into everyday pricing decisions. AirGain’s AI-
powered tools, including Smart Search and AI Daily Digest, will help analysts identify competitor moves 
early, price new routes with confidence, and manage a larger network with less manual effort. As Tashkent 
grows into a hub connecting Europe and Asia, both companies see this as the beginning of a long-term 
relationship aligned with the airline’s growth ambitions. 
 
Speaking on the partnership, Vinay Varma, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Air, RateGain 
Travel Technologies Limited, said: “Central Asia is strengthening its role as a bridge between Europe, the 
Middle East and Asia, with Tashkent playing an important part. Uzbekistan Airways’ fleet investment and 
expanding partnerships reflect a clear ambition to grow internationally. AirGain gives revenue teams a 
clearer view of competitor pricing and market shifts, helping them make faster, more informed commercial 
decisions. We are proud to partner with Uzbekistan Airways as it expands its network and strengthens its 
international presence.” 
 
The agreement also reflects a wider shift in how airlines in fast-growing markets approach pricing. Carriers 
that once relied on periodic fare checks and spreadsheets now need a live view of the market to compete, 
and the gap between airlines with that visibility and those without it is widening quickly. RateGain believes 
the next phase of growth in Central Asia will be won by airlines that pair fleet investment with smarter 
commercial decisions, and AirGain is built to give them that edge. 
 
Shukhrat Yadgarov, Deputy Chairman of the Board for Commerce and Tourism, said: “Demand for air 
travel in Uzbekistan has never been stronger, and we are investing in our fleet and network to meet it. As we 
grow, every pricing decision matters more. AirGain gives our revenue team a clear, real-time view of the 
market across every route we fly, so we can respond to competitors quickly and price new routes with 
confidence. It is the kind of capability a growing national carrier needs.” 
 
The partnership strengthens RateGain’s presence in Central Asia, where multiple airlines in the region 
already use AirGain. The platform helps airlines price more intelligently, respond faster and capture more 
direct revenue. Carriers using AirGain have reported up to 80% faster access to actionable insights, a 1.5%

Uzbekistan Airways Selects RateGain to Strengthen Pricing Agility Across Its Expanding 
International Network 
 
India, 12 November 2026: RateGain Travel Technologies Limited (NSE: RATEGAIN, BSE: 543417) today 
announced that Uzbekistan Airways, the national carrier of Uzbekistan, has selected AirGain, RateGain’s 
competitive fare intelligence platform for airlines. The platform will provide the airline’s revenue 
management team with a clear, real-time view of competitor fares across its network. 
 
The partnership comes at a defining moment for the airline. Uzbekistan Airways carried 6.6 million 
passengers across more than 49,000 flights in 2025, as it continued to expand connectivity across Europe, 
Asia, the Middle East and North America. It operates a fleet of 47 aircraft and is the only Central Asian carrier 
flying direct to New York. The airline plans to at least double its fleet by 2030, backed by orders for 36 new 
Airbus and Boeing aircraft, amid growing domestic competition from new entrants. Following a competitive 
tender, the airline selected AirGain for RateGain’s deep aviation pricing expertise, comprehensive market 
coverage across airline websites, online travel agencies, metasearch and GDS, and proven track record with 
carriers across Central Asia. 
 
Under the partnership, RateGain will work closely with the Uzbekistan Airways revenue management team 
to monitor every route in its network and translate that data into everyday pricing decisions. AirGain’s AI-
powered tools, including Smart Search and AI Daily Digest, will help analysts identify competitor moves 
early, price new routes with confidence, and manage a larger network with less manual effort. As Tashkent 
grows into a hub connecting Europe and Asia, both companies see this as the beginning of a long-term 
relationship aligned with the airline’s growth ambitions. 
 
Speaking on the partnership, Vinay Varma, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Air, RateGain 
Travel Technologies Limited, said: “Central Asia is strengthening its role as a bridge between Europe, the 
Middle East and Asia, with Tashkent playing an important part. Uzbekistan Airways’ fleet investment and 
expanding partnerships reflect a clear ambition to grow internationally. AirGain gives revenue teams a 
clearer view of competitor pricing and market shifts, helping them make faster, more informed commercial 
decisions. We are proud to partner with Uzbekistan Airways as it expands its network and strengthens its 
international presence.” 
 
The agreement also reflects a wider shift in how airlines in fast-growing markets approach pricing. Carriers 
that once relied on periodic fare checks and spreadsheets now need a live view of the market to compete, 
and the gap between airlines with that visibility and those without it is widening quickly. RateGain believes 
the next phase of growth in Central Asia will be won by airlines that pair fleet investment with smarter 
commercial decisions, and AirGain is built to give them that edge. 
 
Shukhrat Yadgarov, Deputy Chairman of the Board for Commerce and Tourism, said: “Demand for air 
travel in Uzbekistan has never been stronger, and we are investing in our fleet and network to meet it. As we 
grow, every pricing decision matters more. AirGain gives our revenue team a clear, real-time view of the 
market across every route we fly, so we can respond to competitors quickly and price new routes with 
confidence. It is the kind of capability a growing national carrier needs.” 
 
The partnership strengthens RateGain’s presence in Central Asia, where multiple airlines in the region 
already use AirGain. The platform helps airlines price more intelligently, respond faster and capture more 
direct revenue. Carriers using AirGain have reported up to 80% faster access to actionable insights, a 1.5% 
increase in direct bookings, and integration time cut by 30 days.

Godrej Capital Secures ₹2,500 Crore from Temasek at a 
Valuation of up to ₹28,000 Crore 
 
Investment supports Godrej Capital's next phase of growth as it targets ₹1 lakh crore in AUM by 2031. 
 
Mumbai, November 12, 2026: Godrej Industries Group today announced that Temasek Holdings 
(Private) Limited via its affiliate Jongsong Investments Pte Ltd will invest ₹2,500 crore in Godrej 
Capital, its financial services arm, valuing the company at up to ₹28,000 crore. Post the transaction, 
the Group will retain approximately 80% ownership in the company.  
 
Founded in 2020, the company brings the Group’s 129-year legacy of trust and integrity to modern-
day financial solutions. Through its subsidiaries, Godrej Capital serves businesses and individuals 
across India with home loans, loans against property, working capital loans, construction finance, 
gold loans, supply chain finance and personal loans. The company has a presence in over 100 cities 
and Assets Under Management (AUM) of ₹35,000 crore as of October 31, 2026.  
 
Commenting on the announcement, Pirojsha Godrej, Chairperson, Godrej Industries Group, said,  
"We are delighted to welcome Temasek as a long-term investor in Godrej Capital. This investment is a 
testament to the exceptional business Manish and his team have built in a remarkably short period, and 
reflects confidence in the significant opportunity ahead. Financial services represents a major long-
term growth area of focus for our Group, and our ambition is to build Godrej Capital into a ₹1 lakh crore 
AUM franchise by 2031. We remain committed to achieving this through disciplined execution, strong 
governance and the values of trust and integrity that have guided the Group for over a century." 
 
Manish Shah, MD & CEO, Godrej Capital, further stated, “When we began this journey, our ambition 
was to build a diversified, technology-enabled financial services business with strong risk management 
and a customer-first approach. Today, with ₹35,000 crore in AUM, we have demonstrated the strength 
of our strategy and execution. This investment will help us accelerate growth, expand our reach across 
India, deepen our offerings for businesses, individuals and the communities we serve, and strengthen our 
technology-led capabilities. With Temasek now part of our story, we are excited about the lasting value 
we will create for all our stakeholders." 
 
The investment reinforces Godrej Industries Group's commitment to building and scaling high-
growth businesses, combining its longstanding values of trust and responsible stewardship with 
entrepreneurial ambition and disciplined execution. 
 
This transaction is subject to requisite regulatory approvals.  
 
 
 
 
About Godrej Industries Group 
 
At the Godrej Industries Group, we serve over 1.4 billion people globally through a diverse 
portfolio of businesses, united by our purpose of Crafting tomorrow. With revenues of USD 7.2 
billion in FY26 and a market capitalization of USD 19 billion as of 31 March 2026, we operate across 
FMCG, real estate, financial services, agriculture and chemicals.  
 

 
 
We are the leading player in India across several business categories, including residential real 
estate, animal feed, crude palm oil, oleochemicals, household insecticides, hair colour and air care.  
 
We are committed to building a more sustainable future through our Good & Green programme, 
with ambitions of net-zero operations by 2035 and responsible supply chains by 2047. In 2025, 
Godrej Consumer Products and Godrej Properties were both ranked number one globally in their 
respective categories on the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Sustainability Indices.  
 
For more information, please visit: www.godrejindustries.com

Godrej Capital Secures ₹2,500 Crore from Temasek at a 
Valuation of up to ₹28,000 Crore 
 
Investment supports Godrej Capital's next phase of growth as it targets ₹1 lakh crore in AUM by 2031. 
 
Mumbai, November 12, 2026: Godrej Industries Group today announced that Temasek Holdings 
(Private) Limited via its affiliate Jongsong Investments Pte Ltd will invest ₹2,500 crore in Godrej 
Capital, its financial services arm, valuing the company at up to ₹28,000 crore. Post the transaction, 
the Group will retain approximately 80% ownership in the company.  
 
Founded in 2020, the company brings the Group’s 129-year legacy of trust and integrity to modern-
day financial solutions. Through its subsidiaries, Godrej Capital serves businesses and individuals 
across India with home loans, loans against property, working capital loans, construction finance, 
gold loans, supply chain finance and personal loans. The company has a presence in over 100 cities 
and Assets Under Management (AUM) of ₹35,000 crore as of October 31, 2026.  
 
Commenting on the announcement, Pirojsha Godrej, Chairperson, Godrej Industries Group, said,  
"We are delighted to welcome Temasek as a long-term investor in Godrej Capital. This investment is a 
testament to the exceptional business Manish and his team have built in a remarkably short period, and 
reflects confidence in the significant opportunity ahead. Financial services represents a major long-
term growth area of focus for our Group, and our ambition is to build Godrej Capital into a ₹1 lakh crore 
AUM franchise by 2031. We remain committed to achieving this through disciplined execution, strong 
governance and the values of trust and integrity that have guided the Group for over a century." 
 
Manish Shah, MD & CEO, Godrej Capital, further stated, “When we began this journey, our ambition 
was to build a diversified, technology-enabled financial services business with strong risk management 
and a customer-first approach. Today, with ₹35,000 crore in AUM, we have demonstrated the strength 
of our strategy and execution. This investment will help us accelerate growth, expand our reach across 
India, deepen our offerings for businesses, individuals and the communities we serve, and strengthen our 
technology-led capabilities. With Temasek now part of our story, we are excited about the lasting value 
we will create for all our stakeholders." 
 
The investment reinforces Godrej Industries Group's commitment to building and scaling high-
growth businesses, combining its longstanding values of trust and responsible stewardship with 
entrepreneurial ambition and disciplined execution. 
 
This transaction is subject to requisite regulatory approvals.  
 
 
 
 
About Godrej Industries Group 
 
At the Godrej Industries Group, we serve over 1.4 billion people globally through a diverse 
portfolio of businesses, united by our purpose of Crafting tomorrow. With revenues of USD 7.2 
billion in FY26 and a market capitalization of USD 19 billion as of 31 March 2026, we operate across 
FMCG, real estate, financial services, agriculture and chemicals.  
 

 
 
We are the leading player in India across several business categories, including residential real 
estate, animal feed, crude palm oil, oleochemicals, household insecticides, hair colour and air care.  
 
We are committed to building a more sustainable future through our Good & Green programme, 
with ambitions of net-zero operations by 2035 and responsible supply chains by 2047. In 2025, 
Godrej Consumer Products and Godrej Properties were both ranked number one globally in their 
respective categories on the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Sustainability Indices.  
 
For more information, please visit: www.godrejindustries.com

CleanMax Signs MoU with Andhra Pradesh to Invest ~₹50,000 crore in an 
Integrated Clean Energy Complex to Power a 2 GW Compute Factory 
 
Highlights  
 
• 3 GW Integrated Renewable Energy investments in AP (Including Wind & Solar energy) 
and 1 GW of Pumped Storage within the next five years 
• 2 GW Compute Factory being set up in Kurnool District in collaboration with Neysa, an 
AI cloud provider, for using 1 GW of the compute capacity 
• CleanMax will play role of powering the Compute Factory with Green energy and the 
power infrastructure through generation and distribution 
 
Mumbai and Vishakhapatnam India, November 12, 2026:  
Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited (NSE: CLEANMAX | BSE: 544717) ("CleanMax"), 
India's largest renewable energy solutions provider for the commercial and industrial ("C&I") 
sector, today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Andhra Pradesh 
Economic Development Board (APEDB), Government of Andhra Pradesh. Under the MoU, 
CleanMax proposes to invest nearly ₹50,000 crore to develop integrated power generation 
facilities aggregating 3 GW of clean energy across wind and solar energy and 1 GW of pumped 
hydro facilities. These will be used to supply a Compute Factory being set up in collaboration 
with Neysa, with CleanMax responsible for the power infrastructure and supplies.  
CleanMax will bring generation, storage and distribution together in one integrated clean 
energy system where Wind and solar projects will generate power at different times of the 
day and year, while pumped storage and BESS (electrical) storage will provide the balancing 
of supply needed to meet round-the-clock demand. CleanMax's own distribution network will 
deliver round-the-clock power to the 2 GW Green Compute Factory. The integrated model 
aligns energy generation to compute demand with dedicated clean energy, from planning 
stage through project lifecycle.  
The Green Compute Factory will be developed in the Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh. 
CleanMax has signed an MoU with Neysa, an AI cloud provider, which will anchor the park 
with 1 GW of IT load.  
The projects will be developed in phases, with at least 1.5 GW of renewable capacity proposed 
to be developed by 2029. 
The Green Compute Factory is developed differently from the ground up. It’s supported by its 
own dedicated clean power, generated, stored and distributed by CleanMax. The Green 

 
Compute Factory will use limited water by adopting direct to chip cooling technologies and 
draw on water supplies allocated to industrial usage by the local administration.  
To distribute power within the park, a CleanMax’s owned and operated special purpose 
vehicle (“SPV”) will apply to the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (“APERC”) 
for a Distribution License, giving the Green Compute Factory its own dedicated power 
network. 
CleanMax commits to making the following social responsibility contributions:  
• Help upgrade the infrastructure of local primary schools (and Anganwadis) in 
partnership with United Way of Hyderabad 
• Work on “Skilling for Jobs”, in partnership with Pratham Education Foundation 
(“Pratham”). CleanMax will work with the Foundation to train local youth for entry-
level roles in Compute Factories. In addition, CleanMax will also run programmes for 
final-year students at local ITIs and engineering colleges to train students in advanced 
cooling and power systems, with the aim of helping students secure job opportunities 
in building and operating Compute Factories 
• Further, CleanMax’s partner, Neysa to provide compute to top tier research institutions 
in AP 
Mr. Kuldeep Jain, Founder and Managing Director, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions 
Limited, said, “Compute is becoming one of the largest new sources of power demand, and it 
needs clean energy that is available every hour of the day. In Andhra Pradesh, we are planning 
generation, storage and distribution integrated with the compute load they serve, rather than 
one after the other. Andhra Pradesh's clean energy policy framework and its strong wind and 
solar resources make it the right place to build this model at scale.” 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
About Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited 
Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited (NSE: CLEANMAX | BSE: 544717) (“CleanMax”) is 
India’s largest pureplay Commercial & Industrial (“C&I”) renewable energy company with 
more than 15 years of operations. CleanMax’s contracted RE Power Sales portfolio reached 
~6.3 GW as of September 30, 2026, with ~85% of new contracted capacity driven by existing 
customers, reflecting strong customer retention and long-term business visibility. The 
Company today serves 606 customers across technology, digital infrastructure, 
manufacturing, and industrial sectors. CleanMax’s credit rating is CRISIL AA/Stable. Its 
clientele includes global and Indian corporations such as Apple, Amazon, Google, Meta, Cisco, 
Equinix, Ultratech, BASF, Shell, CEAT, and STT GDC India, among others 
 
About Neysa 
Neysa is an AI acceleration cloud provider helping enterprises and AI builders train, deploy 
and operate AI at scale. Its portfolio includes Neysa Velocis, a managed AI cloud platform that 
brings together GPU compute, orchestration, inference, observability and cost management; 
and Neysa Tytan, dedicated bare-metal AI infrastructure for customers that need committed 
capacity and greater architectural control. 
Founded in 2023, Neysa is backed by Blackstone. The company combines experience in 
building and operating large-scale data centre and cloud infrastructure with an India-based AI 
infrastructure footprint.

TACC Limited signs a non-binding MoU with global lithium-ion cell 
manufacturer for supply of Anode Active Material 
• 
TACC signs a non binding MOU with a global cell manufacturer 
• 
The proposed long-term supply is for upto 40,000 tonnes of synthetic Anode 
• 
Collaboration also covers R&D and custom development of next-generation fast-
charging, high-range battery materials 
TACC Limited (The Advanced Carbons Company), an LNJ Bhilwara Group company and a 
wholly owned subsidiary of HEG Advanced Material, today announced the signing of a non-
binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with a global lithium-ion cell manufacturer, 
for a proposed long-term supply of upto 40,000 tonnes of synthetic graphite-based Anode 
Active Material (AAM) for electric mobility applications. 
Under the terms of the non-binding MoU, the two companies will work towards a 
progressive supply arrangement subject to further discussions and finalisation of technical 
and commercial requirements of both parties, with built-in scope for further scale-up as 
the Partner's cell manufacturing capacity expands. 
Beyond material supply, the MoU sets down the in-principle discussion to explore research 
and custom material development, focused on advanced anode formulations designed to 
enable faster charging and higher energy density - two of the critical performance levers 
for next-generation electric vehicles. 
Commenting on the development, Mr. Riju Jhunjhunwala, Chairman, TACC Limited, said: 
"We have long understood graphite, and this partnership reflects the trust that global 
leaders are placing in our capabilities. It marks a significant step in our commitment to the 
global energy transition and to building a resilient, globally competitive battery materials 
value chain.” 
Mr. Ankur Khaitan, MD & CEO, TACC Limited, added: "This partnership is a strong 
endorsement of our capabilities, and our focus now is on turning shared intent into 
execution. We are committed to developing next-generation anode materials, driven by 
innovation and delivered with the consistency and quality that our partner expects.” 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CIN:  U31909MP2022PLC064004 

 
 
About TACC Limited 
TACC Limited, a subsidiary of HEG Advanced Materials, is at the forefront of India’s materials 
innovation, specializing in advanced carbon and graphite technologies. TACC is developing 
a broad range of carbon materials and advanced material solutions to meet the evolving 
needs of global energy storage and diverse industrial applications. In its first phase, TACC 
will produce 20,000 MT of anode active material (AAM) annually, with committed expansion 
of 44,000 MT catering to global cell manufacturers. In parrallel, the company is advancing 
commercial production of graphene targeting 500 MT per annum. These efforts are backed 
by strong in-house R&D and manufacturing capabilities, enabling TACC to serve a wide 
range of high-impact industrial applications. 
About HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
HEG Advanced Materials Limited, a part of the LNJ Bhilwara Group, is a new-age platform 
spanning advanced battery materials and graphene, with a strong manufacturing, R&D 
and innovation foundation, and is also engaged in the business of battery energy solutions 
and green power. Building on HEG’s 50+ years of expertise in graphitisation and 
manufacturing know-how, the platform is developing a large-scale anode materials 
business, alongside graphene and future material development, including silicon-based 
anodes. Its capabilities span research to revenue, from advanced research and product 
development to commercialisation, serving the evolving EV, BESS and energy storage 
ecosystem. The company is listed on BSE and NSE. 
 
***
