Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Godrej Agrovet Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by ICICI Securities Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will be 
in listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an 
operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference 
has been recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Probal Sen from ICICI Securities Limited. Thank you, 
and over to you, sir. 
Probal Sen: 
Thank you very much. Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for making time to attend this 
post-Q2 earnings call of Godrej Agrovet. With us, we have members of the senior management 
of the company, including Mr. Burjis Godrej, the Chairperson of the company, Mr. Sunil 
Kataria, the CEO and Managing Director, Mr. Ravishankar, CFO, and we also have Mr. Arijit 
Mukherjee, who is the Chief Operating Officer of Astec LifeSciences. 
 
As always, the management will first give their briefing on the results and their strategic outlook, 
post which we will have an interactive Q&A session. 
 
So, without further ado, I will hand over to the management. Over to you, sir. 
Burjis Godrej: 
Thank you, Probal. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Godrej Agrovet earnings call for 
the second quarter and first half of FY27. Thank you for joining us today. Before I begin, I would 
like to extend my warm wishes to you and your family on the occasion of Diwali.  
The second quarter was marked by a challenging operating environment.  El Niño intensified 
into a super event, with the monsoon ending about 13% below normal and reservoir levels at a 
10-year low, creating uncertainty for the Rabi season. Geopolitical volatility and inflation across 
milk, feed, and packaging continued to pressure input costs. 
 
Despite these headwinds, our diversified portfolio, disciplined execution, and risk management 
helped us deliver a strong performance. Strength in animal nutrition offset pressure in crop care, 
dairy, and Astec, while our transformation agenda continued to progress. 
 
We delivered double-digit revenue growth, with Q2 consolidated revenue growing 17% year-
on-year to INR2,995 crores, driven by higher realizations and volume growth, led by animal 
nutrition, oil palm, and our B2C food segment, while our Bangladesh JV maintained strong 
momentum. 
 
EBITDA remained stable at INR222 crores, despite significant cost inflation, with margin at 
7.4%. Profit before tax grew 5% to INR131 crores, and PAT was up 22% to INR103 crores. 
This earnings resilience was achieved through focused interventions.  
Now, let me briefly touch upon our businesses. 

 
 
Godrej Agrovet Limited
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 18 
 
 
 
 
Animal nutrition delivered another strong quarter with revenue growth of 14% and segment 
profit growth of 32%. Growth was supported by higher realizations and volume gains across key 
segments, while margins improved through favourable mix and operating efficiencies. We 
exited the shrimp feed business to sharpen our focus on profitable growth segments. 
 
Oil palm revenue grew 28%, supported by higher realizations and a 14% growth in Fresh Fruit 
Bunch volumes as our plantations continue to mature. Segment profit increased 4%. During H1, 
we added 13,000 hectares of plantations and inaugurated India's first integrated oil palm complex 
in Khammam in Telangana. 
 
The complex brings together every stage of the oil palm value chain under one roof: seed and 
genetics, nursery, R&D, mill, and upcoming state-of-the-art refinery in the complex. We 
commissioned a mill at the complex along with a CPKO refinery and biogas plant during the 
quarter, strengthening our integrated ecosystem. 
 
Crop care was significantly impacted by the El Niño, and El Niño-led demand weakness and an 
unfavourable product mix. While revenue grew on a lower base, profitability declined, partly 
mitigated by our diversification into newer crop care segments. We continue to scale 
differentiated products such as Ashitaka®, though demand conditions remain challenging. 
 
At Astec LifeSciences, weak enterprise demand offset growth in the CDMO business. EBITDA 
was also impacted due to lower realizations and elevated input costs. However, we remain 
focused on transformation through new products, capacity utilization, and cost optimization. 
 
Dairy revenue grew 6%, led by calibrated pricing and growth in value-added products, which 
now account for 49% of the portfolio. Profitability remained affected by elevated milk 
procurement, packaging, and logistics costs.  
Godrej Foods continued to shift towards higher-value products, with B2C growing by 50% and 
its salience increasing to 38%, supported by consumer demand and successful launches. 
 
Our Bangladesh joint venture, ACI Godrej Agrovet, delivered another strong quarter with robust 
volume, revenue, and growth in profit.  
For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue grew 13% to INR5,847 crores. Profitability was 
impacted by inflation and adverse weather, with EBITDA and PBT declining modestly. The H1 
PAT stood at INR231 crores. 
 
Working capital management remains strong, with net working capital improving to 21 days 
from 32 days last year. Absolute working capital reduced to INR655 crores, strengthening 
balance sheet and returns on capital.  
On sustainability, renewable energy now accounts for 79.3% of our portfolio, while scope one 
and two emissions reduced by 11.1%. We also retained our CDP A- leadership rating and 
continued progressing towards the SBTi-approved emission targets. Looking ahead, we remain 
mindful of weather-related uncertainty, input cost inflation, and geopolitical volatility. However, 

 
 
Godrej Agrovet Limited
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 18 
 
 
 
our strong market position, diversified portfolio, and healthy balance sheet give us confidence 
in navigating near-term challenges while continuing to invest for growth. We remain positive 
on the long-term opportunities across our businesses and India's agricultural and consumption 
story.  
In closing, I would like to thank our employees, farmers, channel partners, customers, and all 
stakeholders for their continued trust and support. Our focus remains on executing our 
transformation agenda, driving operational excellence, and creating sustaining long-term value. 
 
Thank you, and we will now be happy to take your questions. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, sir. We'll now begin the question-and-answer session. The first question is from the 
line of Abhijit Akella from Kotak Securities. Please go ahead. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Good afternoon. Thank you so much for taking my questions. I had a few to start with on the oil 
palm segment. Could you please help update us on the health of the plantations, especially in 
Andhra Pradesh, in the context of a large rainfall deficit in that state in the backdrop of El Niño, 
followed by, I believe, in the past few weeks, twin cyclones that seem to have hit that part of the 
country? How's the output looking like, fresh fruit bunch arrivals for this year and next year? If 
you could please share your thoughts on that? 
Sunil Kataria: 
Okay. Hi, Abhijit. Sunil here. Abhijit, on the oil palm business, definitely one thing which 
happened in the quarter two was that India faced one of the driest June in 100 years, where we 
had some 40%-odd rain deficit. That's one part. The heat continued into the Andhra Pradesh and 
Telangana states during July and August. 
 
If you see geographically, Andhra, Telangana, Karnataka, these southern states have had the 
highest shortfall of rainfall. The impact of that actually showed to us in the drop in the oil 
extraction ratio in this quarter. If you were to remember the data in the first quarter, we have 
been doing very well in OER. In the first quarter, we were much ahead of last year's first quarter 
itself, thanks to our own efficiency drive. 
 
But clearly, this kind of heat wave impacted that oil extraction ratio in this quarter. That is one 
piece which happened. Now, obviously, Bay of Bengal has these whole phenomena of cyclone 
which come together towards October, November, and the last few weeks, we have seen two 
cyclones pan out. 
 
The good news is, these cyclones have dumped a lot of rainwater in big quantities in all the 
mandals across the coastal region, which, in a way, is good because this refreshes some part of 
the soil water level, which is very good for the palm trees. I would say these cyclones, while not 
fully making up for the deficit, but may actually turn out to be pretty much of a boon. 
 
In terms of any uprooting of trees and all, no, there's hardly been any widespread pieces or any 
trees getting damaged, but it's this sharp jump of rain, which has happened in the last, two to 
three weeks. It's in a way pretty good for the coming few quarters. 

 
 
Godrej Agrovet Limited
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 18 
 
 
 
 
Overall, what we are seeing in OER is that despite taking a hit in June, July, August, three 
months, from September onwards, with some intervention that we have done, some of these 
cyclonic phenomena happening, the OER has started coming back. Our September OER was 
pretty much close back to last year September’s OER, and October is marginally ahead of last 
year’s October. This trajectory shift which has happened in what augurs well for the future. 
 
I would say, barring any big changes which were to happen on the weather, I think the two to 
three months that we saw of extreme heat wave-led impact, as of now, it seems a bit behind us, 
and our focus is very clearly to keep scaling up OER back for the next five months and see if we 
can. The target is really that can we make up for the three months hit and end up the year back 
at the overall OER of the last year level at an annualized basis. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Got it, Sunil. That's helpful. Thank you so much. Just to clarify from a fresh fruit bunch arrival 
standpoint. We had expectations of double-digit growth both for FY27 and 2028. 
Sunil Kataria: 
Yeah. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Despite whatever is going on in weather, do you still feel confident that that is achievable? 
Sunil Kataria: 
Yeah, that we don't have an issue. If you see actually quarter two, despite this huge challenge of

So, if you see, on a H1 basis, we are pretty close to a double-digit growth. And this is despite 
three months of six months being extreme weather conditions. And I think what is coming into 
play is part of, as I've always talked to in the narrative whenever I talk to you, that this 
demographic dividend keeps coming up is a bit of a buffer for us, that we have these new 
plantations which keep coming, moving in from juvenile period to productive period. 
 
Then the ones which are in the early, what do you call, adolescence stage, they get into maturity. 
So, I think that is something which keeps coming in handy, and they will keep coming in handy 
for any such adverse conditions. Despite, I would say, three out of six months being hit, we are 
still very close to a double-digit growth, and it should only get better. 
Abhijit Akella: 
That's good to hear. The other question I just had was on the PKO derivatives plant. The slides 
do mention that it has been commissioned now. Did it make any financial contribution in 2Q, or 
if not, then does it begin from 3Q? Shouldn't we expect that this itself could lead to a substantial 
improvement in oil palm segment margins in FY28? 
Sunil Kataria: 
Okay. First of all, it got opened only on 1st of September. Then, these plants take their own time 
to kind of early teething, scaling up, etc. No meaningful number came up in quarter two because 
we just got 30 days, and then in the 30 days, obviously, there's ramping up issues and all that 
stuff which happens. It has started; it's now settling down.

Also in this plant, if you see, we have done right now the first phase of rollout. The full-fledged 
hydrogenation and fractionation piece will come in December. There is also scale-up happening 
in two parts. The first part just gone into place. The second one will come in December. A

Abhijit Akella: 
Yeah. Just to sort of reiterate, I mean, what sort of margin expansion can we expect because of 
this in FY28 for the oil palm? 
Sunil Kataria: 
Abhijit, if you see, we have given a guidance that as this business scale up fully, the downstream 
business scales up fully, that in the midterm, which is over two to three, four-year period, this 
will add overall roughly around 2% to the overall EBITDA margin of the oil palm business. 
Abhijit Akella: 
2 percentage points to segment EBITDA. Got it. 
Sunil Kataria: 
Yeah. Overall. When it stabilizes and scales up in terms, you can take it in the midterm of two 
to three years, that's what it will end up adding to the overall EBITDA margin of the business. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Yes. Perfect. Thank you so much. Just one last thing from my end. On the crop protection side

Sunil Kataria: 
If you see, to my mind, definitely agchem environment is tough, and that's visible across the 
industry, and that it's a matter of degrees depending on the portfolio diversification. But yes, 
everybody has kind of taken a huge hit. 
 
I think a large part of this is primarily, nobody saw this kind of a super El Niño impact panning 
out. In fact, I remember the conversation we had in the last call, I was hopeful that Indian Ocean 
Dipole will play out. July had started looking better, but what has panned out, after 15th July 
again was horrible, impacting our cotton business because we are at the early stage of emergence. 
 
We got impacted on cotton because of very dry heat in June. We were hopeful that this will 
improve from July onwards, but August, September, October have been extremely tough. 
 
I think the pieces that we have to brace for is that India is going to see a tough Rabi season 
because the reservoir levels have crashed. So that is something I think overall agchem industry 
will have to brace for impact. That is one piece which we are very clearly seeing. And the 
question is now, where do we see the long-term part of the business? 
 
I think two parts in the strategy, I would say, which we stay the course. One thing is, we are on

The good news in all these dark clouds of agchem is we have successfully rolled out the first

number which, okay, let me maybe give you a directional number. This would be the launch 
which in its first year would have crossed INR100 crores in revenue. 
 
Now that I can tell you by any standard of imagination would be a very successful launch. And 
that's what we believe will still happen in a very disastrous agchem industry year. 
 
Now, if this we can keep building further, and this will happen on the back of, I think, a super

in Khammam in Telangana.

commissioned a mill at the complex along with a CPKO refinery and biogas plant during the 
quarter, strengthening our integrated ecosystem.

Amagi and Golden Times Media Technology to Bring Chinese Entertainment 
Channels to Global Platforms 
Drama Short, Chinese Kung Fu, and AniVerse join Amagi CONNECT, the global 
content marketplace, giving streaming, FAST, and CTV platforms worldwide a direct 
line to short-form drama, martial arts and animation 
Bangalore, November 12, 2026 — Amagi, the media industry cloud company, today 
announced a partnership with Golden Times Media Technology (stock code 920021.BJ), a 
Beijing-based media and technology company, to bring its entertainment channels to platforms 
and audiences outside of China. The partnership will initially bring four of Golden Times 
Media’s technology channels – Drama Short, Chinese Kung Fu, AniVerse, and C Drama+ – 
onto the Amagi® CONNECT marketplace, making them available for discovery by platforms 
around the world. Golden Times plans to add more channels, including movie, cycling, and 
food channels, to Amagi CONNECT over time.  
Golden Times Media Technology has built its entertainment portfolio for audiences in China 
and is now introducing it internationally. This partnership reflects Amagi’s broader effort to 
bring great content from every market to more viewers, on whatever platform they watch. 
Through Amagi CONNECT, platforms can review the channels and request a connection. 
When a platform agrees to carry a channel, Amagi Direct Delivery supports efficient delivery 
from Golden Times Media to that platform. 
“Reaching audiences outside China has been a goal for us for some time,” said Jason Cheung, 
Global Business Development Manager, Golden Times Media Technology. “Amagi gives us 
a direct way to put our channels in front of international platforms, helping us introduce viewers 
around the world to content our audiences in China already enjoy.” 
“Platforms are always looking for distinctive content that gives viewers reasons to stay, and 
short-form drama, martial arts, and animation each deliver on that,” said Thomas Parsons, 
Senior Director, Amagi. “Amagi CONNECT gives Golden Times one place to present its 
compelling lineup to platforms worldwide, and gives those platforms a streamlined way to 
discover and evaluate it. We see this as the start of a long partnership, and we look forward 
to bringing more of Golden Times’ channels to audiences around the world. 
The four channels included in this initial phase offer distinct entertainment propositions: Drama 
Short features short-form drama programming; Chinese Kung Fu features combat sports 
events and tournaments; AniVerse offers animation content; and C Drama+ focuses on 
premium TV series such as period dramas and romance. Together, they represent a first 
sample of Golden Times Media Technology's broader portfolio as the company begins to 
introduce its content to international markets. 
amag1 

The partnership further demonstrates Amagi’s continued work with Asia-Pacific content 
owners as they take their channels to global streaming, FAST, and CTV platforms. 
Platforms interested in evaluating the channels can find them on Amagi CONNECT. 
About Golden Times Media Technology 
Golden Times Media Technology (founded in 2011, publicly traded on the Beijing Stock 
Exchange under stock code: 920021.BJ) is a leading provider of ultra-high-definition (UHD) 
video transmission technologies and digital content operations, serving major mainstream 
media and entertainment channels across China. Deeply rooted in professional video 
encoding/decoding, UHD transmission, and broadcast-and-telecom-grade distribution, the 
company is actively expanding its global footprint through technology-driven innovation and 
content licensing. Empowered by advanced AIGC and video intelligence capabilities, Golden 
Times Media Technology is building a robust international matrix spanning FAST (Free Ad-
supported Streaming TV) operations, global copyright trading, and advanced technology 
deployment—featuring premium specialized channels such as AniVerse and Drama Short. By 
seamlessly integrating cutting-edge video technology with rich media assets, the company is 
dedicated to delivering superior audiovisual experiences and exceptional commercial value to 
global audiences and partners. 
About Amagi 
Amagi (www.amagi.com) is the media industry cloud, helping broadcasters, streamers, and 
content owners create, deliver, and monetize video at scale. The Amagi platform unifies 
content production, playout, distribution, and monetization across linear TV, FAST, streaming, 
and social so customers can maximize reach, engagement, and revenue. Distributors, 
including connected TV platforms and pay-TV operators, use Amagi to acquire, curate, and 
serve content to their audiences more efficiently. Amagi manages 16,000+ channel deliveries 
across 300+ distributors in 40+ countries.

Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Blue Jet Healthcare Limited Q2 and H1 
FY27 Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only 
mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. 
Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star 
and then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this call is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Advait Bhadekar from EY. Thank you, and over to you. 
Advait Bhadekar: 
Thank you, Yashashri. Good evening and a warm welcome everyone to Q2 and H1 FY27 
Earnings Call of Blue Jet Healthcare Limited. Please note, the investor presentation and the 
financial results are available on the company website and the stock exchange. 
 
Also, anything said on this call which reflects our outlook for the future or which could be 
construed as a forward-looking statement must be reviewed in conjunction with the risks that 
the company faces. 
 
The conference call is being recorded and the transcript along with the audio of the same will be 
made available on the website of the company as well as on the exchanges. Please also note that 
the audio of the conference call is the copyright material of Blue Jet Healthcare Limited and 
cannot be copied, rebroadcasted, or attributed in press or media without specific and written 
consent of the company. 
 
From the management, we have with us today Mr. Shiven Arora, Managing Director, Mr. V.K. 
Singh, Chief Operating Officer, Mr. Ganesh Karuppannan, Chief Financial Officer, and Mr. 
Sanjay Sinha, Deputy Chief Financial Officer. 
 
Now I request Mr. Shiven Arora, Managing Director of Blue Jet Healthcare Limited, to provide 
you with the updates for the quarter and half-year ended 30th September 2026. Thank you, and 
over to you, sir. 
Shiven Arora: 
Thank you, Advait. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. I am pleased 
to report that Blue Jet Healthcare has delivered a strong second quarter, reflecting continued 
improvement in business momentum across our core businesses. 
 
During the quarter, we reported our highest-ever quarterly revenue from operations of 
approximately INR376 crores, with EBITDA of approximately INR119 crores. This represents 
sequential growth of 28% in revenue and 21% in EBITDA. More importantly, the performance 
reflects the progress we have been making in strengthening our business over the past several 
quarters. 
 
Our PI vertical, supported by improving demand from existing programs and contributions from 
newer products. Our contrast media business also maintained healthy momentum, supported by 
our established customer relationships and expanding product portfolio. As we enter the second 
half of FY27, we remain encouraged by the order visibility and customer engagement across 
both these businesses. 

 
 
Blue Jet Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 14 
 
 
Although quarterly performances will continue to be influenced by shipment schedules and 
product mix. Beyond the financial performance, this quarter marks important progress in our 
journey towards building a broader innovation-led CDMO platform. We see this as an important 
milestone in expanding our participation in complex innovator-led pharmaceutical programs and 
demonstrating our ability to develop differentiated chemistry platforms. 
 
Another important development is that our Hyderabad R&D center is now operational, with 
scientific teams onboarded and development activities underway. This facility will play a central 
role in strengthening our developmental capabilities and supporting a broader range of customer 
programs, particularly as we expand in more complex chemistry and CDMO opportunities. 
 
Turning to our long-term investments, I would like to emphasize the strategic thinking behind 
our expansion plans. Our ambition is not simply to add manufacturing capacity. We are building 
a globally competitive CDMO platform that combines decades of complex chemistry expertise 
with integrated R&D, flexible manufacturing infrastructure, and long-standing relationships 
with global pharmaceutical innovators. 
 
Vizag represents an important part of this journey. We are approaching this investment in a 
phased and disciplined manner, with capacity planning closely aligned to identified customer 
opportunities and the progression of our development pipeline. Our vision is to create a 
manufacturing platform capable of supporting multiple chemistry technologies, customers, and 
product life cycles. 
 
Together with the Hyderabad R&D, this will enable us to strengthen our participation across the 
development-to-commercial manufacturing value chain. We also recognize that investments of 
this scale require time for construction, qualification, and commercial ramp-up. Our focus 
remains on disciplined capital allocation, efficient execution, and building capabilities that can 
generate sustainable returns over the long term. 
 
The successful completion of our qualified institutional placement has further strengthened our 
balance sheet and provides us with the flexibility to execute these strategic investments while 
maintaining a long-term perspective. 
 
As we look ahead, our priorities remain clear: sustain the momentum in existing businesses, 
translate our development pipeline into commercial opportunities, and execute our expansion 
projects with discipline. We believe the combination of our established chemistry capabilities, 
deep customer relationships, growing R&D infrastructure, and planned manufacturing 
investments positions Blue Jet to become an increasingly relevant partner to the global 
pharmaceutical innovators. 
 
To conclude, the first half of FY27 has demonstrated encouraging operating momentum 
alongside tangible progress in building the capabilities required for the next phase of growth. 
Our objective is to build a differentiated, globally competitive CDMO platform that creates 
sustainable value for customers and shareholders over the coming decade. 

 
 
Blue Jet Healthcare Limited 
 
 
November 05, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 14 
 
 
Thank you once again for your continued trust and confidence in Blue Jet Healthcare. I now 
invite Mr. V.K. Singh to share further updates on our operations, product development pipeline, 
and expansion projects, following which Ganesh will take you through the financial performance 
in greater detail. Thank you. 
V.K. Singh: 
Thank you, Shiven, and good evening, everyone on the call. This has been our fourth consecutive 
quarter of sequential growth, and we are encouraged by the improved business performance. 
Our focus continues to be on building Blue Jet into a globally competitive, innovation-led 
CDMO platform. The tailwinds for India, and particularly for CDMO sector, present a 
significant opportunity. 
 
To capitalize on this, we believe a sustainable CDMO strategy must rest on two critical pillars: 
globally competitive manufacturing infrastructure and differentiated R&D capabilities across 
complex and diversified chemistry platforms. 
 
Speaking specifically about manufacturing, at Mahad Unit 3, we are creating a globally scaled 
manufacturing capacity for a strategically critical KSM in our contrast media business. This 
facility will enable complete backward integration across the relevant part of our contrast media 
value chain, strengthen cost competitiveness, and provide greater security of supply. 
 
We had earlier indicated that the facility would go on stream in the second half of this year, and 
we remain on track to achieve that. The total capex incurred at Mahad to date is approximately 
INR250 crores. 
 
Moving to Vizag Unit 5 and Unit 6, this will be our next major growth platform. As you may 
recall, we secured approximately 100 acres for the development of an integrated pharmaceutical 
manufacturing facility. The project is being developed in phases. Phase I will include significant 
investments in contrast media, pharmaceutical intermediates, peptide fragments, high-intensity 
sweeteners, and some multipurpose blocks. 
 
Our approach at Vizag is not merely to add capacity. We are consciously designing the facility 
to provide flexibility across chemistry platforms, customers, and product life cycles. The 
infrastructure will support both early-stage incubation and graduation of programs into 
commercial manufacturing, including a couple of lateral transfers. 
 
This flexibility will allow us to respond to evolving customer requirements and bridge scale 
existing opportunities and build new partnerships. The pre-construction activities are underway. 
Statutory compliances like EC and the Consent to Establish are in place. For phase I, as indicated 
earlier, we envisage a capex of about INR1,000 crores. 
 
Coming to R&D, if you recall from our previous earnings calls, as a part of our endeavor for 
platform diversification, we were building a new R&D and innovation center at Hyderabad, 
which would add about 100 fume hoods over two phases to our current capacity. 
 
I am pleased to share that this center, that houses several synthesis labs, a world-class analytical 
facility, is now operational. We have onboarded approximately 50 high-performing scientists,

November 05, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 14 
 
and development activities have commenced. Our objective is to build a chemistry-led R&D 
platform that can support customers from early-stage process development through scale-up and 
commercial manufacturing.

synthesis, peptides, and GLP related intermediates, biocatalysis, high-potency products, and 
solid-phase chemistry. We believe these capabilities will strengthen our ability to address a wide 
range of innovator-led programs and improve our response time to increasing RFPs. 
 
Coming to the development pipeline, we are seeing encouraging progress. During the quarter, 
we successfully delivered and validated a new contrast media intermediate for an innovator. We 
consider this as an important milestone, as it demonstrates our ability to develop and deliver 
specialized chemistry solutions to customers with demanding technical and quality 
requirements.

We focus on opportunities where our chemistry expertise, manufacturing capability, and ability

our manufacturing philosophy. 
 
We have made meaningful progress in increasing the contribution of renewable energy to our 
overall consumption, which today stands at about 80%. We have also achieved a silver rating 
for EcoVadis, reflecting the progress made in our sustainability and responsible manufacturing 
practices.

purchases, inventory consumption, and in-transit stock affects when these higher costs show up

pressure on gross margin before revised pricing takes effect. The net impact will depend on how 
input price will move in the coming quarters, the product mix, and when the customer price 
adjustment becomes effective.

impact in our performance in the coming quarters. EBITDA for the quarter at INR119 crores is

to report that Blue Jet Healthcare has delivered a strong second quarter, reflecting continued 
improvement in business momentum across our core businesses. 
 
During the quarter, we reported our highest-ever quarterly revenue from operations of 
approximately INR376 crores, with EBITDA of approximately INR119 crores. This represents 
sequential growth of 28% in revenue and 21% in EBITDA. More importantly, the performance 
reflects the progress we have been making in strengthening our business over the past several 
quarters.

newer products. Our contrast media business also maintained healthy momentum, supported by 
our established customer relationships and expanding product portfolio. As we enter the second 
half of FY27, we remain encouraged by the order visibility and customer engagement across 
both these businesses.

Although quarterly performances will continue to be influenced by shipment schedules and 
product mix. Beyond the financial performance, this quarter marks important progress in our 
journey towards building a broader innovation-led CDMO platform. We see this as an important 
milestone in expanding our participation in complex innovator-led pharmaceutical programs and 
demonstrating our ability to develop differentiated chemistry platforms. 
 
Another important development is that our Hyderabad R&D center is now operational, with 
scientific teams onboarded and development activities underway. This facility will play a central 
role in strengthening our developmental capabilities and supporting a broader range of customer 
programs, particularly as we expand in more complex chemistry and CDMO opportunities. 
 
Turning to our long-term investments, I would like to emphasize the strategic thinking behind 
our expansion plans. Our ambition is not simply to add manufacturing capacity. We are building 
a globally competitive CDMO platform that combines decades of complex chemistry expertise 
with integrated R&D, flexible manufacturing infrastructure, and long-standing relationships 
with global pharmaceutical innovators.

phased and disciplined manner, with capacity planning closely aligned to identified customer 
opportunities and the progression of our development pipeline. Our vision is to create a 
manufacturing platform capable of supporting multiple chemistry technologies, customers, and 
product life cycles.

development-to-commercial manufacturing value chain. We also recognize that investments of 
this scale require time for construction, qualification, and commercial ramp-up. Our focus 
remains on disciplined capital allocation, efficient execution, and building capabilities that can 
generate sustainable returns over the long term. 
 
The successful completion of our qualified institutional placement has further strengthened our 
balance sheet and provides us with the flexibility to execute these strategic investments while 
maintaining a long-term perspective. 
 
As we look ahead, our priorities remain clear: sustain the momentum in existing businesses, 
translate our development pipeline into commercial opportunities, and execute our expansion 
projects with discipline. We believe the combination of our established chemistry capabilities, 
deep customer relationships, growing R&D infrastructure, and planned manufacturing 
investments positions Blue Jet to become an increasingly relevant partner to the global 
pharmaceutical innovators.

alongside tangible progress in building the capabilities required for the next phase of growth.

sustainable value for customers and shareholders over the coming decade.

complex and diversified chemistry platforms.

investments in contrast media, pharmaceutical intermediates, peptide fragments, high-intensity 
sweeteners, and some multipurpose blocks. 
 
Our approach at Vizag is not merely to add capacity. We are consciously designing the facility 
to provide flexibility across chemistry platforms, customers, and product life cycles. The 
infrastructure will support both early-stage incubation and graduation of programs into 
commercial manufacturing, including a couple of lateral transfers. 
 
This flexibility will allow us to respond to evolving customer requirements and bridge scale 
existing opportunities and build new partnerships. The pre-construction activities are underway. 
Statutory compliances like EC and the Consent to Establish are in place. For phase I, as indicated 
earlier, we envisage a capex of about INR1,000 crores. 
 
Coming to R&D, if you recall from our previous earnings calls, as a part of our endeavor for 
platform diversification, we were building a new R&D and innovation center at Hyderabad, 
which would add about 100 fume hoods over two phases to our current capacity.

facility, is now operational. We have onboarded approximately 50 high-performing scientists,

and development activities have commenced. Our objective is to build a chemistry-led R&D

range of innovator-led programs and improve our response time to increasing RFPs.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Tega Industries Limited Q2 FY27 Conference 
Call hosted by MUFG Intime. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode 
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should 
you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then 
zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the 
conference over to Ms. Sakshi Mehta from MUFG Intime. Thank you and over to you, ma'am. 
Sakshi Mehta: 
Good evening, everyone and welcome to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of 
Tega Industries Limited. Today, we are joined by the senior management teams of Tega 
Industries and Molycop. Representing Tega Industries are Mr. Mehul Mohanka, Managing 
Director and Group CEO, Sourav Sen, CEO, Tega McNally, Mr. Pratik Basu Roy President, 
Product Management and Mr. Ravi Joshi, Chief Financial Officer. Representing Molycop are 
Mr. Lance Dawber, Chief Operating Officer and Mr. Patrick Koley, Chief Financial Officer.                  
I would now like to hand over the call to Mr. Mehul Mohanka for his opening remarks. Thank 
you, and over to you, sir. 
Mehul Mohanka: 
Thank you, Sakshi. Good evening and a warm welcome to all the participants on the call. Thank 
you for joining us today. It's a pleasure to connect with our valued investors, analysts, and 
stakeholders. I hope you and your families are keeping well. I'm pleased to share that the H1 of 
FY 2027 was a period of strong growth and transformation for the Tega Group.  
Our core business delivered its highest-ever first-half revenue, with healthy double-digit growth 
in both revenue and EBITDA. The second quarter marked the first full quarter of Molycop's 
consolidation, significantly expanding the scale and global reach of the group. For the first half 
FY 2027, Tega Group on a consolidated basis delivered a revenue of INR59,775 million 
compared to INR7,614 million in H1 of FY 2026, reflecting the complete consolidation of 
Molycop from 1st of June 2026. EBITDA before one-time expenses was INR8,720 million, with 
an EBITDA margin of 14.4%. One-time expenses of INR2,576 million relate to the Molycop 
acquisition. In addition, an exceptional item of INR117 million reflects the inventory step-up 
charge pursuant to the purchase price allocation. These costs are non-recurring in nature.  
For the first half of FY 2027, for the Tega legacy business of consumables and equipment, 
revenue from operations grew 20% to INR9,143 million from INR7,614 million in H1 of FY 
2026, our highest-ever first-half revenue. EBITDA before one-time expenses grew 25% to 
INR1,949 million from INR1,561 million, with margins expanding by 70 basis points to 20.4% 
compared to the previous year of 19.7%, a clear demonstration of operating leverage.  
Gross margins improved to 61% compared to 59% for the same period last year, supported by 
favorable product mix and pricing discipline. For our consumables business, revenue grew a 
robust 30% to INR8,117 million compared to the previous year period of INR6,264 million. 
EBITDA grew 42% to INR1,916 million compared to the same period previous year of 
INR1,346 million, with margins expanding by 190 basis points to 22.4%.  

 
Tega Industries Limited 
 
 
November 05, 2026 
Page 3 of 14 
 
For our equipment business, revenue for the first half stood at INR973 million, reflecting the 
timing of project execution. Importantly, we saw a strong sequential recovery in quarter two, 
and our order book gives us a strong visibility of the second half.  
For the second quarter of FY 2027, for the Tega legacy business of equipment and consumables, 
revenue from operations grew 19% to INR4,825 million. Our highest-ever second-quarter 
revenue, and grew 11% sequentially over quarter one. EBITDA before one-time expenses grew 
11% to INR937 million, with an EBITDA margin of 18.8%. Consumables revenue grew 26% to 
INR4,209 million, with EBITDA up 28% to INR905 million and margins improving to 20.8%. 
Equipment revenue grew 72% sequentially to INR615 million from INR358 million in quarter 
one, returning to positive EBITDA. Gross margins remain healthy at 60%.  
For our grinding media business, the second quarter of FY 2027, which is our first full quarter, 
revenue was INR37,716 million, which is equivalent to about US$396 million, and EBITDA of 
INR5,144 million, which is approximately US$54 million, at a margin of 14%.  
For first half of FY 2027, for our grinding media business, which is June through September, a 
period of four months, revenue stood at about INR50,632 million and an EBITDA of INR6,772 
million. Transaction-related to one-time costs have tapered meaningfully from INR1,853 million 
in quarter one to INR650 million in quarter two, with the bulk of these costs now behind us.  
For the second quarter of FY 2027, Tega Group consolidated revenue from operations stood at 
INR42,540 million and EBITDA before one-time expenses of INR6,081 million, at a margin of 
14.2%. Our order book as of 30th September 2026, excluding our grinding media business, 
stands at INR13,976 million, up 14% from INR12,313 million at the end of quarter one, with 
INR11,576 million executable within the next 12 months.  
This provides strong visibility and confidence in our growth trajectory. Within just a few months 
of coming together, both Tega and Molycop teams have been working hard to deliver cross-
selling synergies, and we have initiated the journey towards realizing commercial synergies. 
I am pleased to share that we have made a trial supply of Molycop's grinding media to one of 
Tega's existing customers, starting with an initial volume of 500 tons. This trial creates an 
opportunity for annualized supplies of over 30,000 tons. It is an early proof of our cross-selling 
strategy, offering our combined portfolio to customers who already trust the Molycop and Tega 
brands.  
I want to thank our employees for their unwavering commitment, our customers for their trust, 
and you, our investors, for your continued support. We are committed to delivering sustainable 
value and transparent communication. I would now like to hand over to Ravi, who will walk you 
through the consolidated financial performance, and subsequently to Lance and Patrick to take 
you through the market update and financial performance of the Molycop business. Thank you. 
Ravi Joshi: 
Thanks, Mehul, and good evening, everyone. You have heard about the operating performance 
and the Molycop business. Now I would like to take you through the shape of the balance sheet 
after the acquisition and the working capital. This will help the audience to appreciate our 
consolidated results better.  

 
Tega Industries Limited 
 
 
November 05, 2026 
Page 4 of 14 
 
Unless I say otherwise, the figures I refer are consolidated and INR in million. Let me begin 
with the consolidated results. This is the first half of the Molycop consolidation, starting from 
June 1, 2026, and the reported number therefore carries several acquisition-related items, most 
of which are either one-time or non-cash in nature.  
The group reported a loss after tax of INR1,670 million for this half. However, excluding one-
time items, our adjusted PAT is positive by INR452 million. The largest of these items are 
transaction costs, which is INR2,576 million related to the acquisition, which have expensed 
during this period as required under IndAS.  
As earlier mentioned by Mehul, these are tapering quickly, just to reiterate, from INR1,910 
million in Q1 to INR666 million in Q2. In addition, under the purchase price allocation, we have 
recorded a one-time inventory step-up charge of INR117 million, which is non-cash in nature.  
I would also like to draw your attention to the finance cost. The finance cost of INR4,086 million 
reported for this half is including of dividend on redeemable preference share at the Molycop in 
accordance with the Ind AS. Similarly, you have noticed the tax expense of INR1,235 million, 
which we expect that effective tax rate to normalize over the coming quarters. 
Turning to the balance sheet, the acquisition has brought up a step change in the scale. Our 
overall assets stood at INR227,066 million as on September 30, 2026, compared with INR43,145

Cera Sanitaryware Limited 
Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
November 05, 2026 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the earnings conference call of 
CERA Sanitaryware Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only 
mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation 
concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an 
operator by pressing ‘star’ then ‘zero’ on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this 
conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Devrishi Singh 
from CDR India. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Singh. 
Devrishi Singh: 
Thank you. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us on CERA 
Sanitaryware Limited's Q2 FY27 earnings conference call to discuss the results 
announced yesterday. We have with us today the management team comprising, 
Mr. Vikas Kothari - CFO, and Mr. Deepak Chaudhary - VP Finance and Investor 
Relations of CERA Sanitaryware. We will start with brief opening remarks from the 
management, following which we will open the call for Q&A. 
 
A quick disclaimer before we begin. Some of the statements made in today's 
conference call may be forward-looking in nature, and a detailed note in this regard 
is contained in the results document that have been shared with all of you earlier. I 
would now turn the call over to the management for their opening remarks. Thank 
you, and over to you, Deepak. 
Deepak Chaudhary: 
Thank you, Devrishi. Good morning, everyone, and a warm welcome to all of you for 
joining us on CERA Sanitaryware Limited's Q2 FY27 earnings conference call. I will 
begin by sharing a brief overview of the operational and strategic developments 
during the quarter, following which our CFO, Mr. Vikas Kothari will take you through 
the financial performance in greater detail.  
CERA continued to deliver healthy growth during Q2 FY27, with revenues growing by 
27.4% year-on-year. Both our sanitaryware as well as the faucetware business 
performed well, growing by 24% and 38% respectively. Sanitaryware and faucetware 
accounted for 45% and 43% of total revenues respectively, together contributing 
approximately 88% of CERA's overall revenues. Importantly, the growth during the 
quarter was predominantly volume-driven, with healthy traction across key product 
categories, including sanitaryware, faucetware, tiles, and construction chemicals. 
 
From a channel perspective, retail demand continued to recover and was 
complemented by an encouraging performance in the projects business. As many of 
you would be aware, the projects business has been an important contributor to our 
performance over the past several quarters. The improving contribution from retail 
channel is a positive development for the overall business. Another important aspect 
of the quarter was the consistency of growth, with business momentum remaining 
healthy throughout July, August, and September, rather than being concentrated in 
any particular month.  

 
Transcript of CERA Sanitaryware Ltd. Q2 FY27 Earnings Call        
    Page 2 of 14 
 
 
It is important for the investors to appreciate that the broader industry environment 
remains challenging. While demand trends have shown improvement, the operating 
environment continues to be affected by elevated input costs and supply-side 
challenges. Against this backdrop, we believe that CERA's performance reflects the 
inherent strengths of the business model, as well as the multiple interventions we have 
undertaken to further strengthen our competitive position.  
Over the past few years, we have consistently worked on further developing our focus 
markets by strengthening distribution and dealer relationships, improving our market 
approach, and enhancing internal execution capabilities. These initiatives are now 
beginning to yield tangible results and, we believe, have been critical factors that 
have enabled us to win incremental market share.  
From a geographical perspective, we are seeing healthy traction across the wider set 
of markets. Uttar Pradesh has emerged as an important market for us, and the focus 
markets such as Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and MP have also shown 
traction. The work undertaken to strengthen our presence in these markets have 
helped us broaden our geographical presence and offset relatively weaker demand 
in certain traditionally strong regions. We continue to focus on deepening penetration 
and addressing white spaces in existing markets while simultaneously expanding our 
reach into smaller towns and emerging consumption centers.  
Coming to the input cost environment, brass and gas remain elevated during the 
quarter, creating challenges for the industry. We have taken calibrated price revisions 
across our product portfolio over the past few quarters, including a further price 
increase of approximately 8% in the faucetware segment, effective from September 
1st, 2026, to partly offset the impact of higher brass prices. The benefits of this revision 
are expected to flow through the channels from later part of Q3 FY27 onwards. 
 
As discussed in our previous earnings call, there is a lag between implementation of 
price hikes and realizing their full benefits, particularly in the projects business, where 
certain supplies are executed against previously agreed prices. We have therefore 
introduced measures to strengthen pricing discipline for future project commitments 
and better project profitability against further increase in input costs. 
 
Alongside these pricing actions, we continue to focus on cost optimization, process 
improvements, and operating efficiencies. While the full benefits of these initiatives will 
be visible progressively, initial outcomes have led to an improvement in the operating 
margins on a sequential basis. We expect further benefits to flow through the coming 
quarters as these measures take effect.  
Our established sourcing arrangements and strong in-house manufacturing 
capabilities continue to provide us with a relative advantage in navigating the 
challenging cost environment. In particular, our favorable gas sourcing arrangement 
has helped us to cushion the impact of higher energy costs, positioning us favorably 
relative to several other industry participants.  
From a manufacturing perspective, capacity utilization has improved considerably, 
supported by recovery in volumes. Our sanitaryware facilities are currently operating 
at utilization level of 82%. In faucetware, we have been able to increase monthly 
production from 4 lakh units to 5 lakh units by adding certain balancing equipments 
of plant and machinery within the same facility.  
We have also selectively brought certain fast-moving products in-house, reducing our 
dependence on external manufacturers and strengthening our ability to maintain 
consistent product availability. This has been particularly relevant given the operating 

 
Transcript of CERA Sanitaryware Ltd. Q2 FY27 Earnings Call        
    Page 3 of 14 
 
 
challenges faced by several manufacturers in the Morbi cluster. Our ability to service 
customer requirements consistently has helped us respond effectively to the market 
opportunities. 
 
On the brand front, the core CERA brand remains the principal driver of our volume-
led growth. We remain focused on strengthening our position across the mass and 
mid-premium categories through product development, distribution expansion, and 
sustained brand-building initiatives. At the same time, we continue to invest in 
strengthening our newer brands, including Senator and CERA Luxe, with a long-term 
perspective.  
Looking ahead, we remain confident of sustaining our growth momentum, supported 
by improving demand and deeper penetration across existing and emerging 
markets. The investments made in our distribution network, manufacturing 
capabilities, and internal processes over the past few years have strengthened our 
ability to capitalize on the opportunities ahead. While input cost inflation remains an 
important challenge, we expect profitability to improve progressively during the 
second half of FY27, supported by the cumulative benefits of pricing actions, cost 
efficiency initiatives, and the healthy volume growth. We are now confident of 
surpassing the revenue growth target, along with the full year's EBITDA margin outlook 
of 13%-14%.  
With this, I would now like to hand over the call to Mr. Vikas Kothari to take you through 
the financial performance of the quarter. 
Vikas Kothari: 
Thank you, Deepak, and a very good morning to everyone. I will now take you through 
a brief overview of the company's financial performance for the quarter ended 
September 30th, 2026.  
Revenue from operations for the quarter stood at INR 603 crore as compared to INR 
473 crore in Q2 FY26, representing a healthy Y-o-Y growth of 27.4%. For the first half of 
FY 2027, revenue from operations stood at INR 1,089 crore, reflecting a growth of 23.7% 
over the corresponding period of the previous year.  
EBITDA excluding other income for the quarter stood at INR 73 crore as compared to 
INR 67 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The EBITDA margins 
stood at 12.2% in Q2 FY27 compared with 14.2% in Q2 FY26 and 10.1% in Q1 FY27. 
 
While input cost pressures, particularly in brass and gas, continued during the quarter, 
we witnessed a sequential improvement in operating margins. This improvement was 
supported by the benefits of the pricing actions undertaken over the preceding 
quarters, alongside our ongoing focus on operational efficiencies and effective cost 
management. 
 
As mentioned earlier, the benefits of price revisions, particularly in the project business, 
are being realized with a time lag. The revised price arrangements for future project 
commitments should progressively support margins over the coming quarters.  
The average cost of gas during Q2 FY27 stood at INR 47.29 per cubic meter compared 
with INR 33.79 per cubic meter in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. 
Similarly, the average cost of brass during Q2 FY27 stood at INR 932 per kg compared 
with INR 589 per kg in Q2 FY26 and INR 837 per kg in Q1 FY27, representing an increase 
of 58% on Y-o-Y basis and 11% on quarter-on-quarter basis.  

 
Transcript of CERA Sanitaryware Ltd. Q2 FY27 Earnings Call        
    Page 4 of 14 
 
 
In terms of the revenue mix, sanitaryware accounted for 45% of our revenues, 
faucetware 43%, tiles 10%, and wellness 2%. On a Y-o-Y basis, sanitaryware revenues 
grew by 24%, faucetware by 38%, tiles by 9%, and wellness by 71%. 
 
From a channel perspective, the projects business accounted for 39% of the revenues, 
while the retail business contributed 61% in Q2 FY27. In Q1 FY27, we accelerated 
deliveries for certain projects in view of the rising input costs. This resulted in a project-
to-retail revenue mix of 43:57.   Going forward, we expect this mix to stabilize at around 
40: 60.  
Profit after tax for Q2 FY27 stood at INR 56 crore compared with INR 57 crore in the 
corresponding quarter of the previous year. Earnings per share for the quarter stood 
at INR 43.52 compared with INR 43.92 in Q2 FY26.  
On the working capital front, we continue to focus on inventory management, 
receivables, and overall working capital discipline. Inventory days decreased from 83 
days to 69 days. Receivable days reduced from 33 days to 28 days, while payables 
remained unchanged at 39 days. Consequently, our net working capital improved 
from 77 days to 58 days on Y-o-Y basis.  
As of September 30, 2026, our cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 897 crore. Our 
balance sheet remains healthy, providing us with the flexibility to support our ongoing 
business requirements and other strategic initiatives.  
Regarding our capital expense plans, we continue to progress with the investments 
outlined for FY27. Capital expense incurred during the first half stood at INR 27 crore 
against our planned full year outlay of approximately INR 43 crore.  
Looking ahead, we expect operating profitability to improve progressively during the 
second half of FY27, supported by sustained demand, healthy volumes, and the 
benefits of our pricing and cost efficiency initiatives.  
We are actively working on increasing cost efficiency using automation and AI tools. 
We are aggressively evaluating various costs in the system, exploring greater 
automation of processes, and identifying interventions that can yield savings. We are 
confident that these actions will contribute visible and tangible benefits in the next 
couple of quarters and thereafter.  
While input cost movements remain an important factor, the cost actions and the 
likely benefits of operating leverage gives us confidence to maintain our full year 
EBITDA margin outlook. Overall, we remain focused on sustainable profitable growth 
and maintaining a healthy balance sheet.  
With this, I would request the moderator to open the lines for Q&A. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. The first question comes from the 
line of Amit Srivastava with 360 ONE Capital.  
Amit Srivastava: 
Sir, just wanted to understand first, can you give us the breakup of this growth which 
has come in sanitaryware and faucetware? As you mentioned, it is more driven by 
volume. If you can give the breakup, like last quarter you had given volume, price, 
and mix, how much have these contributed in this quarter? 
Vikas Kothari: 
So, in terms of the growth part, as we are witnessing quarter-on-quarter, it is purely 
volume-driven growth. So retail demand continued to recover, which was 
complemented by steady project performance. In terms of the breakup of the growth 

 
Transcript of CERA Sanitaryware Ltd. Q2 FY27 Earnings Call        
    Page 5 of 14 
 
 
for Q2, volume contributed around 16.6%. Price revision actions, which we have taken, 
were partially realized and contributed around 9.1%, and mix contributed around 
1.7%. This was for the overall Company as a whole.  
And I think you have asked for the breakup with respect to sanitaryware and 
faucetware. Again, in case of sanitaryware, volume has contributed 14.3%, and the 
favorable price impact was 6.7%, and 2.7% was the mix impact, which overall resulted 
in revenue growth of 23.7%. In case of faucetware, the breakup of 38% growth is 
largely driven by volume, which contributed 24%, the favorable price impact was 
10.3%, and the balance is the mix impact, which was 1.9%. 
Amit Srivastava: 
Okay. Sir, just to understand where this strong volume growth is coming from. Are we 
gaining market share because we have some advantage on our cost side, or is it 
brand distribution or a new market which is giving us that edge? Or has this price 
increase which we have taken, and the resulting pre-buying also given a kind of push 
to our volume overall? What is really driving it? Is it ground-level demand or expansion, 
all this, if you can explain. 
Deepak Chaudhary: 
Essentially, the volume is being driven by increased demand from the market, 
because pre-buying, like we have taken two price increases during the last two 
quarters, is something which only impacts a particular period. Just immediately after 
the price increase, you find the volume going up substantially, but later on, it all 
normalizes. So, the sustained improvement in demand that we are able to see is not 
on account of just the pre-buying portion building up. It is the improved demand 
which is already there in the market. 
 
More importantly, it is the steps that the Company has taken over the last couple of 
years when the demand was muted, where we have concentrated on both the 
external factors, the distribution channel, improving the market, understanding the 
consumer, understanding our distributors, and trying to improve the entire distribution, 
the product, the manufacturing efficiency, and the outsourcing arrangements. 
 
They are all now coming together to kind of help us, because the external demand is 
there, but you will find that even meeting that demand becomes a challenge in the 
current situation wherein we are dependent, like 50% on outsourcing. As of now, you 
can say that because of the fact that we have taken those initiatives over the last 
couple of years, they are all adding up.  
Would I say that we have gained market share; - I would definitely think that over the 
last three, four quarters, the way that our numbers have grown, market share would 
have gone up. But it is a little difficult to assess in our specific industry because you find 
that most of the players are unlisted, and it takes a little time for the numbers to come 
in. Even the ones which are listed have a large number of products. So, in this 
particular space it is difficult to gauge as to what kind of numbers they are having. But 
we are confident that if we do not talk about just the external competitors, at least 
we are very good, happy in terms of the kind of numbers that we have been able to 
achieve over the last, you can say, three, four quarters. 
Amit Srivastava: 
Perfect. In terms of the project business, sir, you said that the mix has increased to 43%, 
and will move towards 40%. So, can it come down on an immediate basis, like in the 
coming quarter, or is it slightly medium term that it will move towards that direction? 
Deepak Chaudhary: 
It has already happened in this quarter. I will just answer your question about this, but 
it has already happened in this quarter. In this quarter, the project business 
contributed 39% as opposed to 43% in the previous quarter. The previous quarter was 
kind of an aberration because of the input price increases which had happened and 

 
Transcript of CERA Sanitaryware Ltd. Q2 FY27 Earnings Call        
    Page 6 of 14 
 
 
the kind of profitability concerns that they were raising. We had actively pushed 
deliveries of certain projects which were nearing completion. We had kind of 
preponed the deliveries at that point of time because the inputs prices were 
continuously rising. That was an aberration.  
 
 
 
We have already come back to that level of 39% in the current quarter, and we should 
be at that 40%-60% ratio that we have traditionally, as of now, been maintaining over 
the last couple of years. We should be near that on a long-term basis. But that again 
depends on the fact that this has happened, not only because the project business 
was an aberration in the previous quarter, but also because retail has now started 
growing. 
 
Earlier, the project share was growing because retail was not growing, while projects 
were continuing to grow, so that is why the share was becoming disproportionate. 
Now that retail has picked up and the project business is also continuing to do well, 
turnover is increasing, and the proportion of retail and project should remain in that 
ratio of 60%, 40% going forward. 
Amit Srivastava: 
And are there still some orders at the old prices where we will be having a lower 
margin versus the retail segment, or is it now aligned to the new cost structure? 
Deepak Chaudhary: 
That would still be there. Bulk of it has been materialized in the last couple of quarters. 
There would be some parts of it in still Q3, but going to the later part of Q3 and Q4, 
we could be all, we can say, more or less with new project orders, with new prices. 
Amit Srivastava: 
Okay. Perfect. And sir, last question. In terms of the margin profile, if we look at the last 
two quarters, your margin is slightly subdued compared to what we were guiding for 
the full year. Given that the guidance, though marginally revised downward, still 
implies a very strong second-half margin of around 14.5%. Are we confident that with 
this price increase, whatever we have taken, and the current cost structure, we are 
able to manage that profitability? 
Deepak Chaudhary: 
In respect of the margins, we had ended Q1 with 10.13%. We had mentioned at that 
point of time that the low margin was kind of exceptional, and that had happened 
primarily because of a large number of one-time factors which had played our during 
that particular quarter. Going into Q2, you will find that most of those factors have 
reversed, and we have started seeing an upswing in the margin. 
 
I will just give you an idea about the various things which have played out in Q2 and 
what we expect going forward in Q3 and Q4. Just to answer your question in respect 
of whether we are confident about the total margins coming in the range of 13%-14% 
for this full year, we are pretty confident now that we should be able to surpass our 
18%-20% topline growth that we had projected earlier, and also achieve the margin 
of 13%-14%. 
 
Just to give you a sense of how the 12.2% has materialized in Q2, I will start with, let us 
say, 10.13%, which we had projected for, which had actually come in for Q1, and we 
had said that 4.5% was kind of a one-time effect. Those one-time effects have been 
reversed in the current quarter. So 10.13 %+ that 4.5% kind of became 3.83% because 
that turnover also increased substantially as compared to Q1. In Q2, the turnover was 
higher. That 4.5% effectively translated into something like 3.8%. So ideally, 10.1% was 
the base of Q1, 3.8% was the reversal of the one-time effects which had happened 
at that point of time. So we should have ended up with something like 13.9% of our 
revenue, 10.1 % + 3.8%. At that time, we had taken an impact of, projected of 1.5% in 
case of price rise. Actually, the price rise impact on the Company as a whole came 
out to be 2.5%. So, 1% additional we have gained over there, so which takes it to 

 
Transcript of CERA Sanitaryware Ltd. Q2 FY27 Earnings Call        
    Page 7 of 14 
 
 
something like 14.9%. Ideally, our margin should have been 14.9% because of this, as 
these adverse factors have taken effect in Q2 as opposed to Q1. Also, there was an 
operating leverage impact of 1.9%, like because of the fact that our turnover had 
increased, but the fixed costs are remaining constant. So, this 1.9% favorable margin 
impact was there, operating leverage impact. Ideally, our margins in Q2 should have 
been 16.8%.  
There were a few negative factors that brought it down to 12.2%, so I will just 
enumerate these negative factors. The primary factor was the increase in brass prices. 
Brass prices, even over Q1, it went up by roughly 11% - 12%. It was, on an average, the 
consumption was at INR 589 in Q1. It came out to be, sorry, INR 837 in Q1. INR 589 was 
in the previous quarter, INR 837 in the previous Q1 FY27. It came out to be INR 932 in 
the current Q2 FY27. So there is a 12% increase, which led to an overall 2.1% EBITDA 
decline. Publicity expenses increased by 0.5%. Our sourcing of sanitaryware and tiles, 
the prices had gone up, gas prices had gone up in Morbi, so that resulted in -0.3% 
impact on an overall basis in the Company. Also, discounts was a - 1.7%. This was more 
in the project wherein you find that the old projects were still continuing in Q2. So if 
your prices go up, but the selling price which you are effectively giving to the 
consumer remains the same, so the projects remain the same, so the discount 
typically looks higher. That is why the negative impact of discounts slightly has gone 
up in retail also, but which we have taken a lot of steps in the future, which will bring 
it down again. But that -1.7% impact was there on account of discount. All this added 
to something like -4.6% . 
 
I will just repeat them again, the negative factors. Brass, -2.1%, publicity, -0.5%, 
sanitaryware and tiles procurement, -0.3%, discount, -1.7%. So, -4.6% in total, which 
took our margin from that 16.8%, had these negative factor not occurred to 12.2%.  
Going forward, we are confident that in Q3, a few of them should be reversing 
because most of the projects have now started, as I mentioned, the old projects are 
now being completed. Most of the deliveries which will be happening in Q3 and Q4 
onwards, you will find that they will be for the new projects with the new pricing. So 
the discounts over there, the pricing effect would be coming into effect over there. 
So, we expect that the negative discount factor of -1.7% will disappear and also 
improved pricing will further come into play. So that should be impacting us to a large 
extent in the future. Lastly, we have also taken quite a few measures for controlling 
the retail discount also. The September price increase effect of faucets, which was 
not fully reflected in the current quarter of Q2. That will also be playing into Q3 and 
Q4. So going forward, we are pretty confident that the margin of 13%-14%, which we 
had projected for the whole year, should be very easily achievable. 
Amit Srivastava: 
Okay, that is very helpful. Thank you very much from my side. 
Moderator: 
The next question comes on the line of Shreyans Jain with 3A Capital Services.  
Shreyans Jain: 
Just one question from my end. Has the current geopolitical scenario helped 
companies like us in terms of a shift from the unorganized to the organized market, 
especially in the faucetware division where we have shown excellent growth? 
Deepak Chaudhary: 
The geopolitical situation has created a kind of a double-edged situation. It has 
added problems as well as presented an opportunity also.  
The problem is that, if you look at the gas prices, they have been going up continually 
over the past, you can say, one year or so. This has been exacerbated by the 
geopolitical situation, wherein prices have increased quite sharply over the last 
couple of quarters. The gas situation became extremely precarious at the end of the 

 
Transcript of CERA Sanitaryware Ltd. Q2 FY27 Earnings Call        
    Page 8 of 14 
 
 
previous year, Q4, and the beginning of Q1 of the current year. Now, at least the 
prices are higher, but availability is not an issue, but the increased prices are again 
putting a lot of pressure on the input side. The cost pressures have increased. 
 
Coming on to the supply side, we have been able to maintain our sourcing 
arrangements, and we are confident that we do not anticipate any challenges in 
meeting our demand in the future. Morbi players on an overall basis have been slightly 
impacted, but typically, if you look at the Morbi profile for sanitaryware, you find they 
are either OEM suppliers, so that has not been impacted too much because they 
have been able to pass on the increase in the input costs to the OEM players. Like we 
have, our procurement costs have gone up over the last, you can say, couple of 
quarters. So even in their own selling which they are doing under their own brand, 
because the entire market prices have gone up, they have been able to pass on the 
increased cost on the input side to the consumers. There has been some benefit 
because of the fact that the prices have gone up, and the consumers tend to move 
more towards the branded players as opposed to unbranded ones. That has helped 
to a certain extent. But primarily, if I say that it is only because of the pricing situation 
that has evolved in Morbi, and they are not able to supply to the fullest extent, maybe 
on their own to the outside consumer, that would be contributing to some part of the 
demand, but it is mostly, as I mentioned earlier also, what we have undertaken over 
the last couple of years for increasing our channel effectiveness and all the other 
improvements that we have done, which are now kind of yielding benefits and 
enabling us to gain market share in a situation where overall economic conditions are 
a little tough. 
Shreyans Jain: 
Great to hear that, sir. Thank you so much and wish you all the best. 
Deepak Chaudhary: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
The next question comes on the line of Bhupesh Kawdia with ICICI Direct.

“Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited

MANAGEMENT: MR. ASHISH DIKSHIT – MANAGING DIRECTOR –

MR. SURAJ BAHIRWANI – CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER,
