ADITYA BIRLA FASHION AND RETAIL LIMITED 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 2 of 13 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call 
of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited. The call will begin with a brief discussion by the 
company's management on the Q2 FY27 performance, followed by a question-and-answer 
session.  
We have with us today Mr. Ashish Dikshit, Managing Director; Mr. Suraj Bahirwani, CEO 
Pantaloons; and Mr. Jagdish Bajaj, CFO. I want to thank the management team on behalf of all 
participants for taking valuable time to be with us.  
I must remind you that today's discussion may include certain forward-looking statements and 
must be viewed therefore in conjunction with the risks that the company faces. Please restrict 
your questions to the quarter performance and to strategic questions only. Housekeeping 
questions can be dealt separately with the IR team.  
With this, I hand the conference over to Mr. Jagdish Bajaj. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Jagdish Bajaj: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I would like to welcome 
you all to the Q2 FY27 earnings call of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited. Looking back 
at the quarter, demand trends remained broadly in line with the previous quarters. However, the 
Y-o-Y performance was influenced by the shift in festive calendar, including Pujo into Q3 this 
year, along with a subdued wedding season.  
This led to a shift in the timing of consumer purchases, particularly across Pantaloons and our 
ethnic businesses, which together account for nearly 80% of our portfolio, thereby weighing on 
overall revenue growth and operating leverage during the quarter. It is, therefore, important to 
view Q2 performance in this context. Against this backdrop, we saw momentum across our 
businesses, with our emerging growth platforms gaining scale. 
Now moving to the financial performance of the quarter, ABFRL closed Q2 with revenue of 
INR2,030 crores, registering 2% Y-o-Y growth. While the festive shift moderated growth in our 
larger businesses, our emerging businesses delivered a broader contribution to overall growth. 
Our ethnic portfolio, excluding TCNS, grew by 12%. Luxury delivered 11% growth, and 
TMRW grew by 10%. OWND continues its strong growth trajectory, recording 58% year-on-
year growth, supported by the contribution from newer stores.  
This growing contribution from our emerging businesses is an encouraging development and 
reinforces the growth potential of our portfolio. Pantaloons segment, on a festive-adjusted basis, 
delivered 10% Y-o-Y growth in Q2.  
Moving to profitability, EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR67 crores. The decline was driven 
primarily by the shift in festive consumption to Q3, which impacted operating leverage during 
the quarter, the continued investment towards scaling our newer businesses. 
While these factors impacted the profitability, focusing on profitable growth remains a key 
priority as we build scale across our businesses. Our efforts remain directed towards improving 
operating efficiencies, enhancing store productivity, and building a more profitable business 
over time.  

 
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 13 
 
Turning to our balance sheet, we closed Q2 with gross cash of INR 1,143 crores at the 
consolidated level and INR 628 crores at the standalone level, providing sufficient liquidity to 
support our business requirement. Historically, H2 has been stronger for us in terms of both 
revenue and profitability, and we expect this trend, along with the release of working capital 
following the festive inventory buildup, to support cash generation in the second half.  
Coming to our retail network, we continue to expand our presence in a calibrated manner. During 
the quarter, we added 35 stores, taking total additions in the first half to over 80 stores. Our 
expansion strategy remains focused on building a more productive retail network across brands, 
formats, and markets. Our overall retail network now stands at 1,268 stores, spanning 
approximately 7.8 million square feet, compared to 1,190 stores and 7.5 million square feet a 
year ago.  
Now let me take you through the performance of our individual businesses. Starting with 
Pantaloons segment, the reported performance of the Pantaloons format needs to be viewed in 
the context of the festive season moving into the third quarter this year. Adjusting for this 
calendar shift and 16 store closures, the business delivered approximately 6% Y-o-Y growth 
during Q2.  
Our efforts to strengthen the Pantaloons proposition continue to progress, with greater freshness 
in merchandise, sharper assortment, and an enhanced customer experience. During the quarter, 
the brand conducted its festive marketing initiatives across important regional markets, helping 
strengthen brand visibility and customer engagements. 
Our performance during Onam and Pujo has been particularly encouraging, with both festive 
periods delivering some of the strongest results we have seen in recent years, reinforcing our 
confidence in the momentum heading into H2. On the retail front, we continue to refine our store 
portfolio, adding stores in select high-potential catchments while exiting locations that were no 
longer aligned with our network strategy.  
Turning to OWND, the business delivered a strong 58% Y-o-Y revenue growth. Supported by 
the scaling up of its retail network, the brand is making steady progress in strengthening its 
merchandise proposition and enhancing the overall store experience. At the end of the quarter, 
our retail network stood at 90 OWND stores and 387 Pantaloons stores.  
Moving to our ethnic portfolio, the business reported revenue of INR 517 crores during the 
quarter, growing 2% Y-o-Y. Excluding TCNS, the portfolio delivered a healthy 12% growth. 
As you are aware, our ethnic portfolio comprised two distinct segments, designer-led brands and 
premium ethnic. Our designer-led portfolio business continued to deliver healthy double-digit 
revenue growth during Q2, supported by encouraging momentum across our brands.  
We also continued to strengthen our retail presence through selective store additions while 
expanding the reach of our designer brands through international showcases and curated brand 
engagements. These initiatives are helping us build a wider consumer base and strengthen the 
positioning of our designer-led portfolio in the luxury and occasion wear space.  

 
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 13 
 
Coming to our premium ethnic brands, Tasva delivered double-digit revenue growth during the 
first half of the year, despite the shift in the festive calendar. The brand continues to strengthen 
its presence across key wedding markets, supported by a differentiated product offering that is 
resonating with all consumers. With a network of 92 stores, Tasva remains focused on gaining 
market share in men's occasion wear, supported by its growing brand visibility and improving 
consumer acceptance.  
Turning to TCNS and Jaypore, while TCNS continued to face near-term challenges, we remain 
focused on driving its turnaround through sharper product offerings aligned with evolving 
consumer preferences and stronger, more productive retail network. Over the past 12 months, 
we have rationalized our network by closing approximately 60 underperforming stores, which 
has impacted revenue growth.  
However, these changes are important to build a healthier business, with our focus now on 
restoring growth momentum, improving store productivity, and driving sustainable profitability. 
Jaypore also delivered a healthy quarter with a further reduction in losses, reflecting continued 
progress in strengthening the business. 
Moving to luxury retail, the portfolio delivered a strong 20% growth in the first half of the year, 
continued momentum across The Collective and Mono Brands and Galeries Lafayette revenues. 
We remain focused on extending our luxury proposition through the introduction of newer 
international brands and delivering differentiated customer experiences.  
Galeries Lafayette is steadily establishing itself as a distinctive luxury destination. Our focus is 
on deepening engagement with very important clients, building lasting customer relationships, 
and attracting luxury consumers from across India.  
On TMRW, the business delivered 10% Y-o-Y revenue growth, increasing to 19% if we include 
WROGN. 
Encouragingly, profitability improved year on year for the fourth consecutive quarter, reflecting 
continued progress in strengthening the operating performance of the business. Our focus 
remained on scaling the portfolio through sharper product offerings, category expansion, and a 
growing omnichannel presence, while maintaining a clear emphasis on improving profitability. 
Including WROGN, the network now spans over 150 EBOs.  
To conclude, Q2 performance was influenced by the shift in festive and wedding-related 
consumption, while we witnessed momentum across the businesses. As we move into the second 
half of the financial year, the festive season has begun on a positive note, with early trends 
witnessing encouraging momentum in our businesses.  
With festive and wedding-led demand expected to support business momentum, we remain 
confident of delivering a stronger H2, which has historically been a better period for us in terms 
of revenue, profitability, and cash generation. Our focus remaines firmly on driving profitable 
growth across the portfolio.  

 
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 13 
 
As our emerging businesses gain scale, we are placing greater emphasis on operating efficiency, 
store productivity, and disciplined investment to translate growth into sustainable profitability. 
With that, I would like to take this opportunity to wish everyone a very happy festive season. 
Thank you, and we are now open to take your questions. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Mr. Bajaj. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question 
comes from the line of Ashish Kanodia with Citi. Please go ahead. 
Ashish Kanodia: 
Yes. Thank you all. Sir, my first question is around the festive season demand. If you can just 
highlight what kind of LFL you have seen on a festive-to-festive basis, right? Not on a Y-o-Y 
basis, but if you just look at the Diwali minus maybe 30 days, what kind of a growth you are 
seeing? 
Ashish Dikshit: 
Ashish, you know our company is very diversified in terms of nature of businesses. I would say 
if you were to look at the most broad-based business, which is that of Pantaloons, as Jagdish 
spoke about it, both Onam and Pujo have seen one of the highest same-store growth. We are 
close to double digit in Pujo and even higher in Onam on a smaller basis. Subsequently, for rest 
of the country, to some extent, some parts of the country which affected by rain have pulled 
down a part of it, but it is between mid to high single digit across formats. 
Ashish Kanodia: 
And Ashish, maybe just when you say, whether it is a double digit or a high single digit, these 
are like-for-like in terms of festive to festive, right? 
Ashish Dikshit: 
Yes, I am speaking of only like-to-like numbers, same store. 
Ashish Kanodia: 
No, no, same store comparison and also for the festive to festive season period, right? 
Ashish Dikshit: 
Yes, yes. Festive - 30 days, festive - 45 days as we measure. 
Ashish Kanodia: 
Got it. And second question is more around balance sheet and cash flow. Now, if I look at the 
net debt position, as of April 1, 2027, it's almost, net debt is almost INR1,200 crores. You had 
on a net cash a year back of INR430 crores. And when I look at pre-Ind AS EBITDA, it's still 
in the negative territory. So, when you look at the next 18, 24 months in terms of the way you're 
planning to expand business, the capex plan, how should we look at the balance sheet position

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call 
of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited. The call will begin with a brief discussion by the 
company's management on the Q2 FY27 performance, followed by a question-and-answer 
session.  
We have with us today Mr. Ashish Dikshit, Managing Director; Mr. Suraj Bahirwani, CEO 
Pantaloons; and Mr. Jagdish Bajaj, CFO. I want to thank the management team on behalf of all 
participants for taking valuable time to be with us.  
I must remind you that today's discussion may include certain forward-looking statements and 
must be viewed therefore in conjunction with the risks that the company faces. Please restrict 
your questions to the quarter performance and to strategic questions only. Housekeeping 
questions can be dealt separately with the IR team.  
With this, I hand the conference over to Mr. Jagdish Bajaj. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Jagdish Bajaj: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I would like to welcome 
you all to the Q2 FY27 earnings call of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited. Looking back 
at the quarter, demand trends remained broadly in line with the previous quarters. However, the 
Y-o-Y performance was influenced by the shift in festive calendar, including Pujo into Q3 this 
year, along with a subdued wedding season.  
This led to a shift in the timing of consumer purchases, particularly across Pantaloons and our 
ethnic businesses, which together account for nearly 80% of our portfolio, thereby weighing on 
overall revenue growth and operating leverage during the quarter. It is, therefore, important to 
view Q2 performance in this context. Against this backdrop, we saw momentum across our 
businesses, with our emerging growth platforms gaining scale. 
Now moving to the financial performance of the quarter, ABFRL closed Q2 with revenue of 
INR2,030 crores, registering 2% Y-o-Y growth. While the festive shift moderated growth in our 
larger businesses, our emerging businesses delivered a broader contribution to overall growth. 
Our ethnic portfolio, excluding TCNS, grew by 12%. Luxury delivered 11% growth, and 
TMRW grew by 10%. OWND continues its strong growth trajectory, recording 58% year-on-
year growth, supported by the contribution from newer stores.  
This growing contribution from our emerging businesses is an encouraging development and 
reinforces the growth potential of our portfolio. Pantaloons segment, on a festive-adjusted basis, 
delivered 10% Y-o-Y growth in Q2.  
Moving to profitability, EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR67 crores. The decline was driven 
primarily by the shift in festive consumption to Q3, which impacted operating leverage during 
the quarter, the continued investment towards scaling our newer businesses. 
While these factors impacted the profitability, focusing on profitable growth remains a key 
priority as we build scale across our businesses. Our efforts remain directed towards improving 
operating efficiencies, enhancing store productivity, and building a more profitable business 
over time.  

 
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 13 
 
Turning to our balance sheet, we closed Q2 with gross cash of INR 1,143 crores at the 
consolidated level and INR 628 crores at the standalone level, providing sufficient liquidity to 
support our business requirement. Historically, H2 has been stronger for us in terms of both 
revenue and profitability, and we expect this trend, along with the release of working capital 
following the festive inventory buildup, to support cash generation in the second half.  
Coming to our retail network, we continue to expand our presence in a calibrated manner. During 
the quarter, we added 35 stores, taking total additions in the first half to over 80 stores. Our 
expansion strategy remains focused on building a more productive retail network across brands, 
formats, and markets. Our overall retail network now stands at 1,268 stores, spanning 
approximately 7.8 million square feet, compared to 1,190 stores and 7.5 million square feet a 
year ago.  
Now let me take you through the performance of our individual businesses. Starting with 
Pantaloons segment, the reported performance of the Pantaloons format needs to be viewed in 
the context of the festive season moving into the third quarter this year. Adjusting for this 
calendar shift and 16 store closures, the business delivered approximately 6% Y-o-Y growth 
during Q2.  
Our efforts to strengthen the Pantaloons proposition continue to progress, with greater freshness 
in merchandise, sharper assortment, and an enhanced customer experience. During the quarter, 
the brand conducted its festive marketing initiatives across important regional markets, helping 
strengthen brand visibility and customer engagements. 
Our performance during Onam and Pujo has been particularly encouraging, with both festive 
periods delivering some of the strongest results we have seen in recent years, reinforcing our 
confidence in the momentum heading into H2. On the retail front, we continue to refine our store 
portfolio, adding stores in select high-potential catchments while exiting locations that were no 
longer aligned with our network strategy.  
Turning to OWND, the business delivered a strong 58% Y-o-Y revenue growth. Supported by 
the scaling up of its retail network, the brand is making steady progress in strengthening its 
merchandise proposition and enhancing the overall store experience. At the end of the quarter, 
our retail network stood at 90 OWND stores and 387 Pantaloons stores.  
Moving to our ethnic portfolio, the business reported revenue of INR 517 crores during the 
quarter, growing 2% Y-o-Y. Excluding TCNS, the portfolio delivered a healthy 12% growth. 
As you are aware, our ethnic portfolio comprised two distinct segments, designer-led brands and 
premium ethnic. Our designer-led portfolio business continued to deliver healthy double-digit 
revenue growth during Q2, supported by encouraging momentum across our brands.  
We also continued to strengthen our retail presence through selective store additions while 
expanding the reach of our designer brands through international showcases and curated brand 
engagements. These initiatives are helping us build a wider consumer base and strengthen the 
positioning of our designer-led portfolio in the luxury and occasion wear space.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Jain Resource Recycling Limited Q2 and H1 
FY27 Earnings Conference Call hosted by DAM Capital Advisors Limited. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. 
Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star 
then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now 
hand the conference over to Mr. Abhishek Mehra from DAM Capital. Thank you, and over to 
you, sir. 
Abhishek Mehra: 
Good afternoon, everyone. Welcome to Jain Resource Recycling Limited Q2 and H1 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call. From the management side, we have with us Mr. Kamlesh Jain, 
Chairman and Managing Director; Mr. Mayank Pareek, Joint Managing Director; Mr. Hemant 
Jain, Executive Director and CFO; Mr. Sanchit Jain, Executive Director. Without taking any 
more time, I will hand it over to Mr. Kamlesh Jain for his opening remarks. Thank you, and over 
to you, sir. 
Kamlesh Jain: 
Thank you, Abhishek. A very good afternoon to everyone on the call. Thank you for taking the 
time to join us and for your continued interest in our company. I would like to start with a larger 
picture. For us, the first half of FY27 has been about two things: growing our existing business 
and bringing our newer investment into operations. Both have moved forward during the quarter, 
particularly on the copper side. 
 
Over the past several quarters, we have been working to build a stronger, more integrated copper 
business. The idea is to use our experience in recycling and gradually move further into value-
added products. We are now seeing the first commercial result of that work. Our new copper 
anode facility has started contributing to sales, and our Ahmedabad subsidiary, Jain CY, has 
been commenced operations. Let me share a few numbers to put this in context. 
 
Our consolidated revenue in the second quarter was approximately INR3,337 crores, an increase 
of 58% over the same quarter last year and 22% sequentially. In the first half, the revenue 
reached approximately INR6,061.4 crores, up 55% year-on-year. The copper business has 
played a major role in this growth. Copper and copper ingot volume increased by around 74% 
year-on-year quarter 2 FY27, while our copper business including the new initiative contributed 
8% of total revenue. 
 
At the same time, the established business continues to have an important role, led profitability 
improved compared to quarter 1 FY27 and aluminum volume also moved up during this quarter. 
So, the growth is being supported by our existing operations and as well as the new investments.  
On the profitability front, we delivered an improved performance during quarter 2 FY27 with 
EBITDA increasing by approximately 27% and profit after tax growing by around 30% on a 
sequential basis. EBITDA margin stood at 4.2% in quarter 2 FY27 compared to 4% in quarter 1 
FY27, resulting in an H1 FY27 margin of 4.1%. 
 
As we continue to scale up our copper volume, we expect some moderation in EBITDA margins 
due to the evolving product mix. However, the increase in volume is expected to drive healthy 

Jain Resource Recycling Limited 
November 04, 2026 
Page 3 of 17 
Mayank Pareek: 
growth in absolute EBITDA, which remains a more meaningful measures of value generated by 
our expanding operations. Importantly, we also generated positive cash flow from operations 
of approximately INR137 crores, (Please note INR137 crores was mentioned erroneously, it 
should be read as approximately INR 130 crores), supported by a significant improvement in 
working capital efficiency. 
Working capital days reducing to 49 days from 66 days earlier in FY26. This improvement 
reflects our continued emphasis on enhancing the cash generations, optimizing working capital 
and maintaining financial discipline while supporting the next phase of growth. 
On the sourcing side, we continue to strengthen our network in India and overseas. We are also 
closely watching the geopolitical situation and shipping disruptions, especially in the West Asia. 
Our diversified sourcing relationship and hedging practices helped us to manage the risk, but we 
remain cautious about development outside our control. 
Looking at the industry, we continue to believe there's a meaningful long-term opportunity in 
organized nonferrous metal recycling. Customers are placing greater importance on recycled 
materials and source efficiency and substantial manufacturing. We want to be ready for the 
demand with the right capacity, product quality and customer relationships. So, for the balance 
of FY27, our direction is very clear. 
We need to complete the project under executions, steadily ramp up the facilities that have 
started operations, improve the return we earn from the capacity already created. Mayank is 
closely involved in the execution of these projects. I will now request him to take you through 
the operational development and what we are working towards over the coming quarters. Over 
to you, Mayank. 
Thank you, Kamlesh ji. Good afternoon, everyone. As Kamlesh ji mentioned, we have reached 
an important stage in our expansion program. Some facilities are already operating and the next 
step is moving towards commissioning. Let me explain where each project stands and more 
importantly, what we are focusing on now. 
I will begin with Jain Green Technologies and our value-added copper operations. Both phases 
of copper anode plant, each with a capacity of 800 metric tons per month have now been 
commissioned, taking our total installed capacity to 1,600 metric tons per month. Phase II is 
currently in its trial run stage. With commissioning behind us, the priority is to make the plant 
run consistently and improve utilization. 
In a new facility, we have to stabilize the process, maintain product quality and build a reliable 
production rhythm. We are working on all the three. We have also started seeing sales from the 
value-added copper portfolio. In the first half of financial year '27, sales volumes were 
approximately 3,575 metric tons. This is a positive beginning, and our focus is to build on it in 
a disciplined manner rather than rushing to ramp-up. 
The next project is copper cathodes. We are developing total plant capacity of 1,500 metric tons 
per month in two phases. The first phase would be 750 metric tons and the second phase will be 
the equal quantity of 750 metric tons. Civil work for Phase I has been completed and 

Jain Resource Recycling Limited 
November 04, 2026 
Page 4 of 17 
commissioning is pending. In fact, the commissioning is at a very advanced stage and would be 
executed any day from now. For Phase II, we are targeting quarter 4 financial year '27. 
Alongside the commissioning work, we are paying close attention to process stability and 
quality. Our objective is to work towards producing LME-grade copper cathodes. Getting the 
specifications right is just as important as bringing the plant on stream. We are also progressing 
with our downstream projects. 
The copper wire rod facility has planned capacity of 600 metric tons per month. The Busbar & 
Profiles facility has planned capacity of 1,500 metric tons per month. Both are targeted for 
commission in quarter 3 financial year '27. Why are these projects important? 
Because together, they allow us to move beyond basic recycled metal and serve customers with 
a wider range of copper products. We expect the commercial benefits to build gradually as 
production stabilizes and utilization increases. They will not all come on the day a plant is 
commissioned. 
Moving beyond copper, we have two more projects under execution. The first is antimony. This 
facility will help us recover additional value from lead-antimony bullion that comes through our 
recycling operations. The planned output is approximately 100 metric tons per month, and we 
continue to target commissioning in quarter 3 financial year '27. 
The second is our dedicated plastic recycling facility with a planned capital expenditure of 
around INR15 crores. We are targeting commencement of operations in quarter 3 financial year 
'27. Apart from adding plastic recycling capacity, moving this activity to a dedicated location 
should also ease congestion at our existing copper and lead plants. 
Let me now turn to Jain CY Circular Solutions, our Ahmedabad subsidiary with C&Y Group 
Investments Incorporation. The unit has commenced commercial operations and recorded 
approximately INR25.4 crores of revenue during quarter 2. With input capacity to process 
approximately 71,000 metric tons of scrap annually, the plant can produce around 25,000 metric 
tons of copper products per annum at full capacity ramp-up. 
It gives us a stronger operating presence in Western India and the ability to process the broader 
mix of copper bearing scrap. It also fits well into the larger plan of our copper business. By 
strengthening our scrap processing and sourcing network, Jain CY can support the raw material 
requirements of our downstream operations. For now, the focus at Ahmedabad is on increasing 
throughput and stabilizing the plant. 
Finally, on Kuwait, the investment remains part of our long-term plans for raw material security 
and a presence in the Middle East recycling market. The machinery is ready, but shipments and 
project executions are affected by the geopolitical and logistical situations in West Asia. We are 
monitoring developments and we will proceed as conditions permit. Given these external 
uncertainties, we do not want to put forward a firm execution time line that may not be in our 
control.

around 4.2% in Q2 FY27 compared to 4% in Q1 of the same financial year, reflecting a

This improvement was supported by our continued focus on operational efficiencies despite the 
impact of an evolving business mix, raw material dynamics and the initial ramp-up phase of our 
new value-added plants. As these facilities progressively stabilize operations and achieve higher 
capacity utilization, we remain focused on enhancing operational efficiencies and driving 
sustainable profitability on a growing revenue base. 
 
Now coming to the profit. The profit after tax for Q2 FY27 stood at around INR90 crores 
compared to INR69 crores in Q1 FY27, reflecting a sequential growth of approximately 30%. 
The PAT margin has also improved to 2.7% compared to 2.5% in the previous quarter, reflecting 
an improvement in profitability on a quarter-on-quarter basis. For the first half FY27, revenue 
from operations was around INR6,061 crores, up about 65% on a year-on-year basis, while 
EBITDA was INR248 crores compared with INR250 crores in the H1 of the last year. 
 
Profit after tax has increased by approximately 3% to INR160 crores, the first half EBITDA 
margin was 4.1% against 6.8% a year ago. So now let me cover the performance of the individual 
business. In copper and copper ingots, sales volume has reached approximately 16,411 metric 
tons in Q2. 
 
That compares with 9,434 metric tons in Q2 of last year and 14,683 metric tons in the preceding 
quarter, giving us a year-on-year volume growth of around 73%. The copper segment EBITDA 
has also increased from INR46 crores in the Q1 to INR61 crores in Q2. EBITDA per ton also 
has improved from approximately INR31,825 to INR37,237. Value-added copper business has 
started contributing to the revenue, while its profitability will develop as production become 
more consistent and utilization increases. 
 
Now coming to lead and lead alloys ingots business, quarterly volumes has improved to around 
34,851 metric tons from around 32,150 metric tons in Q1. Volumes were below the year ago

picture. For us, the first half of FY27 has been about two things: growing our existing business 
and bringing our newer investment into operations. Both have moved forward during the quarter, 
particularly on the copper side. 
 
Over the past several quarters, we have been working to build a stronger, more integrated copper 
business. The idea is to use our experience in recycling and gradually move further into value-
added products. We are now seeing the first commercial result of that work. Our new copper 
anode facility has started contributing to sales, and our Ahmedabad subsidiary, Jain CY, has 
been commenced operations. Let me share a few numbers to put this in context.

of 58% over the same quarter last year and 22% sequentially. In the first half, the revenue 
reached approximately INR6,061.4 crores, up 55% year-on-year. The copper business has 
played a major role in this growth. Copper and copper ingot volume increased by around 74% 
year-on-year quarter 2 FY27, while our copper business including the new initiative contributed 
8% of total revenue. 
 
At the same time, the established business continues to have an important role, led profitability 
improved compared to quarter 1 FY27 and aluminum volume also moved up during this quarter. 
So, the growth is being supported by our existing operations and as well as the new investments.  
On the profitability front, we delivered an improved performance during quarter 2 FY27 with 
EBITDA increasing by approximately 27% and profit after tax growing by around 30% on a 
sequential basis. EBITDA margin stood at 4.2% in quarter 2 FY27 compared to 4% in quarter 1 
FY27, resulting in an H1 FY27 margin of 4.1%. 
 
As we continue to scale up our copper volume, we expect some moderation in EBITDA margins 
due to the evolving product mix. However, the increase in volume is expected to drive healthy

growth in absolute EBITDA, which remains a more meaningful measures of value generated by 
our expanding operations. Importantly, we also generated positive cash flow from operations

working capital efficiency.

closely watching the geopolitical situation and shipping disruptions, especially in the West Asia.

remain cautious about development outside our control.

materials and source efficiency and substantial manufacturing. We want to be ready for the 
demand with the right capacity, product quality and customer relationships. So, for the balance

commissioned, taking our total installed capacity to 1,600 metric tons per month. Phase II is

value-added copper portfolio. In the first half of financial year '27, sales volumes were 
approximately 3,575 metric tons. This is a positive beginning, and our focus is to build on it in 
a disciplined manner rather than rushing to ramp-up.

per month in two phases. The first phase would be 750 metric tons and the second phase will be 
the equal quantity of 750 metric tons. Civil work for Phase I has been completed and

commissioning is pending. In fact, the commissioning is at a very advanced stage and would be

quality. Our objective is to work towards producing LME-grade copper cathodes. Getting the

News Release 
 
Suven Life Sciences to Present Seven Scientific Posters Highlighting Its CNS 
Drug Discovery and Development Pipeline at Neuroscience 2026 (SfN), 
Washington DC, USA. 
Presentations showcase a diverse portfolio of clinical and preclinical drug candidates 
targeting neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders. 
Hyderabad, India, 12-Nov-2026 - Suven Life Sciences, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical 
company focused on developing innovative therapies for central nervous system (CNS) 
disorders, announced that it will present seven scientific posters highlighting its drug discovery 
and development programs at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for 
Neuroscience (SfN), to be held in Washington, DC, USA, during 14–18, November 2026. 
Society for Neuroscience (SfN), is the world's largest organization of scientists and physicians 
devoted to understanding the brain and nervous system, famous for its massive annual global 
conference. 
The presentations span a diverse range of therapeutic areas, including Alzheimer's Disease, 
Agitation, Schizophrenia, Narcolepsy, Sleep Disorders, Major Depressive Disorder and 
Parkinson’s Disease. The posters highlight Suven's continued progress in advancing innovative 
drug candidates through clinical and preclinical development. 
Suven will present the following seven posters: 
1. SUVN-M8036: A Multimodal Receptor Antagonist That Exhibits Antipsychotic and Anti-
Aggressive-Like Effects in Animal Models. N7; November 14, 2026, 1:00 PM-5:00 PM. 
2. SUVN-I6107 (Tenaclidine): Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of a Pure M1 
Positive Allosteric Modulator: Results from a First-in-Human Study in Healthy Subjects. 
JJ10; November 14, 2026, 1:00 PM-5:00 PM. 
3. SUVN-L1101142: A Novel Muscarinic M4 Positive Allosteric Modulator for the 
Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease and Schizophrenia. JJ11; November 14, 2026, 1:00 PM-
5:00 PM. 
4. Samelisant: Efficacy and Safety of an H3 Receptor Inverse Agonist for the Treatment of 
Narcolepsy With or Without Cataplexy: A Phase 3 Study. EE18; November 16, 2026, 1:00 
PM-5:00 PM. 
5. SUVN-N9503012: Efficacy of a Selective 5-HT1A Receptor Partial Agonist Intended for 
the Treatment of L-Dopa-Induced Dyskinesia. W18; November 17, 2026, 8:00 AM - 12:00 
PM. 
6. Ropanicant (SUVN-911): A Phase 2b Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled 
Study Evaluating Efficacy and Safety in Patients with Major Depressive Disorder. II27; 
November 17, 2026, 8:00 AM-12:00 PM. 
7. Masupirdine (SUVN-502): Baseline Characteristics from a Phase-3 Study in Alzheimer's 
Dementia with Agitation. V22; November 17, 2026, 1:00 PM-5:00 PM. 

 
Suven Life Sciences Limited 
Registered Office: 8-2-334 I SDE Serene Chambers I 6th Floor Road No.5 I Avenue 7  
Banjara Hills I Hyderabad – 500 034 I Telangana I India I CIN: L24110TG1989PLC009713 
Tel: 91 40 2354 1142/ 1152 Email: info@suven.com website: www.suven.com 
 
"Our participation at Neuroscience 2026 reflects the breadth and continued progress of 
Suven's CNS research and development pipeline. We have a diverse portfolio of drug 
candidates from several important therapeutic areas, including agitation, sleep disorders, 
depression, schizophrenia, Parkinson's disease and cognitive impairment. Our programs have 
advanced to the different stages of development, with candidates in Phase-3 and Phase-2 
clinical development, alongside promising preclinical programs progressing towards clinical 
evaluation. We remain committed to advancing innovative therapies that have the potential to 
address significant unmet medical needs, improve outcomes for patients and create long-term 
value for the company" said Mr. Venkat Jasti, Chairman and Managing Director, Suven Life 
Sciences. 
"The volume of scientific presentations at Neuroscience 2026 reflects our continued efforts in 
discovering and developing novel therapeutic approaches across multiple CNS targets. Our 
research encompasses different pharmacological mechanisms, including muscarinic M1 and 
M4 modulation, histamine H3 receptor inverse agonism, serotonin receptor modulation and 
nicotinic receptor antagonism. The presentations include findings from clinical studies of our 
advanced drug candidates as well as preclinical research supporting the development of our 
next-generation pipeline. We believe this integrated research and development approach will 
continue to strengthen our portfolio and support the advancement of differentiated CNS 
therapeutics" said Ramakrishna Nirogi, President and Chief Scientific Officer, Suven Life 
Sciences. 
SfN attendees are invited to visit Suven's Exhibit Booth #423, where senior representatives 
from the company's scientific and business development teams of Suven Life Sciences, India 
& Suven Neurosciences, USA will be available throughout the conference to provide insights 
into Suven's clinical-stage neuroscience pipeline, ongoing development programs, future 
development strategy, and opportunities for collaboration and strategic partnerships. 
About Suven Life Sciences: Suven Life Sciences Limited (Suven) is focused on the discovery 
and clinical development of innovative medicines that address unmet medical needs in CNS 
disorders. We have portfolio of advanced stage clinical candidates and research programs that 
are designed for CNS disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Sleep disorders, Major 
depressive disorders (MDD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), Schizophrenia, Pain disorders, and 
Gastrointestinal disorders. Suven has 5 clinical stage assets across focus therapeutic areas: 
Masupirdine (SUVN-502) for the treatment of agitation in patients with dementia of the 
Alzheimer's type (Global Phase-3 study ongoing, enrollment completed); Samelisant (SUVN-
G3031) for excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) in narcolepsy (Phase-2 study for EDS 
completed; pivotal Phase-3 AWAKE study for EDS is initiated and Phase-2 study for 
Cataplexy is in planning); Ropanicant (SUVN-911) for MDD (Open-label Phase-2a study 
completed; Double blind randomized Placebo controlled Phase-2b study completed and Phase-
3 study is in planning); Usmarapride (SUVN-D4010) for cognitive disorders (Phase-2 study in 
planning), Tenaclidine (SUVN-I6107) for cognitive disorders (Phase-1 study is completed; 
Long term general toxicity and developmental toxicity studies in nonclinical models are in 
progress). In addition to these clinical assets, 7 projects in research pipeline across multiple 
indications. Suven owns all intellectual property rights for its assets in all major world markets.

company focused on developing innovative therapies for central nervous system (CNS) 
disorders, announced that it will present seven scientific posters highlighting its drug discovery 
and development programs at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for 
Neuroscience (SfN), to be held in Washington, DC, USA, during 14–18, November 2026. 
Society for Neuroscience (SfN), is the world's largest organization of scientists and physicians 
devoted to understanding the brain and nervous system, famous for its massive annual global 
conference. 
The presentations span a diverse range of therapeutic areas, including Alzheimer's Disease, 
Agitation, Schizophrenia, Narcolepsy, Sleep Disorders, Major Depressive Disorder and 
Parkinson’s Disease. The posters highlight Suven's continued progress in advancing innovative 
drug candidates through clinical and preclinical development. 
Suven will present the following seven posters: 
1. SUVN-M8036: A Multimodal Receptor Antagonist That Exhibits Antipsychotic and Anti-
Aggressive-Like Effects in Animal Models. N7; November 14, 2026, 1:00 PM-5:00 PM. 
2. SUVN-I6107 (Tenaclidine): Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of a Pure M1 
Positive Allosteric Modulator: Results from a First-in-Human Study in Healthy Subjects. 
JJ10; November 14, 2026, 1:00 PM-5:00 PM. 
3. SUVN-L1101142: A Novel Muscarinic M4 Positive Allosteric Modulator for the 
Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease and Schizophrenia. JJ11; November 14, 2026, 1:00 PM-
5:00 PM. 
4. Samelisant: Efficacy and Safety of an H3 Receptor Inverse Agonist for the Treatment of 
Narcolepsy With or Without Cataplexy: A Phase 3 Study. EE18; November 16, 2026, 1:00 
PM-5:00 PM. 
5. SUVN-N9503012: Efficacy of a Selective 5-HT1A Receptor Partial Agonist Intended for 
the Treatment of L-Dopa-Induced Dyskinesia. W18; November 17, 2026, 8:00 AM - 12:00 
PM. 
6. Ropanicant (SUVN-911): A Phase 2b Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled 
Study Evaluating Efficacy and Safety in Patients with Major Depressive Disorder. II27; 
November 17, 2026, 8:00 AM-12:00 PM. 
7. Masupirdine (SUVN-502): Baseline Characteristics from a Phase-3 Study in Alzheimer's 
Dementia with Agitation. V22; November 17, 2026, 1:00 PM-5:00 PM.

Suven's CNS research and development pipeline. We have a diverse portfolio of drug 
candidates from several important therapeutic areas, including agitation, sleep disorders, 
depression, schizophrenia, Parkinson's disease and cognitive impairment. Our programs have 
advanced to the different stages of development, with candidates in Phase-3 and Phase-2

address significant unmet medical needs, improve outcomes for patients and create long-term 
value for the company" said Mr. Venkat Jasti, Chairman and Managing Director, Suven Life 
Sciences. 
"The volume of scientific presentations at Neuroscience 2026 reflects our continued efforts in 
discovering and developing novel therapeutic approaches across multiple CNS targets. Our 
research encompasses different pharmacological mechanisms, including muscarinic M1 and 
M4 modulation, histamine H3 receptor inverse agonism, serotonin receptor modulation and 
nicotinic receptor antagonism. The presentations include findings from clinical studies of our 
advanced drug candidates as well as preclinical research supporting the development of our 
next-generation pipeline. We believe this integrated research and development approach will 
continue to strengthen our portfolio and support the advancement of differentiated CNS 
therapeutics" said Ramakrishna Nirogi, President and Chief Scientific Officer, Suven Life 
Sciences. 
SfN attendees are invited to visit Suven's Exhibit Booth #423, where senior representatives 
from the company's scientific and business development teams of Suven Life Sciences, India 
& Suven Neurosciences, USA will be available throughout the conference to provide insights 
into Suven's clinical-stage neuroscience pipeline, ongoing development programs, future 
development strategy, and opportunities for collaboration and strategic partnerships.

and clinical development of innovative medicines that address unmet medical needs in CNS 
disorders. We have portfolio of advanced stage clinical candidates and research programs that 
are designed for CNS disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Sleep disorders, Major 
depressive disorders (MDD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), Schizophrenia, Pain disorders, and 
Gastrointestinal disorders. Suven has 5 clinical stage assets across focus therapeutic areas:

Campus Activewear Limited 
Q2 and H1 FY’27 Earnings Conference Call 
November 05, 2026 
 
 
Moderator: 
Welcome to Campus Activewear Limited's Q2 and H1 FY’27 Earnings Conference Call. 
Before we proceed on this call, Campus Activewear would like to point out that the discussion 
may contain forward-looking statements that may involve known or unknown risk, 
uncertainties, and other factors. It must be viewed in conjunction with our business that could 
cause future results, performance or achievement to differ significantly from what is expressed 
or implied by such forward-looking statements.  
As a reminder, all participants' lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the management’s commentary. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing "*" then "0" on 
your phone. 
To discuss the results, I am pleased to welcome Mr. Nikhil Aggarwal - Chief Executive Officer, 
Mr. Uplaksh Tewary - Chief operating officer, and Mr. Rakesh Thakur - Chief Financial officer of 
Campus Activewear Limited. 
Thank you and over to you sir for your opening remarks.  
Nikhil Aggarwal: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone and thank you for joining us for Campus Activewear 
Quarter 2 FY’27 earnings call. I am pleased to share that Campus has delivered another strong 
quarter with a revenue growing 16.9% Y-o-Y to Rs. 452 crores driven by volume growth of 
10.2% to 6.3 million pairs alongside a 6% improvement in ASP. This performance is particularly 
encouraging in a relatively subdued consumption environment. More importantly, our growth 
is increasingly being driven by stronger fundamentals, a broader consumer base, a richer 
product portfolio, and deeper market penetration. Our continued investments in product 
innovation, design, and distribution are translating into tangible results.  
First, we are successfully expanding our consumer base. Our Women and Kids categories grew 
by 27% and 34% respectively during first half FY’27, significantly outperforming the overall 
business. These categories represent substantial opportunities to expand our addressable 
market, and we believe we are still in the early stages of unlocking their potential. Second, 
premiumization is emerging as a powerful structural growth driver. Our products priced at Rs. 
2,000 and above have delivered volume growth exceeding 50% Y-o-Y with a contribution to the 
overall volume increasing from approximately 9% to 13%. This reflects growing consumer 

 
 
Page 2 of 12 
preference for differentiated design, comfort and quality. Third, we are strengthening our 
omnichannel presence. Alongside our traditional distribution network, we are witnessing 
encouraging traction across emerging digital platforms including quick commerce and our own 
brand website. Their combined contribution to D2C online revenue has doubled Y-o-Y during 
the quarter.  
Our strategy is clear. Make Campus available wherever our consumers choose to shop while 
maintaining a sharp focus on channel productivity and profitability. 
Coming to profitability, our material margins remained under pressure due to significant 
inflation and key input costs. While we have taken calibrated pricing actions, there is an 
inherent lag between higher input costs flowing through our inventory and the corresponding 
pricing benefits being fully realized. It is important to distinguish between recovering absolute 
input costs and protecting a percentage margin. We believe maintaining the right balance 
between growth, consumer value, and profitability is more important than pursuing aggressive 
price increases for short-term margin protection. Despite these pressures, we delivered EBITDA 
growth of 12.5% and PAT growth of over 21% Y-o-Y reflecting the resilience of our business. 
Looking ahead, we expect a meaningful recovery in profitability during second half of the year 
supported by the progressive benefits of pricing actions, improving product mix, operating 
leverage and continued cost discipline. We remain confident on delivering a full year FY’27 
EBITDA margin of 17%.  
Stepping back, I believe campus is entering an important phase in this growth journey. FY’27 is 
about sustaining growth and demonstrating operating resilience despite significant input cost 
inflation. FY’28 will be about converting this stronger growth platform into accelerated 
earnings and improving profitability. We remain committed to building a larger, more 
diversified and increasingly profitable Campus while creating sustainable long-term value for 
our stakeholders. 
With that, I would like to thank everyone for joining us and I hand over the call to our CFO Mr. 
Rakesh Thakur.  He will take you through financial performance in greater detail. 
Rakesh Thakur: 
Thank you, Nikhil. Good afternoon, everyone and thank you for joining us for the Q2 FY’27 
Earnings Call. 
I am extremely pleased to report that we delivered double digit volume growth in back-to- back 
quarter 1 and quarter 2 consistently, which is taking the H1 growth at 11% combined. For the 
quarter, the volumes grew by 10.2%. Revenue from operations grew by closer to 17%, which 
has taken our revenue to Rs. 452 crores, with steady growth across all the channels. Our trade 
distribution registered growth of 14% while our D2C online channel grew by 22%. D2C offline 
grew by 13%; wherein retail in fact did pretty well. 

 
 
Page 3 of 12 
We sold, like Nikhil mentioned, 6.3 million pairs during the quarter and ASP has grown by 6% 
year-on-year. Women's and Kids shares in the revenue mix has inched up from 21.7% last year 
to around 22.7% this quarter. Our gross margin, like Nikhil mentioned, is at 51.4% in the current 
quarter versus 53.9% in last quarter and we did witness inflationary pressure on material side. 
Our EBITDA grew by 12.5% year-on-year to Rs. 62 crores and our margin stood at 13.5% during 
the quarter, which is a marginal decline by 50 basis points versus the last year. We recorded a 
strong 21.3% growth in PAT, outpacing revenue growth. PAT stood at Rs. 24 crores which is 
5.3% during the quarter and improvement of 20 bps versus the same quarter last year. That's 
on P&L side. 
Our balance sheet remains strong, with ROCE improving to almost 22.3% and ROE at 18.5%, as 
of September 26. Net working capital days have inched up during the quarter because of the 
planned build-up of inventory for the season in Q3. 
I think with this, I will conclude my remarks and open the floor to the moderator for Q&A 
session. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. If 
you have a question, please press * and 1 on your telephone keypad and wait for your turn to 
ask the question. If you’d like to withdraw your question, you may do so by pressing * and 1 
again. Participants are requested to use handsets while asking a question. First question comes 
from Mahesh Tolani from Goquarter. Please go ahead.  
Mr. Mahesh, please go ahead with your question. There is no response. Next question comes 
from Devanshu Bansal from Emkay Global. Please go ahead. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Hi Nikhil and team. Thanks for the opportunity. Congratulations on good PAT growth in the 
quarter. Sir, you have shared some interesting insights this time around. So, I just wanted to 
check on this Kids and performance wear opportunity. As in what is the current scale of the 
industry per se and what kind of market share are we targeting in the segment? So, whatever 
initial thoughts you have if you could share some sort of insights on, that will be helpful. 
Nikhil Aggarwal: 
Can you please clarify again which segment are you talking about? 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Kids and Performance wear. 
Nikhil Aggarwal: 
Kids and Performance. Okay. So, see these are absolutely nascent segments. We have just 
started revamping these segments and very aggressively so, both Women and Kids. These are 
pretty much like blue ocean markets for us; there is completely big white space. We believe 
that there are very few organized players targeting these two segments. Campus definitely has 
a right to win, given our expertise in sports shoes and the sneaker market. Performance is 
where we are entering now also aggressively. Performance is the next growth driver. We have 

 
 
Page 4 of 12 
already launched badminton and now are in the process of launching cricket and running shoes 
very soon. So, this can be a great opportunity for Campus going ahead as a growth vertical. Our 
growth vectors have been performing very well, and they have been delivering majority of the 
growth, outperforming the core business. Uplaksh, would you like to add something here? 
Uplaksh Tewary: 
Like Nikhil mentioned, we have launched 3 new business opportunities this year. Apart from 
Performance, there is Apparel, which was launched primarily in retail, in Stage 1; ELAN was the 
second launch, and now we have entered Performance as the third launch. We launched this 
category about 60 days ago through an online platform and the initial results are extremely 
positive. You can see and order the products on Flipkart and Amazon as well. We believe this 
will be one of the drivers of disproportionate growth for us because of the white space, Nikhil 
mentioned. On Kids also, like you have seen over the last 2 to 2-1/2 years, a disproportionate 
growth coming from Women segment in our business; you will see a similar pattern coming 
through Kids as well. You have seen the initial nascent stage with disproportionate growth 
coming from the school shoe category for the last 2 quarters. The same will flow into other 
ancillary categories of sports shoes as well as smaller kids or kids of a lower age segment as 
well. The same story that we delivered with Women segment as a business, we will be 
delivering with Kids going ahead session as well as Performance is going to be a very big bet 
starting with badminton, moving on to running, football, and cricket as well. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Got it, sir. That is very encouraging. Secondly, I wanted to check some of your peers in the value 
segment have shared very aggressive outlook in terms of growth. So, wanted to check, is this 
a sector-wide uptick in growth momentum that you are noticing, and would you also like to 
provide some medium-term growth outlook for Campus as a whole? So, that would be helpful. 
Uplaksh Tewary: 
Our direction remains consistent. We believe to be delivering mid-teen growth, and we are 
delivering, and we continue to deliver on the similar pattern going ahead. We don't see any 
changes in that future looking forecast for this year. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Just a small follow-up here, peers like Asian etc. are indicating a 25% growth outlook, so wanted 
to check as in is this kind of a conservative kind of stance that you are adopting or whether we 
can see positive surprises on the growth front because the opportunity seems to be very large? 
Uplaksh Tewaryl: 
We will not leave any opportunity on the table. We are focusing on all segments that we need 
to address while being financially prudent as well. So, our growth has always had a backing of 
financial prudence behind it. We will take decisions looking at profitability of the category and 
we will not run any business for driving revenue without it adding to our bottom line. We are 
very clear on that principle and wherever we see opportunity, we will go aggressive. We are 
confident of delivering mid-teens growth. Of course, we have a bigger plan for the long term 
as well but for this financial year we want to stick to a mid-teens guidance. 
Devanshu Bansal: 
Got it, Sir. Thanks for taking my question and I’ll get back in the queue. 

 
 
Page 5 of 12 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Sir. The next question comes from Videesha Sheth from Ambit Capital. Please go 
ahead. 
Videesha Sheth: 
Hi. I hope I am audible. My first question pertains to channel-wise growth. When I see the 
growth in the Trade Distribution channel versus EBO channel, Trade Distribution accelerated 
to around 14–15%, but EBO has probably moderated to 11% due to the festive shift impact. Is 
it fair to say that the distribution channel would have seen sufficient inventory for the festive 
season, and how do you specifically think of growth for this channel going forward at primary 
and secondary levels? 
Uplaksh Tewary: 
The EBO number has a bit of an underlying reason to it. As we have given commentary earlier 
as well, we were in the process of a model transition for franchise, which is now 100% 
completed. Almost 50 stores got converted in Quarter 2 as well, which of course has an 
accounting where you take the inventory back and then rebill it. So, it has an impact of 
inventory coming into the system and going out again and hence the franchise numbers will 
start showing significantly higher growth. Just to give perspective, in the same quarter our 
COCO business grew at a like-to-like about 20% as well as the partners who transitioned in 
Quarter 4 of last year have shown a growth range of 20% to 40% for H1 of this year. So, we are 
very confident that this retail number, which shows a slightly lower number of 13%, of retail 
that has other channels as well there is LFS within that as well but we are very-very confident 
of showing 20%+ growth on the retail front because that is already what we are seeing just the 
model transition is taking away some of that positive repercussions coming there, but you will 
see that number improving in the upcoming quarters. On trade build, of course the seasonality 
has shifted a bit later. We have seen that happening same with online, same with offline but 
the growth is not driven by this aggressive inventory buildup; it is in line with our standard 
inventory practices. 
Videesha Sheth: 
So, you would expect 15% growth in the trade distribution channel to largely sustain going 
forward? 
Uplaksh Tewary: 
In that range. 
Videesha Sheth: 
Got it. Second, if we break down ASP growth of 6% into premiumization and price hikes that 
would have probably been undertaken, can you call the bifurcation out and even going forward 
to what extent do you expect to see this ASP growth to shape up? 
Nikhil Aggarwal: 
Our ASP, we have taken approximately 40 rupees of ASP jump in terms of absolute value. Rs. 
12 to 13 is attributable to the premium Rs. 2,000+ segment, and the balance is a product mix 
and MRP increases that we have taken. So, that's the broad split of that. This was enough to 
offset any increase in raw material inflation that we have witnessed. So, that we had accounted 
for and that is the kind of increase that we took in the MRPs. 

 
 
Page 6 of 12 
Videesha Sheth: 
Noted. The third question is on the D2C online channel. How different is the portfolio and price 
points being sold across your own website versus the likes of Amazon, Flipkart, and QC? 
Uplaksh Tewary: 
I will take the brand.com question first. Brand.com shares almost an 80% portfolio with what 
the rest of the marketplace operations will be selling, plus they will also have access to retail-
exclusive lines which will only sell between retail and brand.com and will not be offered to the 
rest of the marketplace ecosystem. Quick Commerce is a much more limited set, we were only 
selling for example, open footwear on Blinkit for the longest time, and only about 2.5 and 3 
months ago, we just introduced about 3 shoes. Zepto has a portfolio of about 8 to 9 products - 
4 open footwear and 4 closed footwear. So, much more limited portfolio available to these 
products and not the entire gamut that we have to offer between these channels. 
Videesha Sheth: 
So the growth you have seen in brand.com operations that would primarily be led by which 
price points or any particular part of the portfolio if you would like to call it out. 
Uplaksh Tewary: 
It will be on similar lines of the marketplace but the ASP behavior is significantly better than 
marketplace operations because we also work on selling more premium and showcasing 
products like ELAN, as well as our retail exclusive ranges. So, the ASP profile would at least be 
8% to 10% higher than our marketplace business today. The product that we sell of course 
since 80% of profile matches with what we sell on our partners commerce as well. The product 
profile will not be very different but the new age category that we do be it Apparel, ELAN, or 
Performance Product, or Premium Exclusives will have the highest share on brand.com as 
compared to marketplace operations.  
Videesha Sheth: 
Got it. Lastly, can you call out festive trends you are observing at the consumer level so far and 
how does it compare with the festive last year if any particular categories or channels are 
leading? What kind of trends are you observing? 
Uplaksh Tewary: 
Last year there were multiple inputs that went into market around this time. Of course, there 
was a very big GST change that happened in the market followed by a big festive push. There 
is no GST of course this year, so that one big blip that came into the system at that time but 
doesn't exist this year. But like-to-like if you compare our D2C ecosystem where we are able to 
compare, we are seeing double-digit growth there as well right now. 
Videesha Sheth: 
Got it. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, mam. Participants are kindly requested to ask 2 questions in the initial round and 
may join the queue for more questions. The next question comes from Umang Mehta from 
Kotak Securities. Please go ahead. 
Umang Mehta: 
Hi. Thanks for the opportunity. My first question is on new categories - ELAN, Performance 
footwear, and even sneakers if you can add to that. How much would have they contributed in 

 
 
Page 7 of 12 
first half in terms of topline or volumes? Any color would be very helpful to understand how 
that business is shaping up. Thanks.  
Uplaksh Tewary: 
Since we are a reasonably large organization, whenever a new category is added when I start 
comparing it to my existing base everything looks small, but within their own rights they are 
doing a reasonably good job. We’d have sold over 20,000 units of Apparel already in the last 5 
to 6 months primarily through our retail ecosystem and we would sell over 100,000 units of 
ELAN in this financial year. So, reasonably successful and we are not going very aggressive on 
inventory. We are doing very clean-cut launches, being very clean on channel exclusivity, on 
where we want to launch these products and we are seeing very good sell-through so there is 
no inventory issues of these categories. The partners are happy. There is a very strong brand 
communication. You would have seen the Jim Sarbh campaign that we did along with Amazon 
Prime during launch of that category. We are planning something similar for Kids. So, 
everything is linked to a much larger GTM and not just an ancillary category which I am trying 
to pump a new product into the market. So, we are very happy with the results. Badminton is 
a very nascent launch. The numbers might be small. So, in the last 30 days, we would have sold 
maybe 3000 units only on our online platform, but we are very happy because we launched 
only about 6 products there. So, we are seeing very good traction and that gives us the 
conviction of doubling down on these categories. So, there is already ELAN 2.0 coming next 
month in retail. If you visit our stores next month, you will see a much more unique profile of 
ELAN coming into our ecosystem; same with Performance. So, there is already a cricket line 
coming in January. All that good is happening because we believe all these small categories 
have the right to win and sell and will become small sub-BU in themselves in the next couple 
of years and that's what we are investing behind today. So, we are not very worried if it’s 5% 
of my revenue or 3% but eventually it will be a substantial part of my revenue in the next couple 
of years. That's what we are going behind and on and all three categories that I mentioned, 
Performance, ELAN and Apparel, all 3 are categories we are doubling down and expanding the 
range and not slowing down so that should give you confidence. And we are very happy and 
the entire ecosystem is driven towards making these categories really large.  
Umang Mehta: 
Understood. The second question is to Nikhil. Nikhil, we have heard some chatter around 
promoters wanting to sell, it has been impacting stock sentiment to some extent. Is possible 
to clarify how are you thinking about it? Are there any such plans in the immediate future? 
Thanks.  
Nikhil Aggarwal: 
Hi, Umang. There is no plan from the promoter family in the foreseeable future. We don't tend 
to sell anything right now. 
Umang Mehta:  
Got it. Thanks. I’ll get back in the queue. 

 
 
Page 8 of 12 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Sir. Dear participants, if you have any questions, please press * and 1 on your 
telephone keypad. The next question comes from Bhavesh Jain from DV Investment Advisors. 
Please go ahead. 
Bhavesh Jain:

Welcome to Campus Activewear Limited's Q2 and H1 FY’27 Earnings Conference Call. 
Before we proceed on this call, Campus Activewear would like to point out that the discussion 
may contain forward-looking statements that may involve known or unknown risk, 
uncertainties, and other factors. It must be viewed in conjunction with our business that could 
cause future results, performance or achievement to differ significantly from what is expressed 
or implied by such forward-looking statements.  
As a reminder, all participants' lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the management’s commentary. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing "*" then "0" on 
your phone. 
To discuss the results, I am pleased to welcome Mr. Nikhil Aggarwal - Chief Executive Officer, 
Mr. Uplaksh Tewary - Chief operating officer, and Mr. Rakesh Thakur - Chief Financial officer of 
Campus Activewear Limited. 
Thank you and over to you sir for your opening remarks.  
Nikhil Aggarwal: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone and thank you for joining us for Campus Activewear 
Quarter 2 FY’27 earnings call. I am pleased to share that Campus has delivered another strong 
quarter with a revenue growing 16.9% Y-o-Y to Rs. 452 crores driven by volume growth of 
10.2% to 6.3 million pairs alongside a 6% improvement in ASP. This performance is particularly 
encouraging in a relatively subdued consumption environment. More importantly, our growth 
is increasingly being driven by stronger fundamentals, a broader consumer base, a richer 
product portfolio, and deeper market penetration. Our continued investments in product 
innovation, design, and distribution are translating into tangible results.  
First, we are successfully expanding our consumer base. Our Women and Kids categories grew 
by 27% and 34% respectively during first half FY’27, significantly outperforming the overall 
business. These categories represent substantial opportunities to expand our addressable 
market, and we believe we are still in the early stages of unlocking their potential. Second, 
premiumization is emerging as a powerful structural growth driver. Our products priced at Rs. 
2,000 and above have delivered volume growth exceeding 50% Y-o-Y with a contribution to the 
overall volume increasing from approximately 9% to 13%. This reflects growing consumer 

 
 
Page 2 of 12 
preference for differentiated design, comfort and quality. Third, we are strengthening our 
omnichannel presence. Alongside our traditional distribution network, we are witnessing 
encouraging traction across emerging digital platforms including quick commerce and our own 
brand website. Their combined contribution to D2C online revenue has doubled Y-o-Y during 
the quarter.  
Our strategy is clear. Make Campus available wherever our consumers choose to shop while 
maintaining a sharp focus on channel productivity and profitability. 
Coming to profitability, our material margins remained under pressure due to significant 
inflation and key input costs. While we have taken calibrated pricing actions, there is an 
inherent lag between higher input costs flowing through our inventory and the corresponding 
pricing benefits being fully realized. It is important to distinguish between recovering absolute 
input costs and protecting a percentage margin. We believe maintaining the right balance 
between growth, consumer value, and profitability is more important than pursuing aggressive 
price increases for short-term margin protection. Despite these pressures, we delivered EBITDA 
growth of 12.5% and PAT growth of over 21% Y-o-Y reflecting the resilience of our business. 
Looking ahead, we expect a meaningful recovery in profitability during second half of the year 
supported by the progressive benefits of pricing actions, improving product mix, operating 
leverage and continued cost discipline. We remain confident on delivering a full year FY’27 
EBITDA margin of 17%.  
Stepping back, I believe campus is entering an important phase in this growth journey. FY’27 is 
about sustaining growth and demonstrating operating resilience despite significant input cost 
inflation. FY’28 will be about converting this stronger growth platform into accelerated 
earnings and improving profitability. We remain committed to building a larger, more 
diversified and increasingly profitable Campus while creating sustainable long-term value for 
our stakeholders. 
With that, I would like to thank everyone for joining us and I hand over the call to our CFO Mr. 
Rakesh Thakur.  He will take you through financial performance in greater detail.

has taken our revenue to Rs. 452 crores, with steady growth across all the channels. Our trade 
distribution registered growth of 14% while our D2C online channel grew by 22%. D2C offline 
grew by 13%; wherein retail in fact did pretty well. 

 
 
Page 3 of 12

strong 21.3% growth in PAT, outpacing revenue growth. PAT stood at Rs. 24 crores which is 
5.3% during the quarter and improvement of 20 bps versus the same quarter last year. That's 
on P&L side. 
Our balance sheet remains strong, with ROCE improving to almost 22.3% and ROE at 18.5%, as 
of September 26. Net working capital days have inched up during the quarter because of the

Thomas Cook owned Nature Trails expands network with its seventh 
resort at Dodamarg - nestled in Maharashtra's scenic countryside near 
Goa 
 
Mumbai, November 12, 2026: Thomas Cook (India) Limited’s experiential hospitality brand, Nature Trails, 
has expanded its resort network to seven properties by adding Nature Trails INA Resort in Dodamarg, 
Maharashtra. Marking its fourth property in the state, the addition further strengthens the brand’s presence 
across Maharashtra’s nature-rich destinations.  
 
Nestled in the Sahyadri countryside, Dodamarg offers a distinctive proposition for travellers looking beyond 
conventional Goa holidays. Located in close proximity to North Goa, the destination combines lush green 
landscapes, tranquil countryside surroundings and opportunities to experience the outdoors, making it an 
appealing choice for travellers seeking a more relaxed getaway. Spread across three acres, Nature Trails 
INA Resort brings this setting to life through nature-led stays, outdoor recreation and experiences that 
encourage guests to connect with their surroundings. 
 
Designed to cater to families, couples and groups, the resort offers three accommodation categories – Vana 
Forest View Rooms, Ira Cottages and Arka Cottages. The Vana Forest View Rooms, spread across 538 
sq. ft., feature king-size beds, attached bathrooms, sofa-cum-beds and private balconies overlooking the 
natural surroundings. The Ira Cottages, measuring 237 sq. ft., offer king-size beds, attached bathrooms 
and spacious verandas, while the 388 sq. ft. Arka Cottages feature forest-facing views, king-size beds, 
sofa-cum-beds, attached bathrooms and balconies. Each category offers a comfortable base for guests to 
enjoy the resort and its outdoor experiences. 
 
A key highlight of the resort is its range of outdoor and recreational activities. Guests can enjoy trekking, 
birdwatching, archery, treasure hunts and team games, offering opportunities for exploration, recreation 
and shared experiences. An outdoor swimming pool, set amidst lush greenery, adds to the leisure offering, 
making the property suitable for both relaxed family holidays and engaging group getaways. 
 
Dining at the resort is centered around Mitra – a multi-cuisine restaurant, which features a selection of 
cuisines with Maharashtrian flavours as a highlight. Guests can choose between the air-conditioned dining 
space and the open restaurant setting, offering a relaxed dining experience with a local touch. 
 
Located in Ker, Dodamarg, Nature Trails INA Resort also benefits from its accessibility via North Goa. Mopa 
Airport is approximately 40 km away, with an estimated travel time of one hour, while Thivim Railway Station 
is around 30 km from the property, accessible in approximately 50 minutes. Dodamarg Bus Stand is 
approximately 18 km away, offering connectivity for travellers arriving by road, rail and air. 
 
Mr. Mahesh Iyer – Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Thomas Cook (India) Limited said, 
“The expansion of Nature Trails is aligned with our broader strategy of building a differentiated hospitality 
portfolio that responds to the growing opportunity in experiential and nature-led travel. We see significant 
potential in destinations beyond established leisure hubs, particularly those that offer opportunities to 
develop distinctive holiday experiences while contributing to the growth of emerging tourism markets. Our 
focus is on building a portfolio with a strong destination proposition, supported by the right hospitality 
infrastructure and operating model. 
With the addition of our resort in Maharashtra’s Dodamarg, we are strengthening our presence in a 
strategically important leisure market while extending the Nature Trails brand into another destination with 
considerable potential. As we expand the portfolio, we will continue to evaluate opportunities that align with 
our long-term growth priorities, strengthen our geographic footprint and create sustainable value for the 
business.”

About Nature Trails: 
Nature Trails by Thomas Cook (India) Limited, is an experiential outdoor hospitality brand focused on 
immersive, nature-led getaways. Nature Trails is focused on offering quality, local, authentic activities that 
bring together nature-led experiences in a unique blend of comfort, fun, adventure, learning and 
sustainability. 
Nature Trails operates destinations across Maharashtra’s Durshet, Kundalika, Sajan and Dodamarg, Goa’s 
Ponda, Uttarakhand’s Rishikesh and Karnataka’s Hampi, located amidst large naturally forested 
landscapes and riversides. These properties are well-suited for weekend escapes, educational camps, 
corporate offsites, group travel and family retreats. 
Nature Trails resorts specialise in offering safe outdoor experiences and a wide range of curated activities 
such as trekking, kayaking, zip-lining, high and low rope courses and guided nature trails among others. 
Nature Trails also offers experiential learning and development programmes for youth and professionals. 
For more information, visit: www.naturetrails.in  
For Business Enquiries: 
Sarang Deshpande | +91 9225825111 | Sarang.Deshpande@thomascook.in  
 
About Thomas Cook (India) Limited:  
Set up in 1881, Thomas Cook (India) Limited (TCIL) is the leading omnichannel travel company in the 
country offering a broad spectrum of services including Foreign Exchange, Corporate Travel, MICE, Leisure 
Travel, Value Added Services, and Visa Services. It operates leading B2C and B2B brands including 
Thomas Cook, SOTC, TCI, SITA, Asian Trails, Allied TPro, Australian Tours Management, Desert 
Adventures, Travel Circle International Limited (TCI 勝景遊), Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited, Distant 
Frontiers, TC Tours, Digiphoto Entertainment Imaging (DEI), Go Vacation, Private Safaris East & South 
Africa. 
  
As one of the largest travel service provider networks headquartered in the Asia-Pacific region, The Thomas 
Cook India Group spans 28 countries across 5 continents. 
  
TCIL has been felicitated with MICE Powerhouse at MaxiiiMICE Awards 2025, Outbound Travel Operator 
of the Year (2024) and MICE Travel Operator of the Year (2024 & 2023) at The Economic Times Travel & 
Tourism Annual Awards, MICE Travel Agency (Outbound) at the Economic Times MICE & Wedding 
Tourism Awards 2024, 'Masters of Risk - Travel & Hospitality' at India Risk Management Awards 2024, 
MICE Tour Operator of the Year - Outbound at SATTE 2024, Best Tour Operator at India Travel Awards 
North 2023, winner of the Corporate Citizen Award (Travel Tourism & Hospitality) at the Corporate Citizen 
Conclave & Award 2023, The Outbound Tour Operator of the Year 2022 at the SATTE Awards, IAMAI India 
Digital Awards 2022, CNBC-TV18 & ICICI Lombard India Risk Management Award - Travel & Leisure 
Category 2022 & 2021, CIO100 Award for digital innovation 2022. 
 

   
 
 
CRISIL has upgraded the rating on debt programs and bank facilities of TCIL - ‘CRISIL AA/Stable’ on the 
long-term bank facilities of TCIL and ‘CRISIL A1+’ rating on the short-term bank facilities and short- term 
debt of the company. The highest rating for a travel & tourism company in India. 
 
For more information, please visit www.thomascook.in   
 
Fairbridge Capital (Mauritius) Limited, a subsidiary of Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited, is the promoter of 
TCIL with a shareholding of 64.88% of its paid-up capital. 
 
About Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited:  
Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited is a holding company which, through its subsidiaries, is primarily 
engaged in property and casualty insurance and reinsurance and the associated investment management. 
Founded in 1985 by the present Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. V. Prem Watsa, the company 
is headquartered in Toronto, Canada. Its common shares are listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange under 
the symbol FFH and in U.S. dollars under the symbol FFH.U.

Ancy Johnas | +91 7678042720 | ancy.johnas@thomascook.in 
Shourya Rawool | +91 9619745154 | shourya.rawool@thomascook.in
