Thomas Cook owned Nature Trails expands network with its seventh 
resort at Dodamarg - nestled in Maharashtra's scenic countryside near 
Goa 
 
Mumbai, November 12, 2026: Thomas Cook (India) Limited’s experiential hospitality brand, Nature Trails, 
has expanded its resort network to seven properties by adding Nature Trails INA Resort in Dodamarg, 
Maharashtra. Marking its fourth property in the state, the addition further strengthens the brand’s presence 
across Maharashtra’s nature-rich destinations.  
 
Nestled in the Sahyadri countryside, Dodamarg offers a distinctive proposition for travellers looking beyond 
conventional Goa holidays. Located in close proximity to North Goa, the destination combines lush green 
landscapes, tranquil countryside surroundings and opportunities to experience the outdoors, making it an 
appealing choice for travellers seeking a more relaxed getaway. Spread across three acres, Nature Trails 
INA Resort brings this setting to life through nature-led stays, outdoor recreation and experiences that 
encourage guests to connect with their surroundings. 
 
Designed to cater to families, couples and groups, the resort offers three accommodation categories – Vana 
Forest View Rooms, Ira Cottages and Arka Cottages. The Vana Forest View Rooms, spread across 538 
sq. ft., feature king-size beds, attached bathrooms, sofa-cum-beds and private balconies overlooking the 
natural surroundings. The Ira Cottages, measuring 237 sq. ft., offer king-size beds, attached bathrooms 
and spacious verandas, while the 388 sq. ft. Arka Cottages feature forest-facing views, king-size beds, 
sofa-cum-beds, attached bathrooms and balconies. Each category offers a comfortable base for guests to 
enjoy the resort and its outdoor experiences. 
 
A key highlight of the resort is its range of outdoor and recreational activities. Guests can enjoy trekking, 
birdwatching, archery, treasure hunts and team games, offering opportunities for exploration, recreation 
and shared experiences. An outdoor swimming pool, set amidst lush greenery, adds to the leisure offering, 
making the property suitable for both relaxed family holidays and engaging group getaways. 
 
Dining at the resort is centered around Mitra – a multi-cuisine restaurant, which features a selection of 
cuisines with Maharashtrian flavours as a highlight. Guests can choose between the air-conditioned dining 
space and the open restaurant setting, offering a relaxed dining experience with a local touch. 
 
Located in Ker, Dodamarg, Nature Trails INA Resort also benefits from its accessibility via North Goa. Mopa 
Airport is approximately 40 km away, with an estimated travel time of one hour, while Thivim Railway Station 
is around 30 km from the property, accessible in approximately 50 minutes. Dodamarg Bus Stand is 
approximately 18 km away, offering connectivity for travellers arriving by road, rail and air. 
 
Mr. Mahesh Iyer – Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Thomas Cook (India) Limited said, 
“The expansion of Nature Trails is aligned with our broader strategy of building a differentiated hospitality 
portfolio that responds to the growing opportunity in experiential and nature-led travel. We see significant 
potential in destinations beyond established leisure hubs, particularly those that offer opportunities to 
develop distinctive holiday experiences while contributing to the growth of emerging tourism markets. Our 
focus is on building a portfolio with a strong destination proposition, supported by the right hospitality 
infrastructure and operating model. 
With the addition of our resort in Maharashtra’s Dodamarg, we are strengthening our presence in a 
strategically important leisure market while extending the Nature Trails brand into another destination with 
considerable potential. As we expand the portfolio, we will continue to evaluate opportunities that align with 
our long-term growth priorities, strengthen our geographic footprint and create sustainable value for the 
business.”

by 50% year-on-year, while the second quarter also delivered healthy growth. 
More importantly, this progress continues to be supported by a strong order book, long-term 
customer relationship, and increasing engagement across our established as well as emerging 
industry segments.

manufacturing capacities strengthen our integrated engineering capabilities as demand grows 
across key industries, and that can support the business over the medium to long term. 
Looking ahead, we remain positive about the business outlook and the continuation of 
Omnitech's growth journey. Our order book, customer engagement, and opportunity pipeline 
provide a strong platform for our future growth.

development. We will continue to pursue opportunities across diversified industries while 
maintaining our focus on operational excellence and long-term value creation.

FY27 on a consolidated basis. Revenue grew by 40.5% year-on-year to INR175.56 crores.

management and prudent capital allocations while continuing to invest in capabilities required

3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review 
Engagements (SRE) 2410, "Review of Interim Financial Information performed by the 
Independent Auditor of the Entity" issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India 
(ICAI). This standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain moderate 
assurance as to whether the Statement is free from material misstatement. A review is limited 
primarily to inquiries of the company personnel and an analytical procedure applied to financial 
data and thus provides less assurance than an audit. We have not performed an audit and 
accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion. A review of interim financial information 
consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting 
matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in 
scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does 
not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that 
might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion.

5. We draw attention to the following matters forming part of the notes to the Statement: 
(i) Note No.7 - Gas pooling applicable to Fertilizer (Urea) sector: 
Gas Pool operator in ascertaining the contribution to pool account, considered cheaper market 
price gases specifically contracted by the Company for non-urea operations instead of EPMC / 
Spot gas meant for Urea Operations sourced as per OOF directives. Accordingly differential price 
or contribution to the pool by the company was worked out and issued debit note. 
The Company is of the view that EPMC gas / Spot gas is specifically meant for urea operations 
and thus needs to be subsumed in arriving at the final pool price and the same should be 
considered in the subsidy of urea, since the cost of gas is a pass through. 
As the non-recognition of such EPMC Gas / Spot gas sourced as per DoFfs directives for Urea 
Operations is not in accordance with the principles of gas pooling mechanism, the Company has 
continued to recognize such differential i.e. (EPMC / Spot gas price - Cheaper market gas price) 
amounting to '{ 79.84 crore for the period FY 2021-22 to FY 2022-23 which has been shown as 
receivable from OoF. 
Further, Company has disputed the demand of '{ 52.18 crore raised by GAIL towards pool price 
differential as against receivable of '{ 71.39 crore for FY 22-23 which has been arrived at on 
account of non-recognition of EPMC gas/Spot gas in Urea by FICC by substituting EPMC 
gas/Spot gas with cheaper RLNG gas sourced for non-urea operations. The total disputed 
amount for the year 2022-23 stands at '{ 123.57 crore. Total exposure is about to '{ 203.41 crore. 
Subsequently, OOF, vide OM dated 23rd October 2026, disposed off the Company's 
representation stating action taken by FICC regarding non-recognition of EPMC gas for urea 
production by RCF is in accordance with the policies of the Department of Fertilizers and the 
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas. The Company has submitted further representation to the 
Department of Finance (OoF) dated 11th November 2026, reiterating its earlier position and 
seeking reconsideration of the matter. The company is of the view that the matter will be 
resolved in its favour, and no provision is necessary. 
(il) Note No. 5- Revision in Energy Norms for ThaI Unit under Urea Pricing Policy: 
As per the notification issued by the Department of Fertilizers (OoF) vide Notification No. 
12012/1/2015-FPP dated 25th May 2015, the applicable energy norm for the Company's ThaI 
Unit was 6.200 GcaljMT. Accordingly, the Company had ascertained the subsidy income for FY 
2025-26 based on the aforesaid energy norm. 
Subsequently, the OoF, vide Notification No. 12012/3/2023-UPP (E.34185) dated 30th July 
2026, revised Urea Pricing Policy. As per which the energy norm applicable to the 
ThaI Unit has been revised to 5.984 GcaljMT with retrospective effect from 1st

In accordance with the operational guidelines issued by Department of Fertilizers (DoF), vide F.No.23011/3/2026-P&K dated 29th May 2026 for Kharif 2026 for import of DAP and TSP 
for shipments arriving from 1st April 2026 to 30th September 2026,Company has recognized subsidy income over and above the notified NBS rates on estimated basis on quantities 
sold out of such imports undertaken amounting to ~ 179.28 crore for the current period (~ 151.52 crore for the current quarter). 
The Department of Fertilizers (DoF) vide Notification no.12012/3/2023-UPP (E.34185) dated 30th July 2026, notified revised energy consumption norms under Urea Pricing Policy for 
Company's Thai Unit at 5.984 Gcal!MT as against the existing norm of 6.200 Gcal/MT w.e.f 1st April 2025 applicable upto 31st March,2028.Consequent to the revision,the Company has 
recognized financial impact of H32.52 crore for FY 2025-26,~ 39.02 crore for Ql FY 2026-27 and an additional Impact of ~ 60.17 crore during Q2 FY 2026-27.Accordingly, the total 
financial impact recognised for the period upto 30th September,2026 is ~ 231.71 crore.There is no change in energy consumption norm applicable to the Company's Trombay unit,which 
is continued at 6.50 GcaI!MT. 
Property Plant and Equipment: - Title deeds of Immovable properties 
In respect of immovable properties other than land, i.e. building and other structures Situated at its Trombay and Thai units, Company has self-constructed properties on the land 
owned by the Company as evidenced by property cards/title deeds of land. 
Company had came into existence in 1978 as a result of Government of India reorganising Fertilizer Corporation of India Ltd. and National Fertilizers Ltd. Consequent to the same, 
major portion of immovable assets at its Trombay unit became vested with the Company. In case of Thai unit, such properties on the Company's land were erected over the years 
following land acquisition effected around 1978. Thus records pertaining to self-constructed properties are not readily available Since they date back to more than 45 years. 
Based on legal opinion obtained from legal and regulatory experts on land matters, and also has other documentary evidence in that regard, Company is of the view that it has clear 
title to the same. Company has also initiated the process of obtaining appropriate evidence of the approvals/permissions taken for construction of the self-constructed properties from 
the respective regulatory authorities. 
The matter regarding the differential claimed by GAIL( India) Ltd., due to non-recognition of EPMC gas for 2021-22 onwards and Spot gas sourced during 2022-23 based on DoF 
directives in the gas pool account (replaced with cheaper market-priced gas contracted by the Company for non-urea operations by FICC), has been represented to DoF and is still under 
resolution. 
DoF, vide letter no. 12022/2/2024-UPP (E.38249) dated 25th June 2025,informed that the Committee constituted to examine the issue has found that FICC's stance of non-recognition 
of EPMC gas for Urea is justified. The Company has examined the Committee report and submitted its responses and has once again represented the matter to DoF for re-examination 
and has urged DoF not to initiate any action in this regard. The Company maintains that EPMC/Spot gas sourced as per DoF directives is meant exclusively for urea operations and 
should be included in calculating the final pool price for subsidy purposes, in accordance with gas pooling guidelines and extant Urea policies. 
Accordingly, the Company has continued to account for the differential (EPMC/Spot gas price minus cheaper market-priced gas price) as receivable from DoF. The cumulative amount 
stood at ~79.84 crore up to September 2026. 
Further, the Company has disputed GAIL( India) Ltd. demand of ~52.18 crore for FY 2022-23 towards pool price differential, as against its receivable of ~71.39 crore. This differential 
owing to FICC substituting EPMC/Spot gas with cheaper RLNG gas meant for non-urea use. The total disputed amount for FY 2022-23 stands at ~123.57 crore.Based on Company's 
representation, DoF/FICC has directed GAIL( India) Ltd. and stated the said matter is under examination by DoF. 
Subsequently,DOF, vide OM dated 23rd October 2026,disposed off the Company's representation.The Company has submitted its representation to DoF seeking reconsideration of the 
matter and reiterating its pOSition.

Formula used for calculation of Ratios: 
a. Debt: Equity RatiO = (Long Term Borrowings +Current maturities of Long Term Borrowings) / (Shareholders funds) 
b. Debt Service Coverage Ratio = (Profit before Finance costs, Depreciation, Exceptional Items and Tax) I (Finance Costs+Current maturities of Long Term Borrowings) 
c. Interest Service Coverage Ratio = (Profit before Finance costs, Depreciation, Exceptional Items and Tax) I (Finance Costs) 
d. Current Ratio = (Current assets) I (Current liabilities - Current maturities of long term borrowings) 
e. Long Term Debt to Working Capital = (Long term borrowings + Current maturities of long term borrowings) / (Working capital) 
[working capital refers to net current assets arrived after reducing current liabilities excluding current maturities of long term borrowings from current assets] 
f. Bad Debts to Accounts Recievable Ratio = (Bad debts written off) I (Average trade receivables) 
g. Current Liability RatiO = (Current liabilities - Current maturities of long term borrowings) I (Total liabilities) 
h. Total Debts to Total Assets = (Total borrowings) / (Total assets) 
i. Debtors Turnover = (Revenue from operations) I (Average trade receivables) 
j. Inventory Turnover = (Revenue from operations) I (Average Inventory of finished goods and stock in trade) 
k. Operating Margin % = (Profit before Finance costs, Depreciation, Exceptional Items and Tax - Other income) I (Revenue from operations) 
I. Net profit Margin % = (Profit after tax) I (Revenue from operations)

not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters that

5. We draw attention to the following matters forming part of the notes to the Statement: 
(i) Note No.7 - Gas pooling applicable to Fertilizer (Urea) sector: 
Gas Pool operator in ascertaining the contribution to pool account, considered cheaper market 
price gases specifically contracted by the Company for non-urea operations instead of EPMC / 
Spot gas meant for Urea Operations sourced as per OOF directives. Accordingly differential price 
or contribution to the pool by the company was worked out and issued debit note. 
The Company is of the view that EPMC gas / Spot gas is specifically meant for urea operations 
and thus needs to be subsumed in arriving at the final pool price and the same should be 
considered in the subsidy of urea, since the cost of gas is a pass through. 
As the non-recognition of such EPMC Gas / Spot gas sourced as per DoFfs directives for Urea 
Operations is not in accordance with the principles of gas pooling mechanism, the Company has 
continued to recognize such differential i.e. (EPMC / Spot gas price - Cheaper market gas price) 
amounting to '{ 79.84 crore for the period FY 2021-22 to FY 2022-23 which has been shown as 
receivable from OoF. 
Further, Company has disputed the demand of '{ 52.18 crore raised by GAIL towards pool price 
differential as against receivable of '{ 71.39 crore for FY 22-23 which has been arrived at on 
account of non-recognition of EPMC gas/Spot gas in Urea by FICC by substituting EPMC 
gas/Spot gas with cheaper RLNG gas sourced for non-urea operations. The total disputed 
amount for the year 2022-23 stands at '{ 123.57 crore. Total exposure is about to '{ 203.41 crore. 
Subsequently, OOF, vide OM dated 23rd October 2026, disposed off the Company's 
representation stating action taken by FICC regarding non-recognition of EPMC gas for urea 
production by RCF is in accordance with the policies of the Department of Fertilizers and the 
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas. The Company has submitted further representation to the 
Department of Finance (OoF) dated 11th November 2026, reiterating its earlier position and 
seeking reconsideration of the matter. The company is of the view that the matter will be 
resolved in its favour, and no provision is necessary. 
(il) Note No. 5- Revision in Energy Norms for ThaI Unit under Urea Pricing Policy: 
As per the notification issued by the Department of Fertilizers (OoF) vide Notification No. 
12012/1/2015-FPP dated 25th May 2015, the applicable energy norm for the Company's ThaI 
Unit was 6.200 GcaljMT. Accordingly, the Company had ascertained the subsidy income for FY 
2025-26 based on the aforesaid energy norm. 
Subsequently, the OoF, vide Notification No. 12012/3/2023-UPP (E.34185) dated 30th July 
2026, revised Urea Pricing Policy. As per which the energy norm applicable to the 
ThaI Unit has been revised to 5.984 GcaljMT with retrospective effect from 1st

Property Plant and Equipment: - Title deeds of Immovable properties 
In respect of immovable properties other than land, i.e. building and other structures Situated at its Trombay and Thai units, Company has self-constructed properties on the land 
owned by the Company as evidenced by property cards/title deeds of land. 
Company had came into existence in 1978 as a result of Government of India reorganising Fertilizer Corporation of India Ltd. and National Fertilizers Ltd. Consequent to the same, 
major portion of immovable assets at its Trombay unit became vested with the Company. In case of Thai unit, such properties on the Company's land were erected over the years 
following land acquisition effected around 1978. Thus records pertaining to self-constructed properties are not readily available Since they date back to more than 45 years. 
Based on legal opinion obtained from legal and regulatory experts on land matters, and also has other documentary evidence in that regard, Company is of the view that it has clear 
title to the same. Company has also initiated the process of obtaining appropriate evidence of the approvals/permissions taken for construction of the self-constructed properties from 
the respective regulatory authorities. 
The matter regarding the differential claimed by GAIL( India) Ltd., due to non-recognition of EPMC gas for 2021-22 onwards and Spot gas sourced during 2022-23 based on DoF 
directives in the gas pool account (replaced with cheaper market-priced gas contracted by the Company for non-urea operations by FICC), has been represented to DoF and is still under 
resolution. 
DoF, vide letter no. 12022/2/2024-UPP (E.38249) dated 25th June 2025,informed that the Committee constituted to examine the issue has found that FICC's stance of non-recognition 
of EPMC gas for Urea is justified. The Company has examined the Committee report and submitted its responses and has once again represented the matter to DoF for re-examination 
and has urged DoF not to initiate any action in this regard. The Company maintains that EPMC/Spot gas sourced as per DoF directives is meant exclusively for urea operations and 
should be included in calculating the final pool price for subsidy purposes, in accordance with gas pooling guidelines and extant Urea policies. 
Accordingly, the Company has continued to account for the differential (EPMC/Spot gas price minus cheaper market-priced gas price) as receivable from DoF. The cumulative amount 
stood at ~79.84 crore up to September 2026. 
Further, the Company has disputed GAIL( India) Ltd. demand of ~52.18 crore for FY 2022-23 towards pool price differential, as against its receivable of ~71.39 crore. This differential 
owing to FICC substituting EPMC/Spot gas with cheaper RLNG gas meant for non-urea use. The total disputed amount for FY 2022-23 stands at ~123.57 crore.Based on Company's 
representation, DoF/FICC has directed GAIL( India) Ltd. and stated the said matter is under examination by DoF. 
Subsequently,DOF, vide OM dated 23rd October 2026,disposed off the Company's representation.The Company has submitted its representation to DoF seeking reconsideration of the 
matter and reiterating its pOSition.
